Note:

The General Manager as Returning Officer called for nominations for the position of Mayor and advised that two (2) nominations were received by the General Manager by 6.25pm on Wednesday 9 October 2024.

No further nominations were received from the floor.

The Returning Officer confirmed that the two (2) nominations received for the position of Mayor, were in writing and in order.

These were:
  • Councillor Sarah Swan
  • Councillor Matthew Robertson

The Returning Officer then asked for the meeting to determine the method of voting to be used to elect the Mayor. The Council determined Open Voting.

At the request of a nominee, the Returning Officer allowed each nominator to speak in favour of their nomination for the position of Mayor.
  • Councillor Matthew Robertson spoke in favour of his nomination.
  • Councillor Sarah Swan declined to speak in favour of her nomination.

(Councillor Jarvis/Councillor Robertson)

81/2024 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  • Note that the General Manager as the Returning Officer will proceed with the election of the Mayor of Woollahra in accordance with the provisions of the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 for the period 9 October 2024 to September 2026.

  • Determines that the method of voting for the Election of the Mayor (if more than 1 nomination is received) as Open Voting, due to the Council meeting being held as a hybrid meeting i.e. with some Councillors attending remotely and some Councillors attending in person.

  • Note that the Election of the Mayor will be conducted in accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, with the result to be declared by the General Manager (as Returning Officer).

The Motion was put and Carried.

 


Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Blackwood, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Price, Councillor Regan, Councillor Robertson, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Swan, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Zeltzer
None

15/0


Note:

The Returning Officer then asked for a show of hands for each of the candidates nominated. The results were as follows:
  • Councillor Matthew Robertson 3 votes.
  • Councillor Sarah Swan 12 votes
     
Councillor Sarah Swan was declared the Mayor of Woollahra Municipal Council from 9 October 2024 to September 2026.

(Councillor Carmichael/Councillor Robertson)

82/2024 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Congratulate the Mayor, Councillor Swan on their appointment as the Mayor of Woollahra Municipal Council for the period 9 October 2024 to September 2026.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Carmichael:

Congratulations to Staff on the 'October 7 Remembrance Evening' at Christison Park

The Deputy Mayor, Councillor Carmichael advised that on 13 October 2024 he attended the 'October 7 Remembrance Evening' at Christison Park hosted by the New South Wales Jewish Board of Deputies and Zionist Council of New South Wales. The Deputy Mayor  congratulated Woollahra Council, in particular staff members Roger Faulkner (Team Leader Open Space & Recreation Planning), Tom O'Hanlon (Director Infrastructure & Sustainability) and Craig Swift-McNair (General Manager) on the successful execution of the event.

Councillor Woodgate:

Rose Bay Community Garden 10yr Anniversary / October Family Fest

Councillor Woodgate advised that on 13 October 2024,  he alongside Councillor Regan, Councillor Torsten and Councillor Parmegiani attended the Rose Bay Community Garden 10 year Anniversary. He congratulated the garden's committee on organising the event and bringing the community together.

Councillor Woodgate further advised that on 23 October 2024, that he alongside the Mayor Councillor Swan, Councillor Andruska and Councillor Mitchell attended the Ukrainian October Family Fest. Councillor Woodgate commended the organisers and staff on making the event a success.

The Mayor, Councillor Swan further acknowledged that Kellie Sloane MP was also in attendance at Heartbeats of Ukraine (October Family Fest).

Councillor Regan:

Rose Bay Community Garden 10 Year Anniversary

Councillor Regan advised that on 13 October 2024 she attended the Rose bay Community Garden 10 Year Anniversary. Councillor Regan congratulated the Rose Bay Community Gardens committee and members on the 10 Year Anniversary of the establishment of the gardens. Councillor Regan thanked the Committee members Belinda Johnstone, Pavel Gronich, Charlotte Boulogne, Emma Daniel, Donna Houston and Lindsay Severn for hosting a great event. Councillor Regan acknowledged that the gardens were started over 10 years ago, on a small parcel of unused land.  An active and engaged gardening community has now been created through a shared love of growing herbs, vegetables, flowers and fruits and as well as looking after chickens, honey bees and composting worms.

Councillor Andruska:

October Family Fest

Councillor Andruska advised that on 23 October 2024 he attended the Hearts of Ukraine (October Family Fest). Councillor Andruska remarked on the success of the event facilitated by Woollahra Council and acknowledged the attendance of the Mayor Councillor Swan, Councillor Mitchell and Kellie Sloane MP.

Councillor Robertson:

Valedictory Speech - Former Woollahra Councillor, Nicola Grieve

Councillor Robertson delivered a personal valedictory speech of former Woollahra Councillor, Nicola Grieve.

I rise to speak in valedictory of our former colleague on this council, the indefatigable former Councillor, Nicola Grieve. I do so hesitantly because I may get emotional so I will keep this brief. I can already see across the table that Councillor Zeltzer has quite a lengthy set of speech notes.

I have worked very closely with Nicola Grieve for over 15 years, and I can still remember the first conversation when we were setting up the parameters of our working relationship. I said “Oh, yeah, I’ll get up about 7”, well I have been taking phone calls from 7:00am ever since and until late in the evening. This is a person whose work ethic and their drive to deliver for this community is unparalleled. I know that we all work very hard, but I think we can all acknowledge irrespective of where we sit, that Nicola's commitment to the community and her performance as a Councillor was exceptional.

I want to put on the public record, that at times where I have faced difficulty or challenge, Nicola has always been the one who has continued to drive me. So I want to thank her for that.

Nicola has always been very passionate about this level of Government and the power that we have around this table to make decisions that affect the daily lives of our residents, and no issue has ever been too small or unworthy of Nicola's consideration and I know that the people of Cooper Ward were very lucky to have such a hardworking Councillor on the ground.

I had the opportunity to look back over the 2008 to 2012 term of Council, which was the first term that Nicola served and I was very interested to see and delighted in fact, that her first motion was actually on affordable housing, and that's been something that over the course of this last term from 2021 to 2024, Councillor Grieve worked very hard to bolster and enhance our approach to the delivery of affordable housing.

I also want to acknowledge Nicola's extensive experience on planning and for somebody without a professional background or training in that area, I've always been amazed at how effective Nicola can perform on a panel and she certainly served us very well as a Community Representative previously and will again now I'm pleased to say.

I will leave it there because it's very difficult to summarise the magnitude of the support, the depth of the friendship, and the joy that is working with Nicola Grieve. I have been the very great beneficiary of that over the last 15 years and I also want to say, particularly to the new Councillors, it is sad that you won't have the benefit of experiencing Nichola's drive and passion, however I am very certain that her contribution will continue to be made across Woollahra and for the benefit of all of our residents.

Thank you for the opportunity Madam Mayor.


Councillor Price:

Valedictory Speech - Former Woollahra Councillor, Nicola Grieve

Councillor Price delivered a personal valedictory speech of former Woollahra Councillor, Nicola Grieve.

Thanks Madam Mayor. I'm actually in my green tonight not in my usual pink. It is with sadness that we're not sitting around the table with Councillor Grieve and obviously I'm very pleased that Councillor Torsten is among us.

 


Nicola Grieve was very much larger than life. We all know Nicola and I do think that her sense of community and the fact that she was so engaged, so passionate and enthusiastic, I think will be fantastic that she is on the panel (WLPP).

Councillor Swan, you just made me recollect that you would sometimes be at these community events and maybe a little bit not as backward in coming forward, but certainly, if you stood beside Councillor Grieve, you would certainly get into conversations very quickly with people. She certainly did bring an extra enthusiasm and as I said, we're very grateful for her contribution. Even on Election Day, I remember I was running very late for the Bondi Junction pre-poll. I got there and Councillor Grieve had got all of the Residents First posters and A-frames out and had them all sitting there ready for me and I thought, “You know what? That is actually what it's all about.”

Thank you former Counsellor Grieve for her extraordinary contribution.

Councillor Zeltzer:

Valedictory Speech - Former Woollahra Councillor, Nicola Grieve

Councillor Zeltzer delivered a personal valedictory speech of former Woollahra Councillor, Nicola Grieve.

I rise to make my valedictory remarks for former Councillor Grieve for her significant contribution to this Council and community while in office and in those interim years when she was not.

Councillor Grieve began on this Council with me in 2008 and after 4 years was not returned. She worked continuously on numerous Council initiatives in a long interim period after which she was elected back to office again in 2021. 

Nicola Grieve was a diligent, committed and passionate representative, who held doing the right thing and proper process in the highest regard and was not afraid to call it out when she did not observe this. She was a Councillor who contributed very positively to the debate around this table, came extremely well prepared and spoke without fear or favour. She was not a seat warmer. She was engaged and she engaged us. Her contributions to this community are considerable. 

She had or should I say has an abiding commitment to the environment and community and she demonstrated this not simply by her words here at this Council but by her day to day actions. 

When I first met her she rode her bike to Council. She said short distances should only be on foot or by active transport. She was the first to take up a hybrid vehicle to reduce her carbon footprint well before the phase was coined. She later traded up to an electric vehicle and was able to give good feedback in terms of the roll out of our public recharging stations around the municipality. When not on Council she was an ardent Woollahra bush regeneration volunteer and rarely missed the annual tree planting days, getting down and getting dirty.  Also during this interim period, she came to watch me open the community garden in Rose Bay and has remained its strongest supporter ever since. This garden produced a real community at this Rose Bay location and she was always engaged with it and advocated for it.

In our first term she and I worked to get better, broader access to affordable solar panels and she assisted in brokering a deal with Randwick and Waverly Council, with which we have an environmental sustainability partnership, to increase the critical mass for the demand of solar panels so the prices could be lower due to economies of scale. This meant the solar panels became cheaper to acquire, which made a significant impact on the uptake. She fought strongly to preserve tree canopy in Woollahra and supported the new tree canopy controls fiercely, albeit like I she wanted greater controls to 40% of lot coverage, which was the State Liberal Government’s recommendation. Council finally settled for 35% of lot coverage. She was very astute on DCC site meetings. She developed considerable skills in urban planning and development assessment, which she was able to use when she was instated on the local planning panel. 

While she and I held similar values in terms of the environment, there were areas where we disagreed. One of the biggest contentions in that first term of office was the impact of large fig trees in Yarranabbe Park. Council was divided on whether a strip of trees should be thinned out by removing intermediate specimens to improve light conditions for some residents on New Beach Road. Cr Grieve believed the biggest driver for the removal of these trees was to open up views and she fought strongly against this. I supported the residents particularly as I had door knocked that area and understood the dark interiors in which some elderly residents lived. 

We respected each other’s opinion but agreed to disagree. As the years passed these trees were not removed and now I have the pleasure of doing my Tai Chi class with an older cohort of residents under the canopy of those very trees and I can say that considering the older original residents of New Beach Road have mostly moved on, I am so grateful that Nicola fought the fight for those trees on so many environmental levels. She took up the same fight to save a large stand of trees that were earmarked for removal on the Royal Golf Course at Rose Bay, advocating for habitat preservation and maintaining wildlife corridors. This fight, like the last, took years. 

Nicola was a Councillor who addressed her papers as soon as she got them on Thursday afternoon. By the weekend she was well across everything on the agenda and would sometimes ring me to ask for my opinion on various matters before the weekend was over. It was my habit to give the papers a cursory look on Friday and through the weekend and focus on them more closely on Monday, which I kept reserved for that purpose. Her weekend communication with me about what she viewed as contentious issues and her asking of my opinion, would direct me to a more intense focus on the Monday, so I felt better prepared for the meetings knowing what was coming. 

I need to acknowledge her holding the faith during the term we fought for Woollahra’s Independence. While she was not on Council during that term she continued to provided real support and enable the connection of myself with David Shoebridge, who was a lawyer himself and while many had written this Council off as a merged Council with Randwick and Waverley as Eastern Beaches Council, David Shoebridge thoughtfully encourage me to get the best legal advice in the land, which ultimately directed me to one of the best lawyers in the land. I offered to put up my Mayoral allowance for this advice, which was later not needed. We engaged Bret Walker and through him to briefing solicitors Speed and Stracey and particularly Robin Speed. With these legal minds on our side, we went through two lower courts to the highest court in the land and the rest is history. Nicola was a cog in that machine even though she was not on Council. She was a significant cog.

 


Councillor Grieve was an outstanding ward Councillor who was accessible and quick to respond and who worked closely with Mayor Swan. There was always great respect between them. On occasions if I asked Cr Swan about a matter related to Cooper Ward she would often say “I well get back to you after I have spoken with Cr Grieve to consider her views on this”. There was a collaboration and collegiately between them although they were of different political colours and quite often did not come to the same conclusions or decisions. They had certainly well considered each other’s point of view. 

Nicola was a strident supporter of the visual arts. My husband can recall Nicola giving him a great wrap for me for the success of my notice of motion to put public art on traffic signal boxes. He did not know I had anything to do with this initiative at Council. His comment to me was “so it’s your fault the Council is spending rate payer money decorating traffic signal boxes.”  By no means an art aficionado, he was clearly putting little value in any projects supporting the visual arts. Councillor Grieve did not agree with him. 

Councillor Grieve’s knowledge on wildlife was second to none on this Council. At times we Councillors would get emails from her telling us where she has sighted an Eastern Powerful Owl and for us to go look....Quick!  At one stage I had discovered an Aussie reptile, a skink, climbing the paved common staircase at my then home in a multi-unit Spanish Mission building in Bellevue Hill. This reptile was a handsome specimen who had lost its way and I did not ring Wires as I thought there would be a delay in their response. I rang Nicola who was there is a flash and got the animal back to the exterior without any fuss or injury either to her, to me or to the skink. 

This Council will miss the genuine commitment, environmental responsibility and community mindedness of former Cr Grieve. She is a force of nature and leaves this Council as my friend.

126/2024 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  • Notes its Affordable Housing Policy, adopted on 25 October 2021, and in particular: 
  • Council's commitment to:
  1. “encourage the provision of affordable, inclusive and diverse housing for very low, low and moderate income households, and meets special housing and access needs”; and
  2. “protecting and supporting the supply of affordable housing stock that can be rented or purchased by very low, low, and moderate income households”.
  1. recognition in that policy that “Council may obtain rental housing through various mechanisms, including……housing stock acquired or leased by Council.”
https://www.woollahra.nsw.gov.au/files/assets/public/v/1/plans-policies-publications/woollahra-affordable-housing-policy-2021.pdf

  1. Prepare a report identifying the opportunity for Council to acquire suitable boarding house sites in the municipality and/or its surrounds in order that Council may directly deliver some form of affordable housing for low-income residents and essential workers, such report to consider, amongst other things:
  • an estimate of the number of boarding houses and rooms currently existing in the municipality;

  • current potential boarding houses for sale in the municipality and surrounds;

  • the feasibility of any potential acquisition including potential sources of funding (including from affordable housing cash contributions from development held by, or to be received by Council) and income streams necessary to manage boarding house assets on an ongoing basis;

  • other options for Council to acquire boarding houses through direct purchase or in coordination with other community housing providers;

  • the way boarding house assets acquired by Council could be successfully managed by community housing providers or other similar organisations working with Council; and

  • the methodology that may be employed by Council in future to identify, fund, acquire and manage boarding house sites in the municipality and its surrounds to provide low-cost accommodation for vulnerable and essential workers in the community.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Swan, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Regan, Councillor Andruska, Councillor Robertson, Councillor Price, Councillor Blackwood, Councillor Witt, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Zeltzer, Councillor Mitchell
None

THAT:

  1. [OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD]
[AGENDA_ITEM_NAME][IGNORE_INDENT]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Witt asking:

Could the Staff please provide an update on progress made to date to introduce something similar to Waverley Council's Social Impact Assessment (SIA) requirement for substantial new developments.

Social Impact Assessment Guidelines

Discussion

Waverley Council planners have the discretion to request that applicants prepare a Social Impact Statement (SIS).

The purpose of the SIS is to assist Council Staff in their assessment of the social impacts of proposed new developments “by identifying what social impacts matter when it comes to proposed developments, where the impacts will be felt, and by whom and how.”
In some cases, the need for a Social Impact Assessment (SIA) is based on the expected impact, scope and scale of development, and the impact of similar developments in the past.

A SIS is required for all proponent-led Planning Proposals and Development Applications (DAs) that involve the following:

  • Loss of low-rental dwellings (see State Environmental Planning Policy Housing 2021 for definition)
  • Strata subdivision of 4 or more lots
  • $10,000,000 or greater construction cost
  • Gross Floor Area of 3,000sqm or greater
  • Reduction in dwelling numbers on site.
 A SIS may also be required for the following land uses:

  • Shop top housing
  • Residential flat buildings
  • Build-to-Rent housing
  • Boarding houses and hostes
  • Co-living housing
  • Entertainment facilities for more than 100 persons
  • Pubs, excluding a limited licence and a small bar.
  • Retail premises for more than 500sqm
  • Tourist and visitor accommodation
  • Backpackers’ accommodation
  • Hotel or motel accommodation
  • Serviced apartments
The SIA is expected to take into account the physical catchment for the assessment, the existing social environment, conditions and trends relevant to the impacts, as well the proposed development's resilience against the resultant social impacts of climate change.

Reasons for why the introduction of SIA requirement is appropriate for the Woollahra Local Government Area (LGA)

Like Waverley Council, Woollahra Council is under sustained development pressure, having exceeded its 2016 - 2021 5 year net new dwelling target by 70% and already delivering 43% of its 500 net new dwelling target for 2021 - 2026.*1

The Woollahra municipality is also losing its older style residential apartment buildings, which are typically home to lower cost rentals and/or more affordable apartments available to buy.*2

Scarcity of land and increasing urban density means that ensuring social impacts can be appropriately managed are essential for helping Woollahra Council to meet the goals of its Local Strategic Planning Statement (LSPS) 2020, which sets out the 20-year vision and planning priorities for managing future land use across the Woollahra LGA.

Designed to protect what the Woollahra community values as it moves forward – eg lifestyle, heritage, local character, open spaces, boutique villages, tree canopy, gardens, and natural environment - the LSPS recognises opportunities to enhance what Woollahra offers for the benefit of everyone by:

  • improving environmental health – clean air, land, and water
  • providing plentiful green open spaces
  • conserving heritage and local character
  • supporting local business
  • supporting people’s housing needs at every stage of life
  • Increasing access to affordable housing
  • supporting social cohesion and neighbourhood connections
  • increasing the safety and condition of walking paths for people of all ages and needs
  • prioritising active transport connections between people, jobs, and great places
  • optimising infrastructure and facilities to meet changing needs
The purpose of an SIS

An SIS is designed to go beyond the requirements of a Statement of Environmental Effects (SEE), which only requires the applicant to address the environmental and economic impacts of a proposal.

The SIA and the resulting SIS consider the potential social impacts of developments in the planning and decision making process more comprehensively and consistently.

Applicants are also required to assess possible adverse social impacts, and provide justification for why they are acceptable and how they can be mitigated or removed?

Guidelines for the preparation of an SIS

Waverley Council provides applicants with a set of detailed guidelines for carrying out the SIA and the resulting SIS. Examples of the types of social impacts an SIA is expected to address include:

  • cumulative impacts of the same types of developments in any one area. An SIA, for example, can identify where an existing area may effectively already be saturated with a certain type of development (eg boarding houses, restaurants and night clubs), and identify whether further instances of these types of developments will have a detrimental social impact on the neighbourhood.
  • Alternatively, an SIA may identify where certain types of development are diminishing and whether their loss is considered important to housing diversity and community satisfaction in terms of access to public and private amenities like affordable housing, sporting and recreation land, medical facilities, shopping facilities, mechanics etc.
Social impacts are also expected to be assessed by applicants against the goals and objectives of relevant strategic planning documents prepared by Council. In this regard, an SIS will provide Woollahra Council Staff with regular opportunities to benchmark development proposals against the well considered stated goals and objectives of these important statements.

*1 See Woollahra Council’s submission to the state government’s proposal to create more low and mid-rise housing (February 2024). Woollahra Council's 5 year new dwelling target was recently increased by the DPHI to 1,900 net additional dwellings for the period July 2024 to June 2029. This figure is way in excess of numbers projected in the Woollahra Local Housing Strategy 2021 (Woollahra LHS). It sets the following targets:

2016-2021 - 300 dwellings;
2021-2026 - 500 dwellings; and
2026-2036 - 400 dwellings
See Environmental Planning Committee, Monday 3 June 2024, Late Correspondence.

124/2024 Resolved:

128/2024 Resolved:

THAT Council request staff to investigate and provide a report to Council on whether:


  1. It is possible or reasonable to place load and length limits on construction and demolition heavy vehicles using residential streets through conditions of consent;

  2. There is an avenue to levy for the cost of road repairs based on the impact of frequent construction and demolition heavy vehicle usage on residential streets;

  3. The number of movements of heavy vehicles through residential streets can be limited and in what manner;

  4. Applicants can be required to provide a heavy vehicle movement plan as a condition of consent (outlining frequency, load and number of vehicle movements through residential streets) and the manner in which compliance with such plan will be implemented; and

  5. Consider how limiting the load, truck movements and the size of the vehicles can be enforced. 


The Motion was put and carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Note: Rebecca Lacey - Owner, Zoltan Kovacs - Architect for the Owner, and Alec Tzannes - Architect for the Owner addressed the Committee.

(Councillor Swan/Councillor Regan)

193/2024 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Note the advice provided by the Woollahra Local Planning Panel on 19 September 2024 regarding the planning proposal to amend the local heritage listing at 83 Fitzwilliam Road, Vaucluse to include the dwelling/former shop (including interiors), and associated landscape elements.

  2. Endorse the planning proposal as contained at Attachment 1 of the report to the Environmental Planning Committee of 25 November 2024 to alter the listing for I357 subject to amending the description of the item to be as follows: “ Vaucluse Point Ferry Wharf – remnants of wharf, dwelling/former shop (including internal staircase) and associated landscape elements” which is to be included in Schedule 5 of the Woollahra Environmental Plan 2014 and resolves to forward this to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure with a request for Gateway Determination to allow public exhibition.
     
  3. Request the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces (or delegate) authorise Council as the local plan-making authority in relation to the planning proposal, to make the local environment plan under section 3.36 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.


The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with section 375A of the Local Government Act a Division of votes is recorded on this planning matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Swan, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Regan, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt
Councillor Parmegiani

8.1 Petition

From: Alison Bevege
Tabled by: Councillor Regan 

The petition was in terms, "Calling on Woollahra Council to support Port Hedland Council’s actions to call on the Federal Government to address concerns regarding potential impacts of mRNA vaccines and increase public awareness of those concerns. This petition calls on Woollahra council to support Port Hedland Council’s action, and further to:

  1. Send a similar letter to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, including Dr Speicher’s report
  2. Send a letter to every registered health practitioner and medical clinic within Woollahra Council Local Government Area containing a similar letter and a copy of Dr Speicher’s report.

There were 10 signatures on the tabled petition.


224/2024 Resolved:

THAT the petition lie on the table for fourteen (14) days and referred to the relevant Council department for consideration.

Councillor Carmichael:

  • Appreciation for Staff Efforts Following Woollahra Graffiti Incident
The Deputy Mayor advised that he represented the Mayor on a number of recent occasions and focused his remarks on his support of the Mayoral Minute tabled at this meeting and extended his gratitude to Council staff for their efforts in addressing the mass graffiti incident that took place in Woollahra on 21 November 2024.

Councillor Woodgate:

  • Remembrance Day
Councillor Woodgate advised that on 10 November 2024, he along with the Mayor Councillor Swan and Deputy Mayor Councillor Carmichael attended the Remembrance Day Service and NAJEX (NSW Association of Jewish Service & Ex-Service Men & Women) wreath-laying at the Sydney Jewish Museum. Councillor Woodgate acknowledged the attendance of a number of Waverley Councillors and Kellie Sloane, Member for Vaucluse. Councillor Woodgate congratulated Roger Selby (President of NAJEX) and the Board and recognised Lesley Barold for hosting a great event.

Councillor Regan:

  • Local Government NSW Conference
  • Congratulations to Staff on the Rose Bay Bike Day

Councillor Regan advised that she, along with Councillors Witt, Jarvis and Parmegiani attended the NSW Local Government Conference held in Tamworth on 17 November to 19 November 2024.

Councillor Regan further advised that on 24 November 2024 she attended the Rose Bay Bike Day hosted by Woollahra Council. Councillor Regan congratulated Council's Sustainability Team on the event, notably Mitchell Kirsch (Sustainability Project Officer) and Michelle Rose (Environmental Education Officer). Councillor Regan extended her thanks to the Library Team, in particular Sarah Sproule (Events & Programs Team Leader), Morrin Delves (Senior Library Customer Service Officer) and Brigid Denmade (Library Assistant). Councillor Regan acknowledged that Rose Bay Bike Day helps to raise awareness of the Double Bay to Rose Bay bike path and support active transport users in our area. The event saw around 35 bikes receive free tune-ups from BikeWise bike mechanics. Revolve Recycling collected 11 bikes and 2 scooters for recycling or reuse. People also received riding tips, bike adjustments or took an e-bike for a test ride. Kids had fun with the Library Team decorating their bikes and with bike themed stories and activities.

Councillor Andruska:

  • Remembrance Day
  • Trumper Park Tennis Courts
Councillor Andruska advised that on 10 November 2024 he had the honour of laying a wreath for Remembrance Day at the Paddington Cenotaph.

Councillor Andruska further advised that on 18 November 2024 he met a number of people from the Trumper Park tennis community who passed on their gratitude for Council keeping the tennis centre solely for tennis-use.

Councillor Price:

  • Trans Awareness Week
Councillor Price advised that last week was 'Trans Awareness Week' which is a week to celebrate and amplify "trans voices". Councillor Price attended the Double Bay Library where she heard from prominent trans-community members Shontel Martin and River Nyland, along with members from the Inner City Legal Centre. Councillor Price thanked them all for their leadership and generosity in sharing their experiences, challenges and joys. Councillor Price advised that the day included a workshop conducted by Jackie Mae Turner from the Trans Justice Project, on combating anti-trans rhetoric. Councillor Price thanked Katie Green and her team from Inner City Legal for facilitating this initiative.

Councillor Torsten:

  • Citizenship Ceremony
  • Head On Photo Festival
Councillor Torsten advised that on 20 November 2024 he, along with the Mayor Councillor Swan and Councillor Mitchell attended the Citizenship Ceremony held at Woollahra Council Chambers. Councillor Torsten highlighted that the newest Australian Citizens came from a wide range of nations and will contribute to enriching Woollahra's multicultural diversity.

Councillor Torsten discussed the Head On Photo Festival currently being held at Bondi and at the Paddington Reservoir. Councillor Torsten expressed his intention to liaise with Woollahra's Arts & Culture Advisory Committee to explore how Woollahra Council might support the continuation of the festival in the future.

Councillor Witt:

  • Darling Point Society AGM
  • Local Government NSW Conference
Councillor Witt advised that on 21 November 2024, she along with Councillors Torsten, Silcocks and Ardouin attended the Darling Point Society's AGM. Councillor Witt congratulated Robert Pompei (President of the Darling Point Society) and his team for hosting an excellent meeting and for the energy they bring to fostering community spirit. Councillor Witt advised that at the meeting, Colin Finn of the Blue Green Alliance presented a very interesting proposal for rewilding Rushcutters Bay. 

Councillor Witt further advised that she attended the NSW Local Government Conference held in Tamworth on 17 November to 19 November 2024. Councillor Witt recommended the presentation conducted by Andy Johnston (Local Government Information Unit) where he stresses the importance of advocating for Local Government constitutional recognition, and for hanging onto local planning powers. The presentation can be found on the LGNSW website.

Councillor Parmegiani:

  • Local Government NSW Conference
Councillor Parmegiani advised that he attended the NSW Local Government Conference held in Tamworth on 17 November to 19 November 2024, describing it as a valuable experience for him as a newly-elected Councillor.

Councillor Jarvis:

  • Nielsen Park Update
  • Remembrance Day
  • Local Government NSW Conference
  • Opening of Harbour Early Learning Centre
Councillor Jarvis provided a brief update on the Nielsen Park upgrades, advising that the project has been further delayed but praised the work being done on the kiosk.

Councillor Jarvis further advised that on 1 November 2024 she attended the Remembrance Day ceremony held at Tingira Memorial Park, Rose Bay. Councillor Jarvis informed that those in attendance included 100yo WWII veteran and Vaucluse resident John Ryrie, along with the executive and members of the Rose Bay RSL sub-branch, and Commanding Officer Aaron Scott of HMAS Watson. Councillor Jarvis shared that the HMAS Watson morning tea and tour the next day was hosted by Commanding Officer Aaron Scott who, after 3 years at HMAS Watson will be leaving the Base. Councillor Jarvis expressed her pleasure in meeting the incoming Commander, Kath Jones.

Councillor Jarvis advised that she attended the NSW Local Government Conference held in Tamworth on 17 November to 19 November 2024. Councillor Jarvis reported that all of Council's motions presented at the conference were passed and acknowledged the event's genuine success.

Councillor Jarvis informed the Council that on 22 November 2024 she, along with the Mayor Councillor Swan attended the Harbour Early Learning Centre opening in Vaucluse, advising that it will be a great addition to the LGA for its young people. Councillor Jarvis acknowledged the attendance of Nicole Tainsh, the Principal of the adjoining Vaucluse Public School.

Councillor Silcocks:

  • Darling Point Society AGM
  • Congratulations to Staff on Forest Road Flooding
Councillor Silcocks reported on the Darling Point Society's AGM, recognising Charlotte Feldman, the former President of the Darling Point Society, and congratulated Max Herford on stepping down as Vice President. Councillor Silcocks extended his congratulations to Mr. Herford's replacement Jillian Blackall.

Councillor Silcocks discussed the flooding issues on Forest Road, Double Bay, and congratulated the staff for their efforts in addressing the problem.

Councillor Ardouin:

  • Darling Point Society AGM
  • Double Bay Christmas Festival
Councillor Ardouin advised that on 21 November 2024 he attended the Darling Point Society's AGM, recognising Robert Pompei (President of the Darling Point Society) and his team, particularly for their efforts in significantly increasing the Society's membership.

Councillor Ardouin advised the the Double Bay Christmas Festival will be held on Saturday 30 November 2024 and encouraged all Councillors to attend and support the local community.

Councillor Zeltzer:

  • Acknowledging Paddington Library
Councillor Zeltzer advised that she recently attended the Paddington Library with her Grandson for 'Rhyme Time'. Councillor Zeltzer praised Morrin Deleves (Senior Library Customer Service Officer) and her team on delivering 'Rhyme Time', highlighting growing popularity.

Councillor Mitchell:

  • Citizenship Ceremony
  • Remembrance Day
Councillor Mitchell advised that on 20 November 2024 she attended the Citizenship Ceremony held at Woollahra Council Chambers. Councillor Mitchell expressed her gratitude to Patricia Vella (Executive Assistant to the Mayor & General Manager), for finding photos of Councillor Mitchell’s husband becoming an Australian citizen at Woollahra Council four years ago.

Councillor Mitchell further advised that she observed Remembrance Day and expressed her thanks to Woolworths for observing a one-minute silence in honour of the day.

The Mayor, Councillor Swan:

  • Paddington Chamber of Commerce AGM
  • Doing Business in Woollahra Event
  • Launch of the Royal Motor Yacht Squadron Boating Season
  • Paddington Society AGM
  • NAJEX
  • Reembrace Prayers at Central Synagogue
  • Breast Cancer Foundation Launch
  • Acknowledging Jewish House
  • Citizenship Ceremony
  • Opening of Harbour Early Learning Centre
The Mayor, Councillor Swan advised that on 29 October 2024 she attended the Paddington Chamber of Commerce AGM. The Mayor congratulated the newly elected committee and wish them well for the year ahead and looks forward to working with them all.

On 29 October 2024 the Mayor attended the Doing Business in Woollahra Event. The Mayor congratulated the staff for a wonderful event and thanked guest speaker, Therese Tarlinton (Business Marketing expert, speaker and author).

On 2 November 2024 she, along with the Deputy Mayor Councillor Carmichael attended the launch of the Royal Motor Yacht Squadron boating season. The Mayor congratulated to the club and especially the Commodore for a wonderful day and wished the club all the best for the season.

On 6 November 2024 the Mayor attended the Paddington Society's AGM with Councillors Andruska, Price and Regan.

On 10 November 2024 the Mayor attended the Remembrance Day service and NAJEX (NSW Association of Jewish Service & Ex-Service Men & Women) wreath-laying at the Sydney Jewish Museum.

On 12 November 2024 the Mayor attended the Reembrace Prayers at Central Synagogue. The Mayor congratulated the organisers on a very moving ceremony.

 


On 14 November 2024 the Mayor attended the Breast Cancer Foundation launch at Chiswick Gardens. The Mayor acknowledged the very important work being done to raise funds in support of publicly available healthcare.

On 21 November 2024 the Mayor, along with Deputy Mayor Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Andruska and Councillor Zeltzer attended Jewish House. The Mayor acknowledged the important work in providing a shelter for those in desperate need.

On 21 November 2024 the Mayor attended  the Citizenship Ceremony held at Woollahra Council Chambers.

On 21 November 2024 the Mayor, along with Councillor Jarvis attended the Harbour Early Learning Centre opening in Vaucluse

Councillor Regan asking:


To the General Manager and the Director of Planning and Place.

 

On 15 November 2023 Council passed a Notice of Motion in item 16.2 as follows:


(see next page)

 

 

https://woollahra.infocouncil.biz/Open/2023/11/CO_20231115_AGN_AT.PDF#page249

 

Some developments undertaken under this Housing SEPP have already completed (eg: 58 Newcastle St Rose Bay) and some are due to complete shortly (117 O'Sullivan Rd, Bellevue Hill and 30/32 Newcastle St Rose Bay, where an occupation certificate is imminent). Neighbours to these developments have asked what compliance measures Council has in place to ensure occupation is as required by the Housing SEPP, given the unique consent conditions for the construction and occupation of these developments.

 

Could Council please advise as to when a report will be presented to Council to address the matters raised in the Notice of Motion 16.2 passed on 15 November 2023 given the current situation and anxiety in the community regarding compliance with unique conditions of consent.


Director, Planning & Place in response:

Council maintains a register of all positive covenants for which the Council is the prescribed authority and is proactively involved in the authorisation and registration of these positive covenants. Council receives written confirmation from our agents upon registration of these documents against the property title. A report will be presented to the Environmental Planning Committee at its meeting of 3 February 2025.

(Councillor Silcocks/Councillor Carmichael)

206/2024 Resolved:

THAT approval be granted to replace the existing ‘2P Ticket 9am-6pm Mon-Sat’ located on the eastern side of Bay Street, Double Bay, near shop 15 of 2-22 Knox Street, with ‘No Stopping’ restrictions for a distance of 5.865 metres, as shown in Attachment 1, for the installation of a parklet to support and encourage community connection by introducing additional outdoor seating and planting, subject to the following conditions: 

 

  1. Any directive provided by the NSW Police Force is to be complied with.

  2. All conditions contained within the Parklet Approval issued by Woollahra Council (Attachment 2).

  3. The parklet is to operate in conjunction to the approved footway dining permit and operate for a period of 12 months commencing from the date in which the applicant is notified of the determination of their application with the potential for extension.

  4. The applicant must supply and erect protection barriers for the parklet to ensure public safety. The applicant must remove any implemented barriers, at the completion of the period.

  5. The applicant must inform Council officers when the parklet is no longer required and will be removed.

  6. Council shall be indemnified against all claims for damage or injury that may result from either the activities or from the occupation of part of the public road reserve during the activities. A copy of Public Liability Insurance Cover to the value of $20,000,000 shall be provided to Council prior to the installation of the parklet and Council must be listed as an interested party on the insurance policy.

  7. Council shall be reimbursed for the cost of repair of any damage caused to Council property as a result of the activities.

  8. Noise created by the use of equipment or activity must be controlled as required by the ‘Protection of the Environment Operations (Noise Control) Regulation 2000’.

  9. The applicant must make arrangements to remove all waste/rubbish from the parklet on a daily basis.

  10. Failure to comply with any of these conditions may result in the cancellation of the use of a parklet at Council’s discretion.

  11. Woollahra Council reserves the right to cancel this approval at any time.


The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

None

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Zeltzer asking:

In the light of the reasonable concerns raised by Cr Ardouin at the Finance and Community Services Meeting of the 11th November 2024 regarding mechanisms for controlling, reporting and managing cost blowouts in Council projects, what safeguards does council have in place to prevent or mitigate blowouts in cost in the delivery of larger projects? 

Furthermore, what strategies does Council engage in order to reduce the impact of such blowouts on Council's working capital?

Director, Infrastructure and Sustainability and Chief Financial Officer in response:
 
Capital projects are managed in accordance with Council’s Project Management Framework and more specifically the Project Management Policy and Project Management Procedure adopted by ELT in 2021. The procedure includes processes for setting project budgets and managing variations to scope, time and cost.  In brief, the following process is followed for control of project variations;
 
  1. Status of projects, including potential variations, reviewed by designated Project Manager and Asset Owner (Project Sponsor) at regular meetings.
  2. Written approval is received from the Asset Owner for any variation that affects the overall project budget. 
  3. All ‘at risk’ projects are reviewed by the General Manager, Director Infrastructure and Sustainability, Manager Capital Projects and Manager Property at a monthly Capital Works Projects meeting. 
  4. Variations are reported to the elected Council via the Capital Works Program Quarterly Progress Report and Quarterly Budget Review.
 
Specifically in regard to Council’s strategic property projects, i.e. the Wilberforce and Cross Street Carpark projects, staff are following a project control process based on the process successfully used for the Kiaora Place project at Double Bay. In the case of the Wilberforce Carpark project, the process for managing the construction phase of the project will be;

 

 
  1. A Project Control Group (PCG) comprising of representatives of the appointed building contractor, Council’s appointed Project Manager (Impact Group) and Council’s Manager Property will meet monthly to review progress of the project and review proposed variations/issues.
  2. All requests for contract variations will be reviewed by the Project Manager (following advice from a Quantity Surveyor where necessary) and referred to the Manager Property for consideration. 
  3. The Manager Property will report the activity of the PCG, and any material variations, to the Landowner Project Group (LPG). The LPG is comprised of Director Infrastructure and Sustainability, Director Corporate Performance and Manager Property as core members, with other staff and external advisors attending meetings as necessary. 
  4. The Director Infrastructure and Sustainability will, on behalf of the LPG, provide regular updates to ELT on progress of the project. 
  5. Contract variations within the approved project budget, including contingency, can be approved by the General Manager (and Director Infrastructure and Sustainability as delegated). Variations which will result in expenditure beyond the approved project budget will be reported to Council. 
  6. The elected Council will be provided updates on progress of the project. Such updates to be provided as material issue arise, or otherwise at least quarterly. 
To prevent and manage the potential for a working capital blowout, the council has implemented the following strategies:

  1. Efficient Revenue Collection:
    Council has implemented processes to encourage timely payment of rates and fees, including charging interest on overdue debts. In addition, the council offers quarterly instalment plans and maintains a robust debt collection process.
  2. Prudent Budget Management:
    Council aligns operational and capital expenditures with realistic revenue forecasts and available funding sources, reviewing these quarterly.
    Council undertakes a comprehensive annual budgeting process for both operational and capital expenditures (CAPEX).
    A rolling Long-Term Financial Plan (LTFP) is maintained, covering a 10-year horizon in compliance with Office of Local Government (OLG) requirements, and sensitivity analysis is conducted on the LTFP.
  3. Regular Financial Monitoring:
    Council monitors its cashflow monthly and reports the results to the Council at the monthly Finance, Community & Services (FC&S) Committee meeting.
    Council also tracks upcoming working capital needs, particularly with respect to the maturity of term deposits, before reinvesting.
    Procurement and expenditure are governed by a system of internal controls, including financial delegations, policies, and procedures.
  4. Flexible Financing Options:
    Council ensures access to short-term funding by maintaining a level of cash funds that are readily available.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Ardouin asking:

Noting that the Australian Fashion Council (AFC) released a statement on 13 November confirming that the Australian Fashion Week (AFW) will not proceed in 2025:

  • If the data is available - how many fashion enterprises operate within the LGA and what is their economic impact (i.e. number of employees, contribution to local economy, etc.)?
  • What mechanisms does Council have to support the local fashion industry?
Manager, Strategic Planning & Place in response:

  • If the data is available - how many fashion enterprises operate within the LGA and what is their economic impact (i.e. number of employees, contribution to local economy, etc.)?
  1. There are 665 retail trade businesses in Woollahra LGA (6.4% of total businesses vs 5.9% MSW average, employing 2551 people (11.2% of total employment vs 9.4% NSW average). Source Economy ID.

  2. Department and clothing stores contributed $148.27M to local spend in FY23/24 which was 18% of total local sales and service income.

  3. Year to date calendar year (to 30 October 2024) department and clothing stores have contributed $113M to local spend. $27M from resident local spend and $86M from visitor spend. 

  4. Year to date calendar year (to 30 October 2024) local residents have spent $95M in online spend on department and clothing store items (compared to $27M locally), demonstrating the ongoing market trend and importance of local fashion businesses in providing online trading options.

  5. Further economic and spend data analysis is provided to the business community by Council online at https://www.woollahra.nsw.gov.au/Services/Business/Economic-Insights 
  • What mechanisms does Council have to support the local fashion industry?
 
  • Our new Economic Development Coordinator (who started in April 2024) has been proactively supporting and engaging with businesses (including fashion). Over 2,500 local businesses have been contacted including over 300 fashion businesses.

  1. We are currently working on improving our online resources to simplify and streamline processes at https://www.woollahra.nsw.gov.au/Services/Business. Resources include: Start, Transfer or Grow your Business; Updates, Events and Business Promotions; Grants and Business Support; Grants and Resources.

  2. $95,000 in grant funding was awarded to Placemaking and Business Sector Support applications in July 2024, fashion businesses and business networks that support retail and fashion business are encouraged to apply. Examples are the Bay Street Initiative and the Paddington Chamber of Commerce.

  3. The small business workshop held on 29 October 2024 provided small businesses with training on marketing and the use of AI tools. Ninety two local businesses attended including fashion business.  The feedback has been very positive.

  4. A business networking night is to be held on 4 December, and 306 local fashion businesses have been invited. Currently, 157 businesses in all categories are registered.

  5. More events for fashion and other businesses include quarterly business bites workshops and tech express workshops hosted by Woollahra Library.

  6. Council funding of $25,000 was provided to the Queen Street & West Woollahra Association to facilitate the Woollahra 2025 Festival in March 2025. The program (a work in progress) will include a Fashion and Beauty stream with proposed:
  • Late night Friday opening
  • In-store fashion shows
  • Fashion talks in-store or at an external venue
  • Make up master classes
  • Hair styling master classes
  • Fragrance selection master classes
  • ‘How to become a model’ talks (possible breakfast or lunch talk in a restaurant)
  • Weekend special discounts

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Ardouin asking:

Regarding the Youth Recreation Facility at Rushcutters Bay (aka Skate Park):

  • At what stage is the application concerning the facility to Heritage NSW?
  • What is the flow chart of actions following the determination by Heritage NSW, either to cancellation of the project or commencement of construction?
  • In the event the project is unable to commence, have staff identified alternative sites for a youth facility throughout the LGA?
Manager, Open Space & Trees in response:

  • At what stage is the application concerning the facility to Heritage NSW?The most up to date comment was included in the Capital Works report presented on 11 November FC&S were;

    To proceed with the Rushcutters Bay Park Youth Facility, a Section 60 application to Heritage NSW is required which is currently being prepared. Following a meeting with Heritage NSW for pre-lodgement advice, a Review of Environmental Factors (REF) is being finalised and an Aboriginal cultural values assessment is complete. In review of the draft REF, an updated acoustics report, a detailed site assessment and an Acid Sulphate Soils Assessment is required to be included in the REF. These documents are currently being finalised and will be included in a final REF for submission to the Director, Planning and Place for review and assessment. Should the REF be approved, the S60 application will be submitted. It is expected to be submitted to Heritage NSW in Q2 FY24/25.

  • What is the flow chart of actions following the determination by Heritage NSW, either to cancellation of the project or commencement of construction?

    There is a resolution of Council to proceed with this project, however we need the S60 application approval to proceed with the facility. Assuming that the S60 is approved, Council will move forward with progressing the youth recreation facility.

  • In the event the project is unable to commence, have staff identified alternative sites for a youth facility throughout the LGA?

    The original Council resolution was that the site should cater for the western area of the LGA, Paddington and Edgecliff. During the planning of the facility, we did investigate Trumper Park and Rushcutters Bay Park.

    Council’s Recreation Strategy has a strategic direction that states;

    - An additional site might allow the development of further youth facilities to complement, not duplicate those proposed at Rushcutters Bay. Lyne Park is well positioned for such a development given its location and current user groups.

    - Undertake a feasibility study for the development of a significant youth precinct at Lyne Park (or another appropriate site) providing complementary features to that proposed at Rushcutters Bay.

236/2024 Recommendation:

THAT Council:

  1. Note the content of this report;

  2. Request that staff update the Council’s website setting out the development standards for the installation of air conditioning in Heritage Conservation areas:

    i. under the exempt development pathway in State Environmental Planning Policy (Exempt and Complying Development Codes) 2008; and
    ii. a development application or a complying development certificate must be submitted to obtain development consent for the proposed works if they do not already comply.

  3. Request that staff amend the Woollahra Local Strategic Planning Statement to include the words, "Lobby as appropriate, the State Government for changes to the State Environmental Planning Policy Exempt and Complying Development Codes 2008, to achieve greater transparency and equity in the approval process for the installation of air conditioning within heritage conservation areas."

  4. Note that this Council resolution (initiated by a Notice of Motion on 11 December 2023) is now closed.


The Motion was put and Carried.

In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"The Mayor, Councillor Swan

  • Thanks to Councillors

The Mayor thanked all Councillors who represented her over the last two weeks whilst she was absent from Council.

Councillor Woodgate:

  • Scotts College Awards Day
  • Recognising Woollahra Gallery Volunteers
  • Congratulations to Volunteer SES Retiree, Colin McQueen

Councillor Woodgate advised that on 10 December 2024 he represented the Mayor at the Scotts College Awards Day along with Kellie Sloane (Member for Vaucluse) and Allegra Spender MP. Councillor Woodgate congratulated Macgregor Finlayson on receiving the Rotary Award.

Councillor Woodgate further advised that on 12 December 2024 he represented the Mayor at Woollahra Gallery's event in recognition of the Gallery's volunteers. Councillor Woodgate highlighted a speech given by Oscar Steele in which Mr. Steele emphasised the positive impact that volunteering at the Gallery has had in providing him with connections to the Community and forming new friendships. Councillor Woodgate extended his gratitude to all the Gallery's volunteers.

On 3 December 2024, Councillor Woodgate along with Tom O'Hanlon (Director, Infrastructure & Sustainability) attended the retirement of SES Volunteer, Colin McQueen. Councillor Woodgate acknowledged Mr. McQueen's 55 years of service with the SES and expressed gratitude for his dedication. He requested that the Mayor write a letter of congratulations to Mr. McQueen.

Councillor Regan

  • Double Bay Christmas Fair

Councillor Regan advised that she recently attended the Double Bay Christmas Fair where she was pleased to see former Mayor of Woollahra, Susan Wynne. She congratulated the organisers on a successful event despite the challenging weather.

Councillor Robertson

  • Support for Mayoral Minute

Councillor Robertson apologised for his absence during the consideration or vote on the Mayoral Minute regarding the recent attacks in Woollahra. Councillor Robertson took this opportunity to state that, if present he would have voted in favour of the Mayoral Minute and that it  it will bring some comfort to our community particularly, to the Jewish members of our community at this most difficult time. Councillor Robertson thanked the Mayor for the actions she will take pursuant to the motion.

Councillor Price

  • Recognition Day for Glenmore Road Public School

Councillor Price advised that she, along with Councillor Andruska recently attended the Recognition Day for Glenmore Road Public School. Councillor Price congratulated the school's students and staff for another wonderful year.

Councillor Torsten

  • Queen Street Christmas Window Display Awards
  • Support for the Queen Street Festival

Councillor Torsten advised that he recently attended the Queen Street Christmas Window Display Awards along with Deputy Mayor Councillor Carmichael and Councillor Mitchell. Councillor Torsten highlighted the sense of community being felt in Woollahra .

Councillor Torsten further stated that given the recent anti-Semitic attacks on Woollahra residents, Woollahra Council should offer as much help as possible to former Woollahra Councillor Luise Elsing, who is currently organising the Queen Street Festival in March 2025.

Councillor Witt

  • Staff Rewards & Recognition Day

Councillor Witt advised that she attended the recent Staff Rewards & Recognition Day held at Randwick Racecourse. Councillor Witt congratulated those staff who received awards and recognised those being celebrated for their long-service to Council.

Councillor Parmegiani

  • Anti-Semitism
  • Head On Photo Festival
  • Staff Rewards & Recognition Day 

Councillor Parmegiani advised that on 29 November 2024 he, along with Deputy Mayor Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Jarvis and former Woollahra Councillor Isabelle Shapiro attended the Kehillat Kadimah Synagogue, Rose Bay where they spoke to the Jewish Community about their concerns about antisemitism.

Councillor Parmegiani further advised that on 30 November 2024 he attended the Head On Photo Festival where he spoke with the organiser, Mr. Moshe Rosenzveig OAM. Councillor Parmegiani expressed how impressed he was with the scope and the scale of this international festival, which attracts photographers from all around the world. He noted that some of the exhibition is showcased in the Paddington Reserve and suggested there is potential to expand the event in the Woollahra Municipality.

Councillor Parmegiani also advised that he attended the Staff Rewards & Recognition Day held at Randwick Racecourse. Councillor Parmegiani stated that he was impressed by the stories of award winners and also by staff retention rates. Councillor Parmegiani noted that the ability of the Council to retain staff for such an extended periods a credit to the organisation.

Councillor Jarvis

  • Re-opening of Neilsen Park
  • End-of-Year School Events
  • Thanks to Staff

Councillor Jarvis shared an update regarding the reopening of Neilsen Park, also known as Shark Beach, Vaucluse.

Councillor Jarvis further advised that she recently represented the Mayor at the end-of-year events for Rose Bay Public School, Vaucluse Public School, and McAuley Catholic Primary School. Councillor Jarvis highlighted that these occasions are a proud moment for the children, their parents, and their grandparents.

Councillor Jarvis expressed her gratitude to staff, recognising their hard work and assistance throughout the year.

Councillor Silcocks

  • Staff Rewards & Recognition Day

Councillor Silcocks congratulated staff on the success of the Rewards & Recognition Day, noting that all the Councillors who attended thoroughly enjoyed the event.

Councillor Ardouin

  • Thanks to Staff - Double Bay Flooding
  • Double Bay Christmas Markets
  • Sydney Moring Herald Housing Initiative
  • Double Bay Public School End of Year Presentations
  • Double Bay Residents Association End of Year Event

Councillor Ardouin expressed his gratitude to staff for their ongoing work, highlighting their efforts during the recent flooding in Double Bay. Councillor Ardouin gave particular praise to Tom O'Hanlon (Director, Infrastructure & Sustainability) and his team.

Councillor Ardouin further advised that on 30 November 2024, he attended the Double Bay Christmas Markets and thanked the Bay Street Initiative and all the organisers for facilitating a successful event.

Councillor Ardouin advised that on 2 December 2024, he attended a Sydney Morning Herald Forum where it was announced that a series of articles on housing for Gen Z would be published. The councillor praised this as a valuable initiative. Councillor Ardouin further stated that a recurring theme at the forum was the need for increased funding for Councils, as they are on the front lines of building infrastructure and supporting the growth of dwellings.

Councillor Ardouin further reported that he represented the Mayor at the Double Bay Public School end of year presentation, and thanked the teachers, staff and students for running an excellent event.

Councillor Ardouin advised that on 11 December 2024 he attended the Double Bay Residents Association end of year event. Councillor Ardouin thanked the residents group for being such a robust addition to the Local Government Area, noting their positive input to the debate around developments in the area.

Councillor Zeltzer

  • Congratulations to Larissa Holbert

Councillor Zeltzer advised that she would like to commend Larissa Holbert (Senior Assessment Officer), for her recent comprehensive report submitted to the Sydney Eastern City Planning Panel (SECP). Councillor Zeltzer advised that the Chair of the SECP, the Honorable Carl Scully, recognised the report as being of exceptional quality.

Councillor Mitchell

  • Queen Street West Woollahra Christmas Event
  • Queen Street Christmas Window Display Awards

Councillor Mitchell advised that she, along with Deputy Mayor Councillor Carmichael and Councillor Torsten represented the Mayor at the recent Queen Street West Woollahra Christmas Event and Queen Street Christmas Window Display Awards.

Councillor Mitchell further advised, that at these events she had the opportunity to speak with Giles Edmonds, President of the Queen Street West Woollahra Association with the two sharing ideas around events celebrating Woollahra in 2025.

Councillor Zeltzer asking:


Review of the location of the public phone box on the entry to Glenmore Road from Oxford Street. 

 

Can council contact the agency in charge of the phone box on the entry to Glenmore Road and request that it be moved around onto Oxford Street for the following reasons:


  1. The Phone Box is in garish colours in an area which is a heritage conservation precinct. The colours are out of keeping with the heritage value of this part of Paddington.

  2. As a utility it would serve best on the busier thoroughfare being Offord Street, as it has increased visibility for use. Currently the reports from proximal shopkeepers are that there is no users at all in the current location.

  3. The Phone Box is located such that view lines when entering Glenmore Road are greatly impacted, so the terminal point of the view line being the heritage listed Hotel on this part of Glenmore Road is completely cut off, as the phone box is an obstruction to the much valued view lines, and the sensitively conserved small retail precinct.

  4. So much cost and effort has been given to keeping this location in good order and respecting its heritage values such that a somewhat obsolete phone box (everyone has a mobile phone)  in this day and age, in this heritage sensitive location, makes no sense.
Can council officers report back their findings on this matter and any success in their dealings with the relevant agency in order to have the phone box relocated onto Oxford Street or removed completely . 

Director, Infrastructure & Sustainability in Response:

Staff previously corresponded with Telstra in early 2021 in regards to relocation of the existing telephone box, without success. At the time, Telstra offered at Council’s cost to replace the existing telephone box with a kiosk-style public phone in the same location, which would not have achieved the desired outcome. Staff are happy to revisit the issue and approach Telstra with a request to move the public phone into Oxford Street.

257/2024 Resolved:

That Council:

  1. Notes and deplores:
  1. The recent anti-Israel and antisemitic attack in Woollahra on Wednesday 11 December 2024, which follows on from a similar heinous attack in Woollahra on 21 November 2024.

  2. The ongoing antisemitic graffiti within the Waverley local government area.

  3. The recent terror attack at Adass Israel Synagogue of Melbourne on 6 December 2024.

  4. The Islamophobic graffiti that took place this past weekend in Chester Hill.

  1. Welcomes the ongoing commitment by the NSW Premier to Operation Shelter, which will provide a higher Police presence across key parts of Sydney and the establishment of Operation Avalite by the Australian Federal Police that will focus on investigating an increase in antisemitic threats and violence.

  2. Thanks Woollahra Council staff for their cooperation with New South Wales Police and in particular, their efficient removal of graffiti.

  3. Notes that the Mayor will be seeking an urgent meeting with the following people to discuss the ongoing rise of antisemitism and Islamophobia in our local communities and how all levels of government can work proactively and collaboratively together to combat it, including:
  1. The Member for Wentworth.

  2. The Member for Vaucluse.

  3. The Member for Sydney.

  4. The Member for Coogee.

  5. The Mayor of Waverley Council.

  6. The Mayor of Randwick Council.

  7. The Member for Blaxland.

  8. The Member for Auburn.

  9. The Mayor of Canterbury-Bankstown Council.

  1. Notes that the Mayor will continue to make contact with Islamic and Jewish faith leaders, to discuss how all faiths can come together to support our local communities during this time.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Note:           Cr Toni Zeltzer and Cr Merrill Witt addressed the Panel.

Resolved:

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel advises Council:

  1. To proceed with the planning proposal (at Attachment 1) as it has strategic merit, which seeks to amend the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 by introducing a local provision to restrict net dwelling loss to no more than one (1) dwelling or 15% of existing dwellings, whichever is the greater. 

  2. Given the NSW Government push to increase housing across the Greater Sydney metropolitan region, that the DPHI be requested to review how the issue of a reduction in housing numbers be addressed at a State policy level, given State policies prevail over any local policies.


Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion                      Against the Motion

Graham Brown
Penelope Holloway
Ronald Schaffer
Lisa Trueman

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Note:   The Chair, David Ryan declared a Significant Non-Pecuniary interest in Item 3.1 
            (Planning Proposal -  Double Bay Centre) as David Ryan's company, Gyde Consulting 
            prepared a submission on behalf of a client for the draft Double Bay Strategy.
            David Ryan did not take part in the site inspection, briefing session, debate or vote on 
            this matter.  David Ryan vacated the Chair and Peter Brennan assumed the Chair.

Note:   Malcolm Young declared a Significant Non-Pecuniary interest in Item 3.1 (Planning 
            Proposal - Double Bay Centre) as past President in April 2022 
            I made a submission on behalf of the Double Bay Resident’s Association on the original 
            Strategy as well as making my own personal submissions.  I made both written and oral 
            submission on the Revised Strategy in October 2023.  Malcolm Young
            did not take part in the site inspection, briefing session, debate or vote on this
            matter.   

Note:   Late correspondence was tabled at the meeting by Kim Stuart, NSW EPA, Robert Swift, 
            Malcolm Young, GSA Planning and Double Bay Residents Association.

Note:   Councillor Merrill Witt addressed the Panel

 


Resolved:

 
A.    THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel advises Council that it supports the planning
        proposal (as provided at Attachment 1 of the Panel Agenda), as it demonstrates site-
        specific and strategic merit for the following reasons:

        i.       The planning proposal is consistent with the relevant objectives of the Greater 
                 Sydney Region Plan: A Metropolis of Three Cities and the relevant planning 
                 priorities and actions of the Eastern City District Plan.
       ii.       The planning proposal aligns with the Woollahra Local Strategic Planning
                 Statement, Woollahra Local Housing Strategy and Council’s Community  
                 Strategic Plan Woollahra 2032.
       iii.      The planning proposal provides a clear and coordinated framework to guide future 
                 development in the Double Bay Centre, which has been under significant 
                 development pressure over the past several years.
 
B.     THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel advises Council that it supports the planning 
         proposal for the Double Bay Centre to establish a precinct-based approach and amend 
         the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 as follows: 

        i.    Insert Clause 4.3D Exceptions to building heights that allows a range of
              maximum height controls between 18.4m to 21.5m on certain sites in the
              Double Bay Centre if requirements for minimum frontage length are met;
       ii.    Insert Clause 4.4F Exceptions to floor space ratio that allows a range of maximum
             floor space ratio controls between 3:1 to 3.5:1 on certain sites in the Double Bay 
             Centre if requirements for minimum frontage length are met;
      iii.    Insert local provisions to establish requirements for residential unit mix for all
             development in the Double Bay Centre;
      iv.    Prevent bonuses from other environmental planning instruments applying where the 
             increased building heights and floor space ratios are taken up, given the significant 
             urban design testing that was prepared to inform this planning proposal; 
      v.    Repeal Clause 4.4A Exceptions to floor space ratio (Areas 1 and 1A—Double Bay) 
             which will be superseded by the proposed controls
 
C.    The Woollahra Local Planning Panel advises Council that it supports the planning
        proposal, subject to the following additional considerations:

        i.    Advocacy for amendments to the State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021
             to prevent the application of the bonus provisions.
        ii.   A review of the objectives of new development standards to strengthen the intent of
             minimum site frontage requirements and further express the importance of 
             consolidating sites.

D.    The Woollahra Local Planning Panel notes the late correspondence submitted on 
        this Item, which made detailed and site-specific comments regarding elements of
        the planning proposal. The Panel recommends that staff address these issues
        in a future report to Council.

 


Note:
In accordance with section 375A of the Local Government Act a Division of votes is recorded on this planning matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion




Peter Brennan

Ronald Schaffer

Heather Warton




3/0

Panel’s Decision

The Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, grants development consent to DA300/2024/1 to amalgamate two attached terraces creating a single dwelling with extensive alterations and additions including a new garage and loft above on land at 156 - 158 Jersey Road PADDINGTON, subject to the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

The Panel modified Condition A.4 to include the additional wording “or similar climbing species”.

The Panel included an additional Condition H.5 which prohibits the use of the loft as a separate domicile.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel considered that the matters raised in written and verbal submissions have been adequately addressed in the assessment report and by the conditions of consent.

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Panel’s Decision

The Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council as the consent authority, is satisfied that the matters required to be addressed under Clause 4.6(3) of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 have been demonstrated and that consent may be granted to the development application, which contravenes the Height of Buildings development standard under Clause 4.3 of Woollahra LEP 2014. 

AND 

The Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, grants development consent to Development Application No. 223/2024/1 for Alterations and additions to an existing dwelling on land at 22 Ginahgulla Road BELLEVUE HILL, subject to the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site inspection, considered the submissions and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).


Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.
