164/2025 Recommendation:

THAT Council:

  1. Note the advice provided by the Woollahra Local Planning Panel on 20 February 2025 regarding the planning proposal to amend the controls for the Double Bay Centre.

 

  1. Resolves to support the planning proposal as contained at Attachment 1 of the report to the Environmental Planning Committee of 7 April 2025 to revise controls for the Double Bay Centre and that this is forwarded to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure seeking a Gateway determination to allow public exhibition.

  2. Requests the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces (or delegate) to authorise Council as the local plan-making authority to make the local environmental plan under section 3.36 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

  3. Requests staff to carry out updates to the traffic report (prior to a post exhibition report) in relation to the Double Bay Centre incorporating the cumulative impact of the Low and Mid-Rise Housing Policy.

  4. In response to community concerns raised by the Double Bay Residents Association, requests staff provide advice to full Council on the inter-relationship between the Planning Proposal and Council's relevant studies and controls to abate dewatering in the Double Bay precinct.

  5. Requests staff provide further evidence that increasing the height and FSR controls for the corner sites on Manning Road and Kiaora Lane won’t impact pedestrian access to Kiaora Lane.

The Motion was put and Carried.
 
Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

Note:   Late correspondence was tabled by Nick Economou, Manager Development Control

(O'Hanlon/Pedder)

Resolved: Pursuant to Section 4.16 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979

THAT Council, as the consent authority, is not satisfied that the applicant has demonstrated under Clause 4.6 of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 that compliance with the Floor Space Ratio (FSR) development standard under Clause 4.4(E) of Woollahra LEP 2014 is unreasonable or unnecessary in the circumstances, and there are sufficient environmental planning grounds to justify the contravention of the development standard.

AND 

 

That Council, as the consent authority, refuse development consent to DA470/2023/1 for the demolition of the existing dwelling and construction of a new two storey dwelling with basement garage on land at 76 Kings Road VAUCLUSE, for the following reasons:

1.    Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014, Clause 1.2 Aims of Plan

The proposal has not sufficiently demonstrated that the bulk and scale achieves the desired future character intent, thus failing to achieve the following provision: 
 
  • Woollahra LEP 2014 - Clause 1.2(2) Aims of Plan:

     (l)  to ensure development achieves the desired future character of the area

2.    Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014, R2 Low Density Residential zone

The proposed development results in a building envelope which is visually intrusive therefore will not positively contribute to the desired future character of the neighbourhood, contrary to the following provisions: 

  • To provide for development that is compatible with the character and amenity of the surrounding neighbourhood.
  • To ensure that development is of a height and scale that achieves the desired future character of the neighbourhood.

3.    Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014, Clause 4.4 Floor Space Ratio

The proposed development exceeds the Floor Space Ratio development standard prescribed in Clause 4.4 of the WLEP 2014. The submitted Clause 4.6 Written Request supplies insufficient information and justification toward the non-compliance, thus it is considered to not adhere to the following provisions:

(i)  to ensure the bulk and scale of new development is compatible with the desired future 
     character of the area, and
(ii)  to minimise adverse environmental effects on the use or enjoyment of adjoining 
      properties and the public domain, and

4.    Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014, Clause 4.6 Exceptions to Development 
       Standards

The Applicant’s submitted Clause 4.6 Written Request for Floor Space Ratio is unsatisfactory with regard to the following provisions:

(a)  compliance with the development standard is unreasonable or unnecessary in the 
       circumstances, and
(b)  there are sufficient environmental planning grounds to justify the contravention of 
      the development standard.

5.    Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015, Chapter B3 General Development 
       Controls 

The proposed building envelope is excessive in terms of bulk and scale. It fails to achieve the following relevant objectives and controls prescribed in Chapter B3 General Development Controls of the Woollahra DCP 2015:

  • Part B3.5: Built Form and Context
     Part B3.5.1: Streetscape and Local Character

    Control C1 & Objectives O1 & O2

6.    Public Interest

The proposed development is not in the public interest.

Note:   Late correspondence was tabled by Wilson Perdigao, Paro Consulting.

Note:    Daniel Barber, Applicant addressed the Panel.

Panel’s Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, refuse to grant development consent to Development Application No. 402/2024/1 for alterations and additions to a dwelling house including a second floor (third storey) addition on land at 12 Wentworth Street Point Piper, subject to the Attachment (Adopted Reasons for Refusal).

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site orientation, considered the submissions and late correspondence and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel is satisfied that the application be refused for the reasons set out in Attachment  (Adopted Reasons for Refusal).

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

Note:   Late correspondence was tabled by Amanda Choularton, Organic Food Markets.

Panel’s Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, grant development consent to DA8/2025/1 for day event on Steyne Park - a community fair on 21 April 2025 (alternative date as 9 June 2025) on land at 2 William Street DOUBLE BAY, subject to the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent). 

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site orientation, considered the submissions and late correspondence and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

The Panel did not accept the request to delete Conditions H.5 and H.6 on the grounds that they have been standard conditions imposed on all previous consents on Steyne Park.  The Panel also noted that Condition H.6 does provide flexibility based on the anticipated attendees.


Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Kerry Kyiacou
David Ryan

The Mayor, Councillor Swan:

  • 2025 Woollahra Festival
  • ANZAC Day 2025
  • Remembering Bondi Junction Attack
  • Plaque Unveiling for Donald Richmond Horne AO
The Mayor, Councillor Swan advised that she recently attended the 2025 Woollahra Festival, stating that it was a great weekend of activities starting with the opening Event at Parterre, lunch on Victoria Street and the many activities planned around Woollahra. The Mayor thanked James Granter (Coordinator - Economic Development), Justine Henderson (Manager - Communications & Engagement) and all the Council staff involved in supporting the Queen Street West Woollahra Association in holding this fabulous celebration of Woollahra.

The Mayor further advised that on 25 April 2025 she had the honour to have hosted the Council's ANZAC Day Wreath Laying Ceremony at Steyne Park. This special ceremony was attended by eight (8) local schools, Consular representatives, local community and resident groups, and had Alexander He read his winning piece from the Mayor's ANZAC Day writing competition. The Mayor extended her thanks to all staff involved.

 

The Mayor shared with Council that one year on from the Bondi Junction attack she gathered with staff to remember those affected by the Bondi Junction Attacks. The Mayor stated that it was a moving time to remember and reflect. There was a gathering at Parliament House and a moving ceremony at the Bondi Junction Mall. The Mayor laid a floral tribute for Council and for the Woollahra Community.

On 1 April 2025, the Mayor unveiled a plaque marking the life and career of Donald Richmond Horne AO - a journalist, editor, author and academic, cultural critic, social analyst and one of Australia's foremost and most influential public intellectuals. The Mayor thanked Library staff for organising another successful plaque.

On 25 April 2025, the Mayor attended an ANZAC service at the Royal Sydney Golf Course, and attended a Dawn Service with the Royal Australian Naval Sailing Association (RANSA) where she was honoured to lay a wreath on Council's behalf. The Mayor also attended the Mark Moran Village Annual ANZAC Service. The Mayor expressed that it was an honour to attend the Service and read the two highly-commended entries from the Mayor's ANZAC Writing Competition.

Councillor Silcocks:

  • Remembering Bondi Junction Attack

Councillor Silcocks joined the Mayor in remembering the Bondi Junction attack one year on. Councillor Silcocks honoured all the victims, including those enduring long-term injuries and those who may have been forgotten over time.

Councillor Witt:

  • ANZAC Day 2025
  • Experimental Choreographic Showing at Drill Hall

Councillor Witt thanked the Mayor and all the staff involved in the ANZAC Day Service at Steyne Park, praising it as one of the best she had ever attended.

On 12 April 2025, Councillor Witt attended the Experimental Choreographic Showing at Drill Hall, Darling Point. Councillor Witt was overwhelmed with the amount of people in attendance and described the performance a wonderful showcase of performing art talent.

Councillor Jarvis:

  • ANZAC Day 2025
  • Queen Street Literary Festival
  • Opening of Double Bay Sailing Club Ramp

Councillor Jarvis added to the her fellow Councillor's remarks on the 2025 ANZAC Day Services and shared a brief comment on the plans unveiled at the Rose Bay RSL Club site. Councillor Jarvis stated that the plans mean a great new venue is coming for Rose Bay.

Councillor Jarvis praised staff for their work on the Queen Street Literary Festival, and congratulated local author Diana Reid on the upcoming release of her third book.

Councillor Jarvis congratulated staff on the successful opening of the Double Bay Sailing Club ramp, acknowledging all of the engineering challenges that went into making it happen.

https://woollahra.infocouncil.biz/Open/2023/11/CO_20231115_AGN_AT.PDF#page249

The Mayor, Councillor Swan asking:

  1. How frequently does Council undertake clean up of Double Bay beach?

  2. How frequently does Council undertake clean up of Watsons Bay beach?

  3. What communication has Council had with Sydney Water in respect of the cleanliness of Double Bay beach and Watsons Bay beach?

Manager Civil Operations, and Environment & Sustainability Team Leader in response:

  1. How frequently does Council undertake clean up of Double Bay beach?
Council attends daily to the western end of Double Bay Beach, our team service all waste bins, conduct a manual litter pick, and remove any large debris as required. In addition to this daily schedule, each beach is mechanically cleaned using a beach rake and tractor at least once a week. It's important to note that tidal conditions play a significant role in beach access, with high tides approximately every second week limiting our ability to safely operate machinery along the foreshore. Council cannot access the eastern end of the beach as there is no public point of entry from the land side.

Following a request from Council, Maritime/TfNSW recently conducted a clean on the eastern end of Double Bay Beach due to access issues.

HarbourCare volunteers have completed 3 clean-ups at Double Bay in the last 12 months.

  1. How frequently does Council undertake clean up of Watsons Bay beach?
Council attends daily to Watsons Bay Beach, our team service all waste bins, conduct a manual litter pick, and remove any large debris as required. In addition to this daily schedule, each beach is mechanically cleaned using a beach rake and tractor at least once a week. It's important to note that tidal conditions play a significant role in beach access, with high tides approximately every second week limiting our ability to safely operate machinery along the foreshore.

After the recent storm/high tides, an excavator and backhoe were also used to remove sand from the footpath and remove excessive waste from the beach at Watsons Bay. 

HarbourCare volunteers have completed 23 clean ups at Watsons Bay beach in the past 12 months.

  1. What communication has Council had with Sydney Water in respect of the cleanliness of Double Bay beach and Watsons Bay beach?
Staff have raised issues with the cleanliness of Double Bay Beach with Sydney Water. Sydney Water own the large stormwater outlet that runs from Lough Playing Fields along Kiaora Road, Jamberoo lane and Sherbrook Avenue, draining into Double Bay in the eastern corner.

Council staff will be meeting with Sydney Water staff in May to discuss issues with water quality and whether there is potential to install a pollution trap on this stormwater channel. Council has installed pollution traps further up in the catchment, above Cooper Park, and on the drainage line emptying near Double Bay Ferry Wharf.

Council has not discussed cleanliness of Watsons Bay Beach with Sydney Water, as there are no Sydney Water owned stormwater outlets in the area. Council has a pollution trap at Military Road near Watsons Bay Wharf, and another is planned treating stormwater flowing to Gibsons Beach.

192/2025 Resolved:

Adopted
In Closed Session

Adopted

191/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Note the confidential legal advice included in this report.

  2. Notes that Council has made an application under the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009 (the GIPA request) seeking:
  • Documents evidencing assessments of potential flooding impacts or an increase in flooding risks caused by increasing the supply of housing in moderate to high flood prone areas of Double Bay and Rose Bay under the amendments made in State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) Amendment (Low and Mid Rise Housing) 2025 (EPI 81); and

  • Documents evidencing the steps the Minister considered appropriate or necessary to be taken before recommending the making of State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) Amendment (Low and Mid Rise Housing) 2025 (EPI 81) by the Governor; and

  • Documents evidencing the recommendation from the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces to the Governor recommending the making of State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) Amendment (Low and Mid Rise Housing) 2025 (EPI 81). 

  1. Notes that the Department of Planning and Infrastructure have sought an extension of 10 days for their response to the GIPA request to enable them to consult with third parties.

  2. Staff will table a further report to Council as soon as practicable.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Clause 18.2 of Council's Code of Meeting Practice the Council extended the time of the meeting for a maximum period of 30 minutes.

(Councillor Ardouin/Councillor Swan)

204/2025 Resolved:

That Council:

  1. Notes Woollahra Council’s extensive forward pipeline of capital works (i.e. Cross St and Wilberforce carparks) necessitates investigating options to lower Council’s overall cost of debt.

  2. Request the General Manager liaise with the Office of Local Government and Local Government NSW to explore a Council’s ability under relevant NSW legislation, in establishing a funding vehicle, similar in form and function to NAB's Local Government Funding Vehicle (delivered in conjunction with the Municipal Association of Victoria) as a collective initiative with other councils and capital providers, which would:
  1. Support local governments (including Woollahra Council) to unlock additional flexibility to utilise their balance sheets to invest in community assets that would diversify their income streams;

  2. Deliver a boost to their local economies through the increased investment in community amenities and infrastructure;
  3. Assist local governments to invest in the urgent infrastructure needed to facilitate the growth in dwellings and commercial activity as a result of the Low and Medium-rise Housing Policy;
  4. Increase competitive pressure on the providers of municipal debt, which in turn would lower borrowing costs.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Swan, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Zeltzer

Malcolm Young declared a Significant Non-Pecuniary Interest in Item 4.1 (61/372 Edgecliff Road, Woollahra as Malcolm Young's wife is one of the objectors on this item.  Malcolm Young did not take part in the site inspection, briefing session, debate or vote on this matter.

Note:Late Correspondence was tabled by Wendy Sherman & Angelika Trube.

Note: Angelika Trube, Steve Schinagel, Wendy Sherman & Debbie-Lyn Gibb, objectors & Riccardo Adirosi & Luigi Rosselli, Architects, addressed the Panel.

Panel’s Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, grant development consent to Development Application No. 29/2025/1 for alterations and additions to the penthouse unit (Unit 61) of an existing residential flat building on land at 61/372 Edgecliff Road Woollahra, subject to the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site orientation, considered the submissions and late correspondence and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent) with the addition of new Condition Nos. B.12 & D.1 (c).


Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Panel’s Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, is satisfied that the written request from the applicant under Clause 4.6 of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 to the floor space ratio for dwelling house in Zone R2 development standard under Clause 4.4E of Woollahra LEP 2014 has adequately addressed the relevant matters and the proposed development will be in the public interest because it is consistent with the relevant objectives of the particular standard and the zone. 

AND 

That the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, grant development consent to Development Application No. 558/2024/1 for construction of new four car garage to the front yard, new swimming pool, minor alterations to the existing house and ancillary works including landscaping and new front fence on land at 1A New South Head Road Vaucluse, subject to the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site orientation, considered the submissions and late correspondence and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent), with the addition of Condition D.1(d) and (e).

  • The Panel was supportive of the four car garage on the basis that the existing garage could accommodate four cars, and this was being converted to non-habitable storage area.
  • Malcolm Young, the Community Representative, did not endorse the Panel’s determination to approve the application for the following two reasons.


 


  • The proposed four car garage is double the DCP maximum of two cars. The extra space taken up by the extra two cars could go some way towards meeting the 49% shortfall of deep soil landscaping. It would also better match with No. 3’s   landscaped front setback;
Given the proximity of the neighbour’s bedroom at No. 3, he did not support the proposed trafficable deck above the proposed garage structure. He noted that the house has ample balcony structures across two levels. He would have supported the DA were the garage reduced to a two car garage, set back towards the house with a non-trafficable roof above.


Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion


Penelope HollowayMalcolm Young
Lee Kosnetter
Larissa Ozog


3/1

(Councillor Torsten/Councillor Mitchell)

328/2024 Recommendation:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes the advice provided by the Woollahra Local Planning Panel from 3 April 2025 regarding the FSR Housekeeping planning proposal.
  1. Resolves to support the planning proposal as contained at Attachment 1 to make the following amendments to the Floor Space Ratio controls in the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014:
  1. Amend the FSR Map and Clause 4.4 to apply FSR controls to all development in the R2 Low Density Residential zone to replace the current floorplate controls in the Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015; noting these amendments will not apply to land in the Paddington, Watsons Bay and Woollahra Heritage Conservation Areas. 
  2. Insert subclause to Clause 4.4 to ensure FSR provisions do not apply to attached dwellings, dwelling houses, dual occupancies or semi-detached dwellings in the R3 Medium Density Residential zone within the Paddington, Watsons Bay and Woollahra Heritage Conservation Areas.
  1. Forwards the planning proposal to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure seeking a Gateway Determination to allow public exhibition. 

  2. Requests the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces (or delegate) authorise Council as the local plan-making authority to make the local environmental plan under section 3.36 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

  3. Receives the Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (Amendment No 36) as contained at Attachment 2 and resolves to exhibit this concurrently with the planning proposal, should a Gateway determination be received.

The Motion was put and Carried.

 

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

Note:    Lisa Trueman declared Significant Non-Pecuniary Interest in Item 4.1 (Planning 
             Proposal - Heritage Listing Modern Buildings Priority Study) as Lisa Trueman provided 
             advice to the owners of 132 Paddington Street, Paddington about the potential 
             listing.  Lisa Trueman did not take part in the site inspection, briefing session, 
             debate or vote on 132 Paddington Street, Paddington.

Note:    Late correspondence was tabled by Stephanie, Design Collaborative, Susan Bray,  
             Esther Hayter, The Paddington Society and Andrew Killen.

Note:    Paul Rappoport, David Rippingill, Rosemary Cunningham and 
             Andrew Killen, Objectors and Ruark Lewis and Esther Hayter, Supporter addressed 
             the Panel.

Reasons:

The Woollahra Local Planning Panel gave consideration to all submissions, including the late correspondence in the Council memorandum dated 8 May 2025 and the further submission from Mr Andrew Killen of 9 May 2025. 

The Woollahra Local Planning Panel advises Council that the Planning Proposal (as amended) has strategic and site-specific merit for the reasons outlined in Council officers’ report, and for the following reasons:

o    That the properties individually and collectively contribute to the understanding of the history
      and the heritage of the municipality, which should include representative examples from 
      each style-period, including Modern architecture, and significant architects.

 


o    That the detailed research and investigation carried out in preparing the report and 
      accompanying study, and analysis of issues raised during the assessment process, have 
      been robust, evidence-based and comprehensive.

o    That the pre-engagement with the affected parties has been well-considered and enhanced
       the assessment process. 

The Woollahra Local Planning Panel recommends that Council staff communicate, where relevant, the processes for undertaking works to buildings. This should include the types of maintenance and repair that can be undertaken without development consent to locally listed heritage items. 

The Woollahra Local Planning Panel encourages Council staff to continue to communicate with the owners of proposed heritage-listed buildings where internal access has not been provided.

The Woollahra Local Planning  notes that where the listing title excludes dwelling interiors, that the remainder of the building including common property, foyers, balconies, public and private exterior spaces, etc are included in the listing. 

Resolved:

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel advises Council to proceed with the Planning
Proposal (at Attachment 1) to list the following eighteen (18) places as local heritage items 
in Schedule 5 and on the associated Heritage Maps of the Woollahra Local Environmental

Panel’s Decision

That the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council as the consent authority, refuses to modify the development consent to DA510/2019 for alterations and additions to an existing dwelling house, new swimming pool and cabana on land at 16 Olphert Avenue Vaucluse, subject to the Attached (Adopted Reasons for Refusal).

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site visit, considered the submissions and late correspondence and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel has determined that the modification application be refused for the reasons set out below: 

  • The proposed increase to the height of the cabana structure and the modification to the height and species of landscaping would have an adverse impact on the adjoining property at 18 Olphert Avenue in terms of not achieving a satisfactory view sharing outcome.

Councillor Zeltzer: 

  • Queen Street Festival
  • Watsons Bay Library
Councillor Zeltzer had the pleasure of attending the opening of the Queen Street Festival, which was very well supported by attendees. Councillor Zeltzer commended the Mayor for her contributions at the Festival as well as Giles Edmunds and the Queen Street West Woollahra Association for putting together such a positive, popular event and leading a wonderful organisation. Woollahra Council staff Anne White and Justine Henderson were also commended for their tireless efforts in supporting the function. 

Councillor Zeltzer recognised the Watsons Bay Library staff for supplying a wide variety of activities and for being amenable and flexible to accommodate Councillor Zeltzer's visit. 


Councillor Jarvis:

  • Peter Poland OAM Memorial 
On 1 May 2025, Councillor Jarvis had the honour of attending the memorial for Peter Poland OAM. Peter was a founding member of the Woollahra History and Heritage Society and the memorial was a touching service for friends, family and the wider community to pay their respects. 

Councillor Jarvis also advised that she attended the 77th Birthday Celebrations for the State of Israel, which noted the support provided to the Jewish community since the October 7th attacks. 


Councillor Witt:

  • Peter Poland OAM Memorial 
On 1 May 2025, Councillor Witt had the honour of attending the memorial for Peter Poland OAM, and noted how moving the memorial was, which featured models of the buildings Peter had been instrumental in saving throughout his life. 


Councillor Torsten:

  • Citizenship Ceremony 
  • Allegra Spender MP Election Event
Last week Councillor Torsten attended a Citizenship Ceremony at Woollahra Council, alongside Councillors Mitchell, Silcocks, Andruska, Parmegiani, Woodgate and Mayor Swan, to welcome 61 new Australians. 

On 3 May 2025, Councillor Torsten attended Allegra Spender MP's election night event alongside Councillor Witt and Councillor Regan. 


Councillor Robertson:

  • Peter Poland OAM Memorial 
On 1 May 2025, Councillor Robertson had the honour of representing the Mayor at the memorial for Peter Poland OAM. Four former Woollahra Mayors, Geoffrey Rundle, Keri Huxley, John Comino and Christopher Dawson were in attendance, demonstrating the breadth of influence, altruism and determination Peter had. Councillor Silcocks also attended alongside Woollahra staff. 


Councillor Carmichael:

  • Peter Poland OAM Memorial 
  • Congratulations to Allegra Spender MP
On 1 May 2025, Councillor Carmichael was also in attendance at the memorial for Peter Poland OAM and recognised how dedicated Peter was as a passionate member of the community.

Councillor Carmichael congratulated Allegra Spender MP on her re-election and referenced having worked with her over several years on a number of local issues. Councillor Carmichael credited all other candidates and expressed his interest in continuing to work with the Member for Wentworth in the future. 


Councillor Andruska:

  • Youth Week Day Festival 
  • Citizenship Ceremony
Last week Councillor Andruska attended the Youth Week Day Festival and noted what an excellent day it was.

Councillor Andruska also attended the recent Woollahra Citizenship Ceremony and recognised that it was a incredible evening. 


Councillor Regan:

  • Acknowledged Staff Support at Bellevue Hill Ward Meeting 
  • Queen Street Association Congrats to Giles Edmunds
Councillor Regan thanked staff for their invaluable support at the recent Bellevue Hill Ward Council meeting. 

Councillor Regan offered her congratulations to Giles Edmunds and the Queen Street West Woollahra Association, and attended the Friday night walkaround shop event.


Councillor Woodgate:

  • SES Awards Night
  • NAJEX Anzac Day
On 2 April 2025, Councillor Woodgate represented the Mayor at the Woollahra/Waverley SES award night and was honoured to present two ten-year service awards to Richard Miller and Max Henderson. Awards were also received by Arkham Zaidi for the Paul McQueen Excellence in Leadership Award, Naomi Dinnen received the Spirt of Waverley Woollahra Award, Nathaniel Cox received the New Member Award and Colin McQueen received an acknowledgement award. 

On 4 May 2025, Councillor Woodgate attended the NAJEX Anzac Day event and wanted to offer his congratulations to Roger Selby (President - NAJEX) and his team for organising such a moving event every year. 

 
The Mayor, Councillor Swan:

  • Recognising Vince Caccavo (Woollahra Council Landscape Architect)
  • Bench installation in Double Bay 
  • Europe Day 
  • 84th Anniversary of the Battle of Crete 
  • St Vincent's Health Care Services in Albert St Edgecliff
  • Meet the Ward Councillor events
  • Citizenship Ceremony 
  • Bellevue Hill Public School Centenary Celebrations 
  • Vintage Fair
The Mayor recognised the contributions of Woollahra Council's brilliant Landscape Architect, Vince Caccavo who delivered results on a number of projects in a short time, having joined Council in 2021. Vince moves to a role in the State Government shortly and the Mayor wished him well in his new position.

The Mayor extended her thanks to Woollahra Council staff, particularly Director O'Hanlon, for attending the installation of benches in Kiaora Lane in Double Bay, which will enhance the amenity and allow people to freely enjoy the space created by Council. 

The Mayor advised that she celebrated Europe Day on Tuesday 6 May, at the invite of Consul General of the Republic of Poland, Mr Piotr Radowski. 

The Mayor attended the 84th Anniversary of the Battle of Crete on Saturday 17 May, at the invite of the Joint Committee for Commemoration of the Battle of Crete and the Greek Campaign. It was a moving ceremony and the Mayor was proud to represent the Woollahra community by laying a wreath. 

The Mayor further advised that on 19 May 2025 she had an enjoyable time meeting the residents and staff of St Vincent's Health Care Services in Albert St Edgecliff, and hearing about the important work they undertake. 
 
The Mayor offered thanks to the Executive Leadership Team for being part of the first two Meet the Ward Councillor events, which took place in the Bellevue Hill Ward on 29 April and Vaucluse Ward on 20 May, with another being held in the Double Bay Ward on 27 May, and the last two scheduled on 17 June in Paddington and 22 July at Cooper Ward. 

On 22nd May the Mayor had the pleasure of welcoming new Australians at a Citizenship Ceremony. The Mayor extended her thanks to the Member for Wentworth and Member for Vaucluse for attending, in addition to Councillors Silcocks, Mitchell, Andruska, Parmegiani and Torsten. 

The Mayor was incredibly pleased to attend Bellevue Hill Public School on Sunday 25 May to celebrate 100 years of their operation. The Principal, Ms Sue Bennett, and the wider school put together an excellent event for the community and the Mayor recognised the extraordinary achievement of Ms Bennett celebrating 25 years in the role. 

Lastly, the Mayor thoroughly enjoyed attending the Vintage Fair organised by St Michaels at the previous weekend.


(Councillor Swan/Councillor Carmichael)

279/2025 Resolved without debate:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes the advice provided by the Woollahra Local Planning Panel from 3 April 2025 regarding the FSR Housekeeping planning proposal.

  2. Resolves to support the planning proposal as contained at Attachment 1 to make the following amendments to the Floor Space Ratio controls in the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014:
  1. Amend the FSR Map and Clause 4.4 to apply FSR controls to all development in the R2 Low Density Residential zone to replace the current floorplate controls in the Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015; noting these amendments will not apply to land in the Paddington, Watsons Bay and Woollahra Heritage Conservation Areas.
  2. Insert subclause to Clause 4.4 to ensure FSR provisions do not apply to attached dwellings, dwelling houses, dual occupancies or semi-detached dwellings in the R3 Medium Density Residential zone within the Paddington, Watsons Bay and Woollahra Heritage Conservation Areas.
  1. Forwards the planning proposal to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure seeking a Gateway Determination to allow public exhibition.

  2. Requests the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces (or delegate) authorise Council as the local plan-making authority to make the local environmental plan under section 3.36 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

  3. Receives the Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (Amendment No 36) as contained at Attachment 2 and resolves to exhibit this concurrently with the planning proposal, should a Gateway determination be received.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Price, Councillor Robertson, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Swan, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Zeltzer, Councillor Regan

266/2025 Resolved:

Note:Late correspondence was tabled by Esther Hayter (The Paddington Society), Paul Menzies, Dr Peter Arnold OAM, Tony Bond (Edgecliff Residents Group) and Will Naughton. 

Note:Councillor Zeltzer declared a Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in this item as Councillor Zeltzer is one of Council's representatives on the Sydney Eastern City Planning Panel. Councillor Zeltzer left the meeting at this item, did not participate in debate and did not vote on the matter.

Note:Councillor Robertson declared a Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in this item as Councillor Robertson is one of Council's representatives on the Sydney Eastern City Planning Panel. Councillor Robertson left the meeting at this item, did not participate in debate and did not vote on the matter.

Note:Councillor Jarvis declared a Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in Item 14.6 as Councillor Jarvis is one of Council's representatives on the Sydney Eastern City Planning Panel. Councillor Jarvis left the meeting at this item, did not participate in debate and did not vote on the matter.


Note:Part F and Part G of the Resolution were amended ahead of the vote. 

(Councillor Witt/Councillor Carmichael)

267/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes the significant number of State Significant Developments Applications (SSDAs) in our Local Government Area (LGA) currently in the process of being lodged with, or assessed by, the Department of Planning Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI).

  2. Recognises that most Woollahra Council residents are not familiar with the approval pathway for SSDAs, and would not be aware of recent amendments to the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 2017 (EP&A Act) that:
  1. Allow for a possible reduction in the minimum public exhibition period for State significant development related to residential housing from 28 days to 14 days.
  2. State that only submissions received during public exhibition periods will be counted for determining consent and appeal right purposes, although late submissions will still be considered in assessments.
  1. Requests the General Manager:
  1. To publish information about the SSDAs on the Council's website with links to supporting documentation on the NSW Planning Portal and also links to any other Council reports and/or submissions that could be helpful for residents planning to make a submission.
  2. Write to the DPHI to request that residents be notified of exhibition dates for SSDAs via mail and by notification in the local newspaper.
  1. With respect to the SSDA for 136-148 New South Head Road Edgecliff, requests the General Manager to write to the DPHI and to the developer Lendlease to explain that:
  1. Feedback from surrounding residents and the relevant residents associations suggests that they weren't notified of the exhibition period.
  2. The exhibition period deadline was not clearly stated on the NSW Planning Portal.
  3. The Communications Consultation Report, prepared for the developer, says that the relevant residents associations were contacted on 11 October 2024. But the residents groups have reported that they did not receive any correspondence from the Consultant and, as a consequence, did not take up the offer for further consultations or a dedicated briefing on the SSDA.
  4. The Communications Consultant also didn’t follow-up on a “forthcoming” offer for a group Councillor briefing in early 2025.
  5. The approved Voluntary Planning Agreement (VPA), entered into with the previous owner for this site, must be revised to reflect the impact on Council’s infrastructure and services from the SSDA’s proposed increase in the site-specific height and FSR controls as articulated in Section 6.11 of the Woollahra Local Environment Plan 2014. The SSDA is proposing a 40% increase to the number of dwellings originally envisaged for this site.
  1. Requests that in light of consideration of the above, the General Manager asks for DPHI to consider re-exhibiting the SSDA for 136-148 New South Head Road Edgecliff.

  2. Should DPHI not agree to re-exhibiting the SSDA for 136-148 New South Head Road Edgecliff, then the General Manager seek legal advice on the prospects of challenging the matter by class 4 action. 

  3. Requests the General Manager advise the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces, the Hon Paul Scully MP, and the Secretary of DPHI, Kiersten Fishburn in relation to concerns with regards to staging of construction of SSDAs in Edgecliff.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Price, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Swan, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Regan
None

269/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes Lazard’s Levilised Cost of Energy (LCOE) report (June 2024) and the CSIRO’s GenCost 2024-25 conclusively demonstrates that solar and battery storage is the cheapest and most efficient form of energy production.

  2. Requests the General Manager prepare a report to the Finance, Community & Services Committee at a later date, recommending strategies to:
  1. work with capital and/or development partners to facilitate the construction of community batteries (CBESS) and provide a virtual battery scheme to residents (provided that the impact of installation on green spaces are minimised);
  2. partner with other councils to fund the development of a grid-scale battery;
  3. any other recommendations to incentive further take-up of rooftop solar and battery storage by both private dwellings and commercial premises.
  4. setting parameters on where community batteries will be located and how they present to the streetscape and surrounds.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
Councillor Carmichael declared a Non-Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in this item as Councillor Carmichael is a current member of the Royal Sydney Golf Club. Councillor Carmichael indicated that, as the matter is not a substantive issue he would remain the meeting during this item.

Councillors Woodgate, Robertson, Regan & Zeltzer asking:


On 24 February 2025 Council passed a Notice of Motion (14.1) as put forward by Cr Zeltzer and Cr Robertson. Noting that the 60-day timeframe has passed:

  1. Can staff please provide an update on this matter?

  2. What steps are being taken to remove the fence from council land?

  3. Have we sought legal advice on this matter, if so, what is Councils position?

  4. When can we expect an outcome on this matter?


Director Infrastructure & Sustainability in Response:

The consultant designer of the O'Sullivan Road pathway project has amended the concept design at the corner intersection to take advantage of part of the land proposed to be reacquired from Royal Sydney Golf Course (RSGC). In doing so, he notes the following;

The extent to which the pathway can be widened is constrained by the topography and significant vegetation characteristic of the land currently within the RSGC fence. Filling over the embankment to achieve falls suitable for a shared user path would be incompatible with the existing vegetation.  

The existing fence provides de facto edge protection to the path by shielding path users from the steep terrain and trees. Reacquisition of all land by relocating the fence to the property boundary would result in these hazards being unshielded unless additional barrier fencing were provided at the path edge. The required barrier fencing would make the land beyond generally inaccessible. 

The upshot of this is that the revised design will widen the pathway by 0.5m - 1m, with a barrier installed by Council at the top of the embankment.  It is noted that the additional 0.5 - 1m does provide a material improvement to the design. 

More broadly, Council staff are liaising with RSGC with a view to addressing the considerable logistical difficulties associated with moving the RSGC fence to the property line.

On-site assessment from within the golf course has demonstrated that moving the fence to the actual property boundary could only be achieved with very considerable impact on vegetation, including a number of large trees.  Council staff intend to continue working with RSGC with a view to achieving a mutually agreeable outcome which minimises vegetation impact. 

 

No legal advice has been sought on the matter as, to date, there has been no dispute raised by RSGC. As stated, all discussion has been around logistics and vegetation management. 

It is proposed that a site meeting will be arranged for interested Councillors at which staff will further illustrate the logistical issues outlined above.

THAT Council:

  6. Undertake a community education campaign as to how our community can help improve outcomes for those experiencing homelessness, including a better understanding of Councils Homelessness policies and procedures through the following types of activities: social media campaigns; print media and correspondence to community and resident groups.

Sends a copy of the correspondence from the Mayor to: Kellie Sloan Member for Vaucluse, Marjorie O’Neill Member for Coogee, Alexander Greenwich Member for Sydney and Rose Jackson Minister for Water, Minister for Housing, Minister for Homelessness, Minister for Mental Health, Minister for Youth and Minister for the North Coast to inform them of our actions and inviting them to engage with the education campaign.

  1. Resolves as a priority to seek Public Private Partnership (PPP) Expressions of Interest (EOIs) for the Wilberforce car park site in Rose Bay that include, at a minimum:

Panel’s Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council as the consent authority, is satisfied that the matters required to be addressed under Clause 4.6(3) of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 have been demonstrated and that consent may be granted to the development application, which contravenes the Floor Space Ratio development standard under Clause 4.4 of Woollahra LEP 2014.

AND

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, grant development consent to Development Application No. 2/2025/1 for alterations and additions to the existing semi-detached house, including substantial demolition of the existing structure and construction of a new two storey dwelling with rear garage on land at 45 Fletcher Street WOOLLAHRA, subject to the recommended conditions in Attachment 2.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site orientation, considered the submissions and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. 

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

Panel’s Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council as the consent authority, is satisfied that the matters required to be addressed under Clause 4.6(3) of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 have been demonstrated and that consent may be granted to the development application, which contravenes the minimum lot size and Floor Space Ratio development standards under Clause 4.1A and 4.3 of Woollahra LEP 2014.

 



AND

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, grant development consent to DA452/2024/1 for demolition of existing residential flat building and construction of a new multi-dwelling housing development for three dwellings and strata subdivision on land at 55 William Street DOUBLE BAY, subject to the Attached (Adopted Conditions of Consent)

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site orientation, considered the submissions and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. 

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).


Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, grant development consent to Development Application No. 100/2025/1 for change of use to a tattoo studio on land at 64 William Street Paddington, subject to the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent)

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Parmegiani 

  • Fanny Redding plaque 
Councillor Parmegiani was honoured to attend the plaque unveiling for Fanny Redding, who founded the Council of Jewish Women of NSW which then became the National Council of Jewish Women, and tirelessly devoted herself to the local and international community. 

Councillor Zeltzer 

  • Indigenous artwork unveiling 
Councillor Zeltzer joined the Mayor in the unveiling of the first indigenous piece of artwork at Steyne Park.
Councillor Mitchell

  • Indigenous artwork unveiling 
Councillor Mitchell also joined the Mayor and Councillor Zeltzer in the unveiling of the first indigenous piece of artwork at Steyne Park.

Councillor Torsten

  • Indigenous artwork unveiling 
Councillor Torsten commended the wonderful artist and staff who supported the unveiling of the artwork at Steyne Park.

Councillor Price

  • Screening of film Her Name is Nanny Nellie
Councillor Price had the honour of representing the Mayor at the screening of Daniel King's documentary film Her Name is Nanny Nellie. The film concerns the 1925 Australian Museum unveiling sculptures depicting Aboriginal people, one of which was of an Aboriginal woman, who for many years was held in the public gaze, stripped of her identity. The film traces how her living descendants worked with the Museum to reclaim her story.

 

Councillor Andruska 

  • Indigenous artwork unveiling 
  • Spring Street Playground
Councillor Andruska also attended the unveiling of the first indigenous piece of artwork at Steyne Park.

Councillor Andruska joined the Mayor, Councillor Robertson and Councillor Price at the opening of the Spring Street Playground.
Councillor Carmichael 

  • Parliamentary Inquiry into Antisemitism 
Councillor Carmichael was honoured to represent the Mayor and Woollahra at the recent Parliamentary Inquiry into Antisemitism.
Councillor Robertson 

  • Indigenous artwork unveiling 
Councillor Robertson also attended the unveiling of the first indigenous piece of artwork at Steyne Park and found the event extremely moving. Councillor Robertson offered particular thanks to Councillor Zeltzer for her work in overseeing the event.

Mayor Swan

  • Community Forum 
  • Social Cohesion Forum 
The Mayor thanked Kellie Sloane, Member for Vaucluse, for organising a well attended community forum on 11th June, in addition to Woollahra Council staff Scott Pedder, Director Planning & Place, Craig Swift-McNair, General Manager and Anne White, Manager for Strategic Planning & Place for supporting the event. 

The Mayor thanked Woollahra staff Patricia Occelli, Director Community & Customer Experience and Vicki Munro, Manager for Community and Culture, for their support in organising the follow up social cohesion forum, held jointly with Randwick and Waverley Councils. The Mayor noted that for the most part, the community feels a strong sense of place and connection to the geography as well as to each other. 

The Mayor encouraged Councillors to reach out to the owner of the news agency on Queens Street, who unfortunately was subject to a recent robbery and assault. The Mayor extended her condolences and thanked the NSW Police for their efforts in apprehending the perpetrators of this case, as well as recent break-ins from the previous weekend in the locality. 

The Mayor thanked all Councillors who represented her at events over the past month. 

The Mayor attended Cranbrook School to encourage them to get behind the Push Up Challenge on 4th June. 

The Mayor noted it was a pleasure to attend the International Women's Day art auction.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Regan asking: 

I refer to my question with notice in item 17.2 of the Council meeting held on 11 June 2024 and my question with notice in item 15.1 of the Council meeting held on 16 December 2024 and thank council staff for their responses. 

Could Council please provide a further update on the matter specifically: 

  1. On the timing for production of a report on the ability of Council to use the Park n Pay application or similar in the municipality including in relation to unmetered, timed parking spots. 
  2. On what communications have been had with neighbouring councils, SSROC and the State Government on the Park n Pay app and the outcome of those communications.
  3. Whether the State Government has provided any update in relation to the Park n Pay app and its ongoing use. 

Manager Engineering Services in Response: 

Council staff are continuing their investigations on the types of smart parking systems in which the public may use to pay for on-street parking. A report was anticipated to Council in the fourth quarter of this financial year, however this was subject to further information provided by the Department of Customer Service on whether the Park’n’Pay application will continue to be served in the next financial year. 

Over the past couple of years, various local councils and the Department of Customer Service participated in roundtable sessions and the Department has now requested feedback from local councils through a questionnaire survey to help better understand council priorities, technical challenges, and commercial considerations. 

 


The Department have advised that this survey is separate from any previous consultations and is designed to inform future improvements to the Park’n’Pay platform based on current council needs and experiences. This survey was released late May 2025, asking Council staff for feedback. 

Following the conclusion of this survey and feedback from the Department of Customer Service on their position to whether they will continue to provide this service, Council’s Engineers will prepare a report collating all the information for consideration.

364/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:

1. Notes:
 
  1. The Vision of its ‘Oxford Street and Paddington Place Plan’, including a range of ‘placemaking pillars' to create:
  •  'An animated heritage streetscape as a backdrop to memorable village offerings with activity flowing onto the footpath’; and 
  • ‘An inviting and welcoming place offering unique experiences complemented by intimate settings that awaken the senses'.



  1. Chapter C1 of the Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (WDCP) and in particular, Paddington’s desired future character and vision statement recognising Paddington’s ‘unique national heritage significance’ and its importance as a ‘rare and distinctive area’.

  2. The provisions of the WDCP concerning exterior building colours in the Paddington Heritage Conservation Area (HCA), including that:
  • Colour Schemes must be appropriate to the building type and styles’ (C1.5.9 (C1)); and
  • The intensity and hue of colour must relate to the style of the building and the streetscape context‘ (C1.5.9(C4)).
  1. There are many internationally renowned areas (such as Notting Hill in London, Nyhavn in Copenhagen and Alamo Square in San Francisco) that have integrated vibrant colour schemes into heritage settings and contributed to local identity, tourism and a sense of place.
 
2. Requests the General Manager prepares a report considering the appropriateness (or otherwise) of permitting a more diverse colour palette in the Paddington HCA including, but not limited to, investigating options for the preparation of guidelines for colour schemes in the Paddington business precincts.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

353/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes the feedback on the Woollahra Domestic and Family Violence Accommodation and Support Program delivered under the Women's Housing Company funding agreement, 2022-2025 as outlined in the Woollahra Domestic and Family Violence Accommodation and Support Program Summary, July 2022 - June 2025.

  2. Endorse the continuation of the Woollahra Domestic and Family Violence Accommodation and Support Program through a new three-year agreement with the Women’s Housing Company, from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2028.

  3. Approve funding of $338,580 to the Women's Housing Company from the 2025-2026 draft budget, noting that unspent funds from prior years will be utilised prior to any drawdown from the 2025-2026 budget.




  4. Determine future funding for Women's Housing Company for 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 on an annual basis with the proposed budget provided to Council by the Women's Housing Company, through an annual report on the Woollahra Domestic and Family Violence Accommodation and Support Program by 31 October each year, providing 6 months written notice of the upcoming proposed Funding Agreement Schedule for the following financial year, for the consideration of Council.

  5. Note that a Councillor Workshop will be held during the first quarter of 2025-2026 to discuss the most appropriate use of the potential saving of up to $265,306 to Council's budget in the 2025-2026 year.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

The Mayor, Councillor Swan, disclosed a Non-Significant, Non-Pecuniary interest in relation to item 12.3.2, as the Mayor was previously a Director of Holdsworth Community. The Mayor remained in the meeting, participated in debate and voted on the matter.

(Councillor Carmichael/Councillor Andruska)

352/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council: 


  1. Notes the feedback on the five programs delivered under the Holdsworth Community funding agreement, 2022-2025 as outlined in the WMC and Holdsworth Three Year Program Evaluation FY23-25.

 

  1. Endorses the proposed new 3-year Agreement with Holdsworth Community for the period 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2028, with total funding proposed of $621,095.90 for first year of the agreement for the 2025-2026 budget as follows:

 

  1. Woollahra Connect! $172,609.40  
  2. Woollahra Playgroup Program $191,690.23  
  3. Woollahra Life! $185,101.20  
  4. Dementia Friendly Woollahra $71,695.07

 


  1. Notes that the newly established program Woollahra Life! will be evaluated after the first year of operation to determine future funding within the 2026-1027 and 2027-2028 financial years.

  2. Determine future funding for Holdsworth Community for 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 on an annual basis with the proposed budget reported to Council with the Holdsworth Community’s annual report and program evaluation by 31 October each year, providing 6 months written notice of the upcoming proposed Funding Agreement Schedule for the consideration of Council.

  3. Notes that a Councillor Workshop will be held during the first quarter of 2025-2026 to discuss the most appropriate use of the remaining budget of $344,252.10 for the 2025-2026 year. 


The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

Note:
Part B of the resolution was amended and Part D added to the resolution ahead of the vote.

(Councillor Zeltzer/Councillor Carmichael) 

Resolved: 

THAT Council, in accordance with clause 14.1(g) of the Code of Meeting Practice, resolve to enter into Closed Session with the press and public excluded to consider Confidential Attachment. These matters are to be considered as per clause 10A(2)(g) of the Local Government Act 1993 as it concerns litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege.

Adopted
In Closed Session

Note:The Council discussed the confidential matter. 

(Councillor Swan/Councillor Carmichael)

THAT Council move into Open Session. 

Adopted
In Open Session 

(Councillor Swan/Councillor Carmichael)

346/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:
 
  1. Note the correspondence received from the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces on 25 August 2024 and 7 May 2025 relating to the Low and Mid-Rise Housing Policy.
  1. Resolves that subject to feedback from the NSW Government that it may consider alternatives to the Low and Mid-Rise Housing Policy, request staff to prepare an alternative housing scheme which includes Rose Bay and Double Bay to facilitate housing growth but does this in a sustainable and strategic way that addresses the key issues associated with the current Low and Mid-Rise Housing Policy. 

  2. Requests the General Manager to arrange a meeting between the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces and the Mayor.

  3. Requests the General Manager seek legal advice, following discussions with Ku-ring-gai Council regarding their current legal challenge with the State Government in relation to planning reforms.

The Motion was put and Carried.

 

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Price, Councillor Robertson, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Swan, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Zeltzer, Councillor Regan

Panel’s Decision

 

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council as the consent authority, is satisfied that the matters required to be addressed under Clause 4.6(3) of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 have been demonstrated and that consent may be granted to the development application, which contravenes the Floor Space Ratio (FSR) development standard under Clause 4.4 of Woollahra LEP 2014.

 

AND 

 

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, grant development consent to Development Application No. 150/2025/1 for the substantial demolition of the existing dwelling and construction of a new dwelling and associated landscaping on land at 9 Small Street WOOLLAHRA, subject to the Adopted Conditions of Consent.

 

Reasons for Decision

 

The Panel has undertaken a site orientation and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

 

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

 



Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

Panel’s Decision

 

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, refuse to modify development consent to DA 478/2023/1 for the demolition of existing dwelling and associated structures and the construction of a new multi-storey dwelling with basement garage; new swimming pool, landscaping and siteworks on land at 4 Graylind Place VAUCLUSE (Lot C in DP 371950, and Lot 101 in DP 1263986), for the following reason:

 

  • The development to which the consent, as sought to be modified, is not the same or substantially the same development as the development for which consent was originally granted within the meaning of s4.55(2) of the EP&A Act 1979 due to the:

 

  • Qualitative differences between the proposed modified development against the approved originally approved development.
  • Consequences such as the environmental impacts, namely view affectation, of carrying out the proposed modified development compared to the original approved development.

 

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

Panel’s Decision

 

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, is satisfied that the applicant has demonstrated under Clause 4.6 of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 that compliance with the height of buildings and floor space ratio development standards under Clause 4.3 and 4.4E  of Woollahra LEP 2014 is unreasonable or unnecessary in the circumstances, and there are sufficient environmental planning grounds to justify the contraventions of the development standards.

 

AND 

 

 


THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, grant development consent to Development Application No. 320/2024/1 for modifications to the alterations and additions approved under a Complying Development Certificate to the existing dwelling; as well as external landscaping and siteworks on land at 4 Black Street Vaucluse, subject to the Adopted Conditions of Consent.

 

Reasons for Decision

 

The Panel has undertaken a site orientation, considered the submissions, late correspondence and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

 

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the deletion of recommended Condition A.5 b) (Transplanting of palms) which corrects a discrepancy and with the Conditions as set out in the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).


For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

366/2025 Resolved:

  1. On key sites identified on the Key Sites map to the WLEP 2014
  2. For regionally significant DAs with a capital value greater than $30m, and

  1. For the reasons set out in the report, does not proceed with the constitution of a design review panel under the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulations 2021.

  1. Resolves to establish Woollahra Site Specific Design Review Panels from a pool of external design consultants with a range of specialist skills and expertise, which may include the following:
  1. Urban Design
  2. Apartment Design Guide (ADG)
  3. Public domain/commercial centre
  4. Landscaping
  5. Heritage
  6. Sustainability
  7. Architecture
  8. Design excellence

  1. Requests the General Manager to bring a report back to Council in December 2026 updating Council on the operation of the Woollahra Design Review Panel, subject to there having been meetings held during this period

368/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Receive and note the report on compliance with the Housing SEPP in respect of independent living unit requirements for Seniors Housing whiting the Woollahra LGA.

  2. Undertake the actions specified in the report including:
  1. The creation of a new entry in Council’s record system incorporating a register in readiness for the submission of future positive covenants for development in accordance with the condition of consent, such register to contain information regarding the location, type and number of independent living units within the development;
  2. Maintaining all certified copies of the restrictive covenants in such developments once issued; 
  3. To ensure that all development consents for such development are notified to the Strategic Planning and Place team so that this information is incorporated into the relevant property attributes to ensure that any planning certificates advise of the seniors housing conditions
  4. Requesting yearly verification statements from the site manager or strata manager of the development confirming compliance with the senior housing occupation requirements and add this information to the Legal Register report to a meeting of Council the following year; and
  5. To undertake such action as Council deems appropriate regarding non complying properties subsequent to the yearly compliance check referred to above.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Note:Sharon Veale declared a Significant Non-Pecuniary Interest in this Item as the report for this Item was authored by Lisa Trueman and Leonie Masson. Both of whom are known to her. Lisa Trueman is a former GML staff member, and Leonie Masson is a current GML staff member. Sharon Veale did not take part in the site inspection, briefing session, debate or vote on the matter.

Note:Late correspondence was tabled by Esther Hayter.

 


Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel

 

  1. Advises Council to proceed with the Planning Proposal (at Attachment 1 of the Report) to list the following five (5) buildings (two (2) individual buildings and one (1) group item comprising three (3) properties) as local heritage items in Schedule 5 and on the associated Heritage Maps of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014: 

 

  1. “Centennial Flats – residential flat building, including interiors” at 2A Queen Street Woollahra (Lot 4, Lot 5, Lot 6, DP 15117)
  2. “Former gymnasium, restaurant and nightclub” at 60-80 Oxford Street Woollahra (previously known as 78-80 Oxford Street), (part of Lot 103, DP 1290591) 
  3. “Victorian Rustic Gothic Terraces heritage item group” (see also 84 and 86 Oxford Street, Woollahra) at 82 Oxford Street Woollahra (Lot 11, DP 598783) 
  4. “Victorian Rustic Gothic Terraces heritage item group ” (see also 82 and 86 Oxford Street, Woollahra) at 84 Oxford Street Woollahra (Lot 2, DP 225838) 
  5. “Victorian Rustic Gothic Terraces heritage item group ” (see also 82 and 84 Oxford Street, Woollahra) at 86 Oxford Street Woollahra (Lot 3, DP 225838)

 

  1. Notes the following two recommendations included in the Oxford Street properties and Centennial Flats heritage assessment prepared by Lisa Truman, that Council may wish to consider:

 

  1. Should Council undertake a future study of the LGBTQIA+ significance of Woollahra, the social significance of the former Gymnasium, Restaurant and Nightclub at 60-80 Oxford Street Woollahra, should be included in the study to determine if it holds social significance for the LGBTQIA+ community of NSW.
  2. The developer/owner of 60-80 Oxford Street Woollahra should be encouraged to name the building after its previous names rather than ‘Ox House’, in order to identify the history and significance of the building.

 

Reasons

The Woollahra LPP advises Council that the Planning Proposal has strategic and site-specific merit, for the reasons outlined in the Council report.  The Panel supports:

 

  • The elevation from contributory item to a heritage item for the buildings listed in the recommendation.
  • The assessment prepared by Lisa Trueman and Council Staff is a thorough assessment of all the properties included in the study areas

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion


Nicola GrieveNil
Megan Jones
David Ryan


3/0

Panel’s Decision

 

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, grant development consent to Development Application No. 102/2025/1 for substantial demolition of existing structure and construction of a new two storey dwelling including a garage on land at 1 Brittania Lane Woollahra, subject to the Adopted Conditions of Consent as amended.

 

Reasons for Decision

 

The Panel has undertaken a site orientation, considered submissions and late correspondence and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

 

The Panel considered the various matters raised by the objectors which primarily related to visual bulk, privacy, solar access, character and public interest.  The Panel considered that these matters have been adequately addressed in Council's assessment report and by the conditions of consent as amended.


For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to Conditions as set out in the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent) with the modification of Condition D.1 J. (Balcony/Windows Privacy Measures) and the deletion of D.1 K. (Roof Parapet to Balcony Design).

 
Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion


Nicola GrieveNil
Megan Jones
David Ryan
Sharon Veale

Panel’s Decision
 
THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council as the consent authority, is satisfied that the matters required to be addressed under Clause 4.6(3) of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 have been demonstrated and that consent may be granted to the development application, which contravenes the Floor Space Ratio development standard under Clause 4.4 of Woollahra LEP 2014. 
 
AND
 
THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, grant development consent to Development Application No.174/2025/1 for alterations and additions to the existing dwelling including a new garage and a new first floor to the rear on land at 22 Saber Street Woollahra, subject to the Adopted Conditions of Consent.
 
Reasons for Decision
 
The Panel has undertaken a site orientation and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  
 

 


For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in the Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent). 
 
Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

Tabled by: Councillor Witt

The petition was in terms:

We, the undersigned residents, community members, and visitors to Watsons Bay, urgently request comprehensive safety improvements at the roundabout at the intersection of Old South Head Road and Robertson Place to address three critical safety concerns affecting our community.

We request:
  • Installation of a properly engineered steel-reinforced concrete barrier or a more substantial safety barrier system that meets current road safety standards.
  • Implementation of traffic calming measures on all approaches to substantially reduce vehicle speeds before reaching the roundabout.
  • Installation of surveillance cameras and noise-capturing technology to identify and penalise offenders.
  • Additional traffic calming measures specifically designed to prevent the speeds and manoeuvres associated with antisocial driving.
  • Implementation end enforcement of a strict No U-Turn" policy for vehicles exceeding a specified length.
There are 94 signatures on the petition.

(Councillor Witt)
