Nicola Grieve declared a Non-Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in this item, as Nicola Grieve knew the late Angela Isles and family, as she was a friend of Nicola Grieve’s aunt. Nicola Grieve remained in the meeting, participated in debate and voted on the matter.

Community Representative, Nicola Grieve declared a further Non-Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in this item, as Nicola Grieve previously served on Council with Mayor Sarah Dixson. Nicola Grieve remained in the meeting, participated in debate and voted on the matter.

Note: 
Late correspondence was tabled by Bob Chambers (BBC Planning), Gabrielle Coltrona, and Jennis Askin (aSquare Planning).

Note: 
Jennie Askin (aSquare Planning), John Aspinall (Urbaine), Anthony Boskovitz (Boskovitz Lawyers), Robert Chambers (BBC Planners), Rohan Dickson (AEDesign Studio), Polly Harbison (Polly Harbison Design), Andrew Isles, and Councillor Hugh Woodgate addressed the Panel.

 

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, modify development consent to DA275/2024/1 for demolition of existing structures and construction of a new dwelling house with garage, new swimming pool and landscaping works on land at 24A Drumalbyn Road BELLEVUE HILL, subject to the recommended conditions of consent in Attachment 2.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel considered the late correspondence submitted by the Applicant, specifically relating to the rewording of Condition D.1(d). The Panel accepted the Applicant's submission on the grounds that the modification plans had already lowered the building by 400mm and hence the Condition required updating to respond to the Section 4.55 architectural drawings, whilst maintaining the approved RL of 54.90 AHD. Additionally the Panel also modified Condition D.1(d) to allow for the lowering of the basement floor level due to the omission of this possibility from the condition as originally imposed. 

The Panel considered the proposed removal of the Jacaranda Tree T39 and the majority of the Panel was satisfied that this removal was acceptable in order to facilitate the construction of the boundary retaining wall to provide light and amenity for the rear of the proposed dwelling. The Panel was satisfied that the submitted survey plan clearly indicated that Tree T39 was located within the subject development site. 

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

Community Representative, Nicola Grieve, did not support the modification application only due to the removal of the Jacaranda Tree T39. 

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion


Penny HollowayNicola Grieve
Peter Brennan
Megan Jones


3/1

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, is satisfied that the applicant has demonstrated under Part 4.6 of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 that compliance with the exceptions to floor space ratio dwelling houses, dual occupancies and semi-detached dwellings in Zones R2 and R3 development standard under Clause 4.4E of Woollahra LEP 2014 is unreasonable or unnecessary in the circumstances, and there are sufficient environmental planning grounds to justify the contravention of the development standard.

AND
 
THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, grant development consent to Development Application No. 270/2025/1 for extensive alterations and additions to the existing building including a new two storey rear wing subterranean plant room, a new carport and associated driveway and associated landscaping works on land at 12 Darling Point Road DARLING POINT, subject to the recommended conditions in Attachment 2.

 

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel imposed an additional condition D.1(h) which required all reference to the proposed bamboo landscaping being deleted and substituted with an alternative screen planting.

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, is satisfied that the matters required to be addressed under Clause 4.6(4) of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 have been adequately demonstrated and that consent may be granted to the development application, which contravenes the floor space ratio development standard prescribed under Clause 4.4E of Woollahra LEP 2014.

AND

That the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, grant development consent to DA140/2025/1 for construction of a two storey single car garage to the front yard, with gym below, driveway reconfiguration and ancillary works on land at 12A The Crescent (the subject site), subject to the conditions in Attachment 2.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

In reviewing the late correspondence which specifically related to "Swept Paths", the Panel was satisfied that vehicular access to the proposed carport achieved compliance with Australian Standards. In this regard, the Panel deleted condition D.1(a).

 

Additionally, the Panel imposed an additional condition, requiring an amended landscape plan to be submitted and approved by Council which deletes the two proposed trees in the vicinity of the proposed carport adjacent to the right of way.

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

Tabled by: The Mayor, Councillor Dixson

The petition was in terms:

We, the undersigned residents of Woollahra Council in accordance with Clause 22 of the Woollahra Council Code of Meeting Practice, petition the Woollahra Council to amend the Changes to Dog Controls at Kutti Beach as approved by Woollahra Council on 27 October 2025.

Proposal:

We propose a variation to the Dog Controls at Kutti Beach as follows:

Proposal 1 (preferred): Kutti Beach to be a designated off-leash area at all times, as per Woollahra Council’s original proposal as at page 2 and 9 of the Finance, Community & Services Committee Agenda 13 October 2025.

Council initially proposed to change the restrictions at Kutti Beach to off-leash at all times. We urge the Council to reconsider their change of heart, and revert to their original position on Kutti Beach.

This Proposal was by far the most popular request received from the community, and is therefore the most representative of community wishes. As above, Kutti Beach is a fully enclosed beach, making it an ideal off-leash location for dogs to enjoy. Dogs owners in our community are largely responsible, and of course the normal regulations governing dog-ownership apply: ensuring proper control over your dog, cleaning up after your dog, and disposing of waste thoughtfully.

We are in favour of rangers enforcing the existing rules of dog-ownership, and any community member doing the wrong thing should be advised so. We may suggest that an additional waste bin placed at Kutti Beach may benefit the community on busy days, where the one supplied bin may become full. Further, additional signage placed at the entrance to Kutti Beach reminding out-of-area patrons of the expectations of the community and Council may benefit all in maintaining a safe and hygienic environment.

We urge the Council not to punish the majority of community members who are responsible dog owners, and cherish this small space where our dogs can swim, based on the actions of a few irresponsible individuals whose actions can be regulated through existing dog-control regulations.

If the Council is not with us on Proposal 1, we propose a variation to the Dog Controls at Kutti Beach as follows:

Proposal 2: Kutti Beach to be a designated off-leash area between the hours of 3:30pm and 10:30am, AND an on-leash area between 10:30am and 3:30pm.

This will ensure that Woollahra Council is able to balance the safety concerns of families, who are most likely to visit the beach during the busiest period of the day (10:30am to 3:30pm); as dogs will be required to be on-leash during this time.

Further, this Proposal will still allow for dogs and their owners to enjoy the beach off-leash in the mornings and afternoons, when the beach is likely to be less busy.

This Proposal considers the enforcement challenges faced by rangers, as rangers will be easily able to patrol the beach with clear designation of hours in which dogs are allowed to be off-leash.

The same designation of hours (off-leash between 10:30am and 3:30pm) at other Council managed sites (including Rushcutters Bay Park, Lyne Park, and Christison Park) have showed great success in balancing the needs of families with those of dogs and their owners. Dogs and owners are respectful of the shared hours, allowing the community to share the space successfully.

 

This will also go to addressing the increased popularity of Kutti Beach as a result of social media and the increased number of out-of-area visitors to the beach. Those wishing to travel to the beach with their dogs will be required to adhere to the shared hours.

If the Council is not with us on Proposals 1 or 2, we propose a variation to the Dog Controls at Kutti Beach as follows:

Proposal 3: Kutti Beach to be a designated off-leash area Monday to Friday, AND between the hours of 3:30pm and 10:30am on weekends. Dogs will be prohibited between 10:30am and 3:30pm on weekends.

This will allow for families to visit the beach on the most popular days (weekends) during the busiest period of the day (10:30am to 3:30pm) without the presence of dogs; while still allowing dogs and their owners to enjoy the beach on weekend mornings and afternoons, and during the week.

This Proposal considers the enforcement challenges faced by rangers, as rangers will be easily able to patrol the beach with clear designation of days and hours in which dogs are allowed.

This will also go to addressing the increased popularity of Kutti Beach as a result of social media and the increased number of out-of-area visitors to the beach. Those wishing to travel to the beach with their dogs will be required to adhere to the shared hours. As a result, dog owners will be unable to remain at the beach for the entire day, which was a concern voiced by residents.

There are 834 signatures on the petition.

(Councillor Dixson)

Note: The Mayor, Councillor Dixson returned during this item, the time being 7:50pm.

Councillor Jarvis:

  • Condolences - Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack
Councillor Jarvis stated that there was a lot the Councillors could speak about in relation to their Councillor updates, but thought it appropriate to send condolences to the community impacted by

 

the Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack that took place on 14 December 2025. Councillor Jarvis expressed her condolences and acknowledged that the bravery and fearlessness of everyday Australians, surf lifesavers, police and ambulance workers should give us hope. Councillor Jarvis ended her address with the words, "Lets not now do nothing."

Councillor Parmegiani:

  • Condolences - Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack
Councillor Parmegiani echoed Councillor Jarvis' remarks, adding that he was at first hesitant to switch on his Christmas lights at home however, after speaking with Jewish friends, he was encouraged to “turn on those lights, don’t let darkness win.”

Councillor Andruska:

  • Meeting a Member of Waverley Council's Street Cleaning Staff
Councillor Andruska acknowledged the Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack, before sharing a lighter story about meeting a member of Waverley Council’s street cleaning team. The worker told him he was living his dream of being a “Garbo.” Councillor Andruska added that it’s great to have a goal in life, achieving it, and simply be happy.

Councillor Witt:

  • Condolences - Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack
Councillor Witt expressed her condolences to the community impacted by the Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack. Councillor Witt commended Kellie Sloane, Leader of the Opposition in New South Wales on an emotionally moving statement that was shared on social media. Councillor Witt stated that the attack at Bondi Beach was not just on the Jewish people of Australia, but on the whole Country. Councillor Witt ended her address saying that we need to do everything we can in our power to stamp-out anti-Semitism and terrorism, and to cherish the life we all want to live and cherish about our Country.

Councillor Robertson:

  • Condolences - Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack
  • Support for Mayoral Minute 9.2
Councillor Robertson offered his condolences to the community impacted by the Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack, in particular to the Jewish community. Councillor Robertson endorsed his support for the Mayoral Minute (9.2 - Response to Bondi Beach Terror Attack), and expressed the need for people to come together and to support each other at this time, and importantly, our brothers and sisters in the Jewish community.

Councillor Carmichael:

  • Condolences - Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack
Deputy Mayor, Councillor Carmichael conveyed his condolences to the community affected by the Bondi Beach terrorist attack and shared his close and personal experience of the incident. Councillor Carmichael expressed his hope that we as a nation really pull together. We have to. We've got no choice.

 

Councillor Mitchell:

  • Condolences - Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack
Councillor Mitchell conveyed her condolences to the community affected by the Bondi Beach terrorist attack and shared her personal experience of the incident. Councillor Mitchell expressed that we all live in a different world now, and we just have to get on with each other.

Councillor Price:
  • Condolences - Bondi Beach Terrorist Attack
  • Glenmore Road Public School Recognition Day
Councillor Price expressed her strong support for the sentiments expressed by her fellow Councillors, and conveyed her deepest sympathies to the Jewish community and the people of Bondi.

Councillor Price advised that on 15 December 2025, she was privileged to attend the Glenmore Road Public School Recognition Day Ceremony, in her capacity as Paddington Ward Councillor, but also on behalf of the Mayor. While attending the school, Councillor Price spoke with the school's Principal, who was initially apprehensive to proceed with the event given the tragic events of 14 December, however felt it important that we keep seeing the good in things and keep celebrating 'the good'. Councillor Price congratulated Yaaron Finkelstein as a member of the Glenmore Road community and President of the School Council, and highlighted that his son had been awarded 'Dux of the School'. Councillor Price shared an emotional message, emphasising that we must be united and that the Recognition Day Ceremony is an opportunity to look out over a sea of beautiful young children who are our future, and to believe that there is good in the world.

Motion moved by Councillor Dixson

THAT Council:

730/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:
 
  1. Notes the updated Street Tree Master Plan.

  2. Resolves to form a sub-committee to review the updated Street Tree Master Plan consisting of at least five Councillors representing each municipal Ward, responsible for:
  1. Reviewing the updated Street Tree Masterplan as a whole including its aims and strategies.
  2. Reviewing the updated Plan’s Species Lists for their respective Ward including Proposed Species and Critical Comments.

Councillor Parmegiani asking:

  1. Does Woollahra Council's Division of Planning and Place have an easily and readily accessible database of individual residential properties that have been heritage-listed or are pending NSW Government approval for heritage-listing in the Woollahra LGA?

    Yes / No

    If yes, what is the number of individual residential properties that have been heritage-listed or are pending NSW Government approval for heritage-listing in the Woollahra LGA?


  2. Does Woollahra Council's Division of Planning and Place have an easily and readily accessible record of the total surface area of the Woollahra LGA, expressed in square meters, which is currently listed as Heritage Conservation or pending NSW Government approval for listing as HCA?

    Yes / No

    If yes, what is the total surface area of the Woollahra LGA, expressed in square meters, which is currently listed as Heritage Conservation or pending NSW Government approval for listing as HCA?

Manager, Strategic Planning & Place in response:

  1. Extracted from the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 (Woollahra LEP 2014), Council staff have access to all the heritage listed properties. However, this is raw data only, and staff have analysed the information request into the categories below.

According to our analysis, there are 726 heritage listings in the Woollahra Local Government Area, of which 459 are residential heritage listings:

  • Residential Properties – Dwellings = 382
  • Residential Properties – Residential Flat Buildings (which each contain a number of units) = 77
Please note that the total number of residential heritage listings calculated (459) does not include residential properties that are listed for the heritage significance of other elements such as trees, fences, walls, grounds, gates, gardens etc.

It should also be noted that the schedule includes a number of other heritage listings (not just residential properties) such as commercial properties, reserves, beaches, street trees and public & private infrastructure.

With regards to the proposed heritage listed residential properties (which are currently pending NSW Government approval).  There are 37 properties, which can be categorised as follows: 

  • Residential Properties – Dwellings = 15
  • Residential Properties – Residential Flat Buildings (which each contain a number of units) = 22

  1. Yes.
The total surface area of the Woollahra LGA is 12.2 km sq (12,200,000 m sq).

The total surface area that is currently identified as a heritage conservation area (under the Woollahra LEP 2014) is 2.9 km sq or 2,900,000 m sq (approx. 23.77% of the total LGA area).

The total surface area that is a proposed heritage conservation area which is currently pending NSW Government approval is 3,433m sq (approx. 0.0281% of the total LGA area).

739/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes it's Night Time Economy Policy (adopted December 2019) and further notes its commitment to supporting:
  1. a night-time economy that enables local business to thrive whilst improving the liveability, amenities and lifestyle for residents; 
  2. Council supports cutting unnecessary red-tape so that local businesses can focus on what they do best;
  3. the need to better manage patrons throughout the LGA so that economic activity does not come at the expense of local residential amenity.
  1. Requests the General Manager prepare a report to be tabled at the Environmental & Planning Committee in early 2026 on the costs and resourcing required to review the Night Time Economy Policy and any other related policies (i.e. Footway Dining Policy and Guidelines), with a view to updating the policy(s) to reflect:
  1. Enabling actions to implement the NSW Government's Vibrancy Reforms package, particularly the feasibility of 'Special Entertainment Precincts' for both licensed and non-licensed premises in suitable locations within the LGA;
  2. Any necessary harmonisation between neighbouring Council's night-time economy plans (particularly along Oxford St);
  3. Recommendations to upgrade late-night transport, patron management (particularly in Double Bay), cleanliness, traffic management and general enforcement of rules, as to mitigate the impact on resident amenities - including how Council could partner with community organisations and groups to accomplish any such recommendations;
  4. Recommendations to continue to support the expansion of alfresco dining throughout the LGA.

The Motion was put and Carried.

 

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Price, Councillor Robertson, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Zeltzer, Councillor Regan
Councillor Mitchell

13/1

Note: 
The Council amended Part A and added new Part D to the original Motion, which formed the Resolution.

Note: 
Councillor Carmichael declared a Non-Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in this item, as Councillor Carmichael previously served on Council with Anthony Boskovitz, being a member of the public who previously made submissions on the item. Councillor Carmichael remained in the meeting, participated in debate and voted on the matter.

Note: 
Councillor Zeltzer declared a Non-Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in this item, as Councillor Zeltzer previously served on Council with Anthony Boskovitz, being a member of the public who previously made submissions on the item. Councillor Zeltzer remained in the meeting, participated in debate and voted on the matter.

 

Note: 
The Mayor, Councillor Dixson declared a Non-Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in this item, as Councillor Dixson is in the same Liberal Party branch as Anthony Boskovitz, being a member of the public who previously made submissions on the item. Councillor Dixson remained in the meeting, participated in debate and voted on the matter.

Note: The Mayor vacated the Chair during this item. Councillor Carmichael, as Deputy Mayor assumed the Chair, the time being 6:32pm.

Motion moved by Councillor Carmichael
Seconded by Councillor Jarvis

THAT Council:

  1. Note the post exhibition report on Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (Amendment No. 37) which seeks to strengthen provisions for housing in accessible areas (land subject to the low and mid-rise housing reforms).

  2. Resolves to re-exhibit Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan (Amendment No. 37) at Attachment 1 (which contains one post exhibition amendment) as contained in the report to the Extraordinary Environmental Planning Committee meeting of 8 December 2026 from Tuesday 16 December 2025 to Monday 9 February 2026. This extended exhibition will take into account the public holidays and comply with the requirements of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, and the Woollahra Community Participation Plan.

  3. Notes that a post exhibition report will be tabled at an Extraordinary Meeting of the Council on or before 23 February 2026.

Amendment moved by Councillor Witt

THAT Council:

  1. Note the post exhibition report on Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (Amendment No. 37) which seeks to strengthen provisions for housing in accessible areas (land subject to the low and mid-rise housing reforms).

  2. Resolves to re-exhibit Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan (Amendment No. 37) at Attachment 1 (which contains one post exhibition amendment) as contained in the report to the Extraordinary Environmental Planning Committee meeting of 8 December 2026 from Tuesday 16 December 2025 to Monday 9 February 2026. This extended exhibition will take into account the public holidays and comply with the requirements of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, and the Woollahra Community Participation Plan.

  3. Notes that the draft DCP (Amendment No 37) has been put on public exhibition and that based on the feedback received, Council would have recommended it for adoption at the Ordinary meeting of Council on 15 December 2025. Consequently, DA applicants have already been given notice of an important new policy direction, in this case the introduction of Chapter B4, which establishes specific objectives and controls for housing in accessible areas having regard to the site and its context, and including provisions for streetscape presentation, building design, heritage conservation, amenity, dwelling mix, and car parking.

  4. Notes that planning regulations and case law recognise that a draft DCP may be a relevant consideration in the assessment of Development Applications (DAs) under section 4.15(1)(e) "public interest" of the EP&A Act, and that the draft DCP (Amendment 37) will therefore be considered in the assessment process for DAs lodged after 16 December 2025.


  5. Resolves to allow for submissions made during the first exhibition period to be recorded as submissions received during the second exhibition period, given that the draft DCP (Amendment No. 37), to be re-exhibited for 28 days, is substantially the same as the one that just came off public exhibition.

  6. Notes that a post exhibition report will be tabled at an Extraordinary Meeting of the Council on or before 23 February 2026.

The Amendment lapsed for want of a Seconder

The Motion was put and Carried

(Councillor Carmichael/Councillor Jarvis)

733/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Note the post exhibition report on Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (Amendment No. 37) which seeks to strengthen provisions for housing in accessible areas (land subject to the low and mid-rise housing reforms). However, the exhibition did not comply with the minimum 28 days required  in accordance with the relevant legislation.  

  2. Resolves to re-exhibit Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan (Amendment No. 37) at Attachment 1 (which contains one post exhibition amendment) as contained in the report to the Extraordinary Environmental Planning Committee meeting of 8 December 2026 from Tuesday 16 December 2025 to Monday 9 February 2026. This extended exhibition will take into account the public holidays and comply with the requirements of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, and the Woollahra Community Participation Plan.

  3. Notes that a post exhibition report will be tabled at an Extraordinary Meeting of the Council on or before 23 February 2026.

  4. Requests the General Manager to inform members of the public who made submissions during the first exhibition period, that their submissions will need to be resubmitted in order for them to be taken into consideration.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Witt

734/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Endorse the draft concept design for O'Sullivan Road Recreation Path, presented as Attachment 1, for the purpose of public exhibition for a period of 28 days.

  2. Note that a further report will be prepared for the Finance, Community & Services Committee following the close of the public exhibition period and assessment of submissions received.

  1. replacement of missing trees on the O’Sullivan Road verge
  2. further enhancing tree canopy along the O’Sullivan Road Recreation Path
  3. slight relocation of the pedestrian crossing proposed at Bunyula Road
  4. additional bike-parking infrastructure, especially near the Plumer Road village
  5. pedestrian gate access through the new chain link fence in similar locations to those that exist, providing access for residents in Manion Avenue
  6. the design demonstrating the location of the newly installed electric vehicle chargers in the Easts Rugby Club carpark
  7. investigation of the placement of the centre road line outside 223 O’Sullivan Road so that no car parking is lost on the Western side of the street
  8. during exhibition a clear and simple site plan is provided which includes the following:
  • the corresponding street addresses across the road from the path.
  • whether the bike path will be marked showing separation of walkers and bike users.

D. Note that feasible changes identified by staff may be made prior to the concept design being placed on exhibition.

  2. Adopt the draft Grants Policy and Grants Guidelines presented as Attachment 1 and Attachment 2.

  3. Endorse the criteria relating to the 2026/27 Outgoing Sponsorship Program and the themes relating to the 2026/27 Grants round for the Community and Cultural Grant stream and the Placemaking Grant stream.

  4. Give consideration in the development of the draft 2026-2027 budget to increasing the grant funding amounts for 2026-2027 to the following:

  1. Community & Cultural grants - Small Grants from $3,000 to $3,900 and Large Grants from $7,500 to $9,750

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, is satisfied that the matters required to be addressed under Clause 4.6(3) of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 have been demonstrated and that consent may be granted to the development application, which contravenes the Height of Buildings development standard under cl 4.3 of the Woollahra LEP 2014.

AND

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, grant development consent to Development Application No. 254/2025/1 for demolition of the existing dwelling and construction of a new dwelling with a detached garage, swimming pool, new landscaping and associated works on land at 1 Wentworth Road VAUCLUSE, subject to the conditions at Attachment 2

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

Brett Daintry, Fran Ezra and Julie-Anne McMillan addressed the Panel.

Panel's Decision

That the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council as the consent authority, modify the development consent to DA436/2020 for the demolition of an existing dwelling house and the construction of a new dwelling house and swimming pool and associated works on land at 18 Olphert Avenue Vaucluse in accordance with the modified conditions of consent in Attachment 2.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report and late memorandum prepared by Council officers that address the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.56 including 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. 

In terms of the concerns expressed by 20 Olphert Avenue at the public meeting (which specifically related to privacy impacts), the Panel was satisfied that these were adequately addressed in the assessment report and condition of C.1(h).

The concerns expressed by 16 Olphert Avenue at the public meeting related to privacy, location of planting and wording of condition A.7. The panel was satisfied that these were adequately addressed in the assessment report and conditions A.7 and E.27 (with minor modifications). Another concern expressed by 16 Olphert Avenue related to unauthorised works. The Panel noted that these works did not form part of the modified consent as versed in condition A.7, and that this is a matter for Council's Compliance Department.

 

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions of Consent).

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion

Note: 
Councillor Carmichael declared a Non-Significant, Non-Pecuniary Interest in this item, as Councillor Carmichael is a supporter of Lifeline. Councillor Carmichael remained in the meeting, participated in debate and voted on the matter.

(Councillor Dixson)

761/2025 Resolved:

THAT Council: 
 
  1. Notes the Mayoral Minute tabled at the 15 December 2025 Council meeting strongly condemning the senseless and deplorable terrorist attack that took place on Sunday 14 December 2025 at Bondi Beach that targeted our Jewish community.

  2. Extends our deepest condolences to the families of the victims and all those affected by the tragic events of the Bondi Beach terrorist attack.

  3. Formally acknowledges the incredible work of the Police, all emergency services, medical teams, first responders, including lifeguards (on-duty and off-duty), and members of the public in response to the attack. 

  4. Endorse Woollahra Council pledging support for Jewish Australians and reaffirm our commitment to a peaceful and harmonious NSW in line with the pledge established by Multicultural NSW. The pledge reads:

    In the wake of the unspeakable attack on our Jewish community at Bondi Beach, we come together across cultural, linguistic and religious differences to make a unified pledge:

  •  We collectively mourn for victims and their families and pledge our support and solidarity for the Jewish community in NSW. 
  • We pledge to stand up and stand united against antisemitism, racism and hate and to support all victims of racism, hate and religious intolerance. 
  • We pledge to protect and promote the rights and responsibilities of all the people of NSW in a cohesive and multicultural society.
  • We pledge to work in unity across cultural, linguistic and religious differences to uphold our democratic values and freedoms.
  • We are stronger together.

  1. Allocates a total of $45,000, to the following organisations for work to support the Woollahra community in the aftermath of the Bondi Beach attack:

  1. Jewish House (for counselling services or similar) - $20,000
  2. Lifeline (for trauma counselling or similar) - $20,000
  3. Kids Giving Back (for volunteering opportunities for families & children) - $5,000

  1. Notes that the $45,000 detailed in Part E, will be funded from Council's working funds balance.

  2. Requests the General Manager table a report at the June 2026 Council meeting detailing information on the expenditure of the funds referred to in Part E above.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Price, Councillor Robertson, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Dixson, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Regan
None

12/0

AND

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, grant development consent to Development Application No. 380/2025/1 for alterations and additions to the existing dwelling house, including the construction of two lift shafts, rear addition and new windows and doors on land at 40 Drumalbyn Road BELLEVUE HILL, subject to the conditions in Attachment (Adopted Conditions).

The Panel viewed the site using electronic resources, considered the submissions and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the majority of the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved.

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, refuse development consent to Development Application No. 361/2025/1 for the addition of new awning structure covering the outdoor dining area of the food and drink premises operated as Ruma Dining at Tenancy K1 on land at 1 Kiaora Road DOUBLE BAY, for the reasons in Attachment 2.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site inspection and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the majority of the Panel is satisfied that the application be refused as set out in Attachment (Adopted Reasons for Refusal).

In dissenting from the majority, the Chair, David Ryan, considers that the proposal is reasonable and acceptable and not inconsistent with the DCP principles for the Kiaora Lane Public Plaza.

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion

Note: Christopher Carolan, Robert Fiaini, Tony Moody, Lucretia Liu and Hector Abrahams addressed the Panel.

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, defer the determination of Development Application No. 256/2025/1 for extension of an existing lift shaft to provide lift access to the roof terrace at 10 Wentworth Street, Point Piper, to allow:

  1. the Panel to carry out site inspections at the objectors’ properties at No. 8 Wentworth Street, Point Piper; and
  2. the Applicant be requested to submit to the Council prior to the site inspection if practicable, further details of the proposed lift shaft in terms of its visual appearance perceivable from the residential flat building at No. 8 Wentworth Street, Point Piper to assist the Panel’s site inspections. These may include visualisations from No. 8 showing proposed materials, finishes and colours in the context of the existing building.
The application will then be determined electronically by the Panel (as constituted on 19 February 2026) no later than 5 March 2026, unless otherwise decided by the Chair.

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

Councillor Witt:

  • Condolences - Michael Gleeson-White AO

Councillor Witt acknowledged the recent passing of Michael Gleeson-White AO, a long‑term Vaucluse resident who passed away at the age of 100. Councillor Witt acknowledged his involvement with the Art Gallery of New South Wales and recognised his contributions to the arts.


Councillor Silcocks

  • Acknowledgement of Staff - Celebrate Double Bay Festival

Councillor Silcocks acknowledged and thanked Council staff for their efforts in delivering the Double Bay Festival over the weekend. He noted that this marks the beginning of a three‑year program, which he expects will generate strong local interest and local involvement. Councillor Silcocks added that he hopes the festival will continue to grow over the next two years, and commended staff for achieving so much in a short timeframe. Councillor Silcocks extended his congratulations to all involved.


Councillor Robertson

  • Woollahra Life! Program
  • Ukraine-Russia War Anniversary
  • Progressive Pride Flag Raising 

Councillor Robertson advises that as Council's representative on the Holdsworth Community Centre Board he is pleased to report to Council the success of Holdsworth's new community based program, Woollahra Life! 

 

Woollahra Life! recorded 778 attendances from 149 participants in Q2, with 98% aged 65+ and 94% residing within the Woollahra LGA. Momentum has continued into Term 1 2026, with more than 80 new participants welcomed in the opening weeks following targeted local marketing and strong word-of-mouth referrals. The program currently delivers 15 weekly classes, with several at full capacity and others building steadily as the pilot phase informs future program curation. This term’s Get Healthy This Term focus has strengthened physical activity, wellbeing and social connection across the cohort. Participant feedback consistently highlights improved confidence, balance and reduced isolation. Congratulations goes to facilitator, Llanos Perez, for her leadership, dedication and infectious enthusiasm that has been critical to such a positive start for the new Woollahra Life! program.

Councillor Robertson advises that tomorrow (24 February 2026) marks the fourth anniversary of the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Councillor Robertson is very proud of Woollahra Council's continuing support for the people of Ukraine and for the Ukrainian community here in Sydney. This anniversary is a sobering reminder of the ongoing human cost of war and we stand in solidarity with those who continue to show extraordinary resilience in the face of hardship and conflict. At our 2025 End of Year Celebration, Councillor Robertson was deeply moved to receive feedback from the Vice President of the Ukrainian Council of NSW, Mr & Mrs Andrew Mencinsky who both spoke about how much Woollahra Council’s visible and consistent support means to the Ukrainian community. This reinforces the importance of local leadership in moments of global significance. As a person of Ukrainian heritage, Councillor Robertson believes our advocacy makes a difference. Councillor Robertson is very proud that as a Council we remain committed to standing with Ukraine and to ensuring members of our local Ukrainian community feel seen, supported and valued.

On 13 February 2026, Councillor Robertson was privileged to take part in the raising of the progressive pride flag to mark the commencement of the Mardi Gras festival. This occasion always reminds him of the struggle for equality and the recognition of minority rights was a hard fought battle, and an ongoing one for our trans and intersex communities. Councillor Robertson was so pleased to be joined by 78s Wanda Kluk and Rebbel as well as Rabbi Ninio of Emmanual Synagogue and of course Councillor Harriet Price and Councillor Sean Carmichael.","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[],"minutes":[]},{"id":13205,"name":"Conclusion of the Meeting","parentId":-1,"sortOrder":18,"minutesSortOrder":18,"minutesParentId":-1,"outlineNumber":"17.","fullOutlineNumber":"17.","htmlContent":"

71/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Note the post exhibition report on Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (Amendment No. 37) which seeks to strengthen provisions for housing in accessible areas (land subject to the low and mid-rise housing reforms).

  2. Approves the amended Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan (Amendment No. 37) at Attachment 1, of the report to the Council meeting of 23 February 2026, which is being adopted after extensive consultation with interested persons including the affected community.

  3. Notes that Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (Amendment No. 37) is already being used as a matter for consideration in assessments of development applications. 

  4. Notes that Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (Amendment No. 37) was on exhibition during the period 30 October 2025 and 26 November 2025 and re-exhibited between 16 December 2025 and 9 February 2026.

  5. Notes the significant number of submissions and community interest in this item.

  6. Amend part 2.1.1 of the Draft DCP to also apply to consents given under section 4.56 Environmental Planning and Assessment Act.

  7. Requests that the Draft Woollahra Development Control Plan 2015 (Amendment No. 37) comes into effect as soon as practicable.

The Motion was put and Carried.

In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

Note:

Note: 
The Council amended Part B ahead of the vote.

(Councillor Witt/Councillor Regan)

81/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Requests the General Manager to report back to Council on the costs and anticipated timeline for revising The Double Bay Floodplain Risk Management Plan and Study (2014) and The Rose Bay Floodplain Risk Management Plan and Study (2014).

  2. Notes that the above Plans were informed by studies done in 2008 and 2010 respectively, which identified moderate to high flood risk across Double Bay and Rose Bay.

  3. Notes that serious flood events have occurred in Rose Bay and Double Bay in 2015, 2018, 2019, March 2022, April 2022, February 2023, April 2024, and December 2024.

  4. Notes that both Plans recommended that any consideration of uplift beyond the Council's existing planning controls (ie 3 to 4 storey apartment buildings in the R3 Medium Density Residential zones) should be accompanied by revised flood impact assessments in the flood risk areas.



  5. Notes that the Conservation Programs, Heritage and Regulation (CPHR) Group of the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) recently  advised the Department of Planning Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI) that the Rose Bay Floodplain Risk Management Study and Plan could not be relied upon by the applicant of the 23-31 Dover Road State Significant Development Application (SSDA) for the preparation of its Flood Impact and Risk Assessment.

  6. Notes that the CPHR recommended that a new site-specific flood study be commissioned and prepared in accordance with Understanding and managing flood risk: Flood risk management guideline FB01 (DPE, 30 June 2023), and requested that the flood study incorporates an extended area to include upstream, downstream and adjacent properties.

  7. Notes that in December 2025, the NSW Government released Flood Planning Principles as an Appendix to the Sydney Plan (now on public exhibition), and that the seven principles listed below are directly relevant to the flood prone areas of Woollahra Council.

  8. Notes that because of the numerous Low and Mid-Rise (LMR) Housing Policy SSDAs and DAs currently in the development assessment process pipeline, a re-assessment of whether current plans and controls are required to protect public and private property is not only prudent but urgent.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

Councillor Ardouin asking:

  1. As at 1 October 2024 what was the count and quantum (in annual revenue $) of lease contracts which had expired or were due to expire in the next 3months and had not been renewed (i.e. left on a monthly rolling basis)?

  2. As at 1 July 2025 what was the count and quantum (in annual revenue $) of lease contracts which had expired or were due to expire in the next 3months and had not been renewed (i.e. left on a monthly rolling basis)?

  3. As at 1 January 2025 what was the count and quantum (in annual revenue $) of lease contracts which had expired or were due to expire in the next 3months and had not been renewed (i.e. left on a monthly rolling basis)?

  4. What is the status of the Dunbar House lease EOI process which closed in October 2025? When might Council expect a report on this?

Manager - Property & Projects in response:

Some of the above questions (1, 2 & 3) regarding the status of various leases; however, some of the information requested cannot be provided. The delay in tendering and releasing leases since 2019 arose from the impacts of COVID 19 and the pending adoption of the Plans of Management for buildings situated on Crown land. Councillor Ardouin asking:

  1. What has been the average time for DA processing each year over the last 5 years (inc. YTD), including any breakdowns to this which would assist stakeholders to understand what is driving trends in DA processing times (i.e. by application types/size)?

  2. Has Council identified any additional strategies to increase the efficiency of DA processing in line with the Minister for Planning’s Statement of Expectations of <85 days?

  3. How will the NSW Government’s planning reforms impact on the ability of Council to conduct proper and thorough assessment of DAs submitted to Council? How will these impact on Council resources and has it been quantified in the revised FY25-26 budget?

Manager - Development Assessment in response:

General Notes/Comments:

  • Based on the above figures, the current trend for DA Processing Times is trending downwards (i.e. 2024, 2025 and 2026)
  • Factors which may impact on DA processing times include:
  • No of Applications Lodged
  • Type of Applications (simple vs complex DAs)
  • Staff Resources
  • No of Appeals
  • Covid
  • Legislative and Policy changes including new planning reforms 
  1. Has Council identified any additional strategies to increase the efficiency of DA processing in line with the Minister for Planning’s Statement of Expectations of <85 days?

Note: The current Ministerial Statement of Expectation in terms of DA Processing Times for the period between 1 July 2025- 30 June 2026 is 105 Days which Council is currently achieving (88 Days). 
For the period between 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 and 1 July 2027 to 30 June 2028, the Ministerial Statement of Expectation in terms of DA Processing Times will be 95 and 85 days, respectively.

The following strategies have been implemented to improve Council’s average DA Processing Times and to ensure compliance with the Statement of Expectations Order (initially made in July 2024):

  • A Review of the DA Assessment Service undertaken in 2023
  • Adopting and implementing the recommendations made in the ‘Review  of the DA Assessment Service’
  • Adoption of a new Delegations for Planning Applications” Model in December 2023
  • Reviewed the Development Assessment Review Process
  • Introduction of the following work strategies:
  • Monthly meetings are held between the Manager of Development Assessment and the respective Team Leaders to:
  • Undertake an audit and review of all outstanding DAs and s4.55s
  • Develop a monthly work plan for each Team and their respective Planning Officers
  • Identify Applications which are to be Fast-Tracked
  • Attend DARC meetings with a focus on reducing the number of formal referrals and the use of standard conditions (at DARC) including nominating service delivery for referrals to be completed (i.e. 25, 35 and 40 days)

  • Reviewed  Council’s Report Templates with the aim of streamlining DA Assessment Reports
  • Forward planning in recruiting new staff when vacancies arise
  • Team Leaders taking a firm approach to not accept Replacement Applications or amended plans
  • Refusing all Applications that do not meet the 14 day ‘Stop the Clock’ period
  • Focus has been on DAs and not s4.55s as the Ministerial Expectation only relates to DA processing times
  • Utilising external planning consultants for major DAs with subsequent Appeals

  1. How will the NSW Government’s planning reforms impact on the ability of Council to conduct proper and thorough assessment of DAs submitted to Council? How will these impact on Council resources and has it been quantified in the revised FY25-26 budget?

Since the introduction of the Low to Mide Rise Policy(LMR)  in February 2025, Council to date has received 25 DAs and commented on 5 State significant DAs (State Government is the consent authority). These Applications are complex, have attracted numerous submissions and have or are  most likely to be the subject of an Appeal. This will have significant impact on:

  • Council’s DA Processing Times
  • Legal Costs
  • Staff Resources (i.e.time)

These planning reforms (LMR) will not impact on Council undertaking a proper and through assessment of Applications.

How will these impact on Council resources and has it been quantified in the revised FY25-26 budget?

See above.

Not quantified in the FY25-26 budget.

Councillor Ardouin asking:

  1. What has been the community engagement around any programs Council has been running to increase the uptake of solar or batteries in private residences?

  2. How has the rollout of solar on Council-owned or managed properties been progressing?

  3. Has there been any further engagement from LGNSW, OLG, SSROC or bilaterally with other Councils regarding progressing community or grid-scale battery or solar projects?

Team Leader - Environment & Sustainability in response:
  1. A solar and batteries community workshop was held at Double Bay Library in September, providing information to the community about how to install solar and batteries and how to access the various government subsidies available. The information has been included on Council’s website: Solar panels and home batteries | Woollahra Municipal Council. Information has also been distributed to the community via Council’s newsletters and social media platforms. Another community workshop is being held at Double Bay Library on 25 March 2026.

  2. Where feasible, solar panels have been installed on Council owned buildings, including the Council chambers at Redleaf, Double Bay Library, Vaucluse Bowling Club and Council’s depots. Solar output is monitored by staff and the panels are maintained regularly to ensure that they are operating at optimal capacity. The Quarry Street Depot roof is due for replacement, we are assessing the potential for installing a larger solar array and battery once the new roof is installed.

  3. The most recent development in Sydney is a trial by Ausgrid of a ‘Community Power Network’ in the Mascot-Botany area. Council staff were briefed about this initiative at a meeting held by SSROC. This project will involve Ausgrid offering incentives for customers to install additional rooftop solar in the trial area, and use of community batteries to store excess energy, redistributing it at peak times. If successful, this may be rolled out to other areas. Staff meet with Ausgrid periodically and will pursue any feasible opportunities that arise for community batteries. Grid-scale batteries are not feasible in the Woollahra area due to space constraints, they are suited to large greenfield or brownfield development sites.

Councillor Ardouin asking:

  1. Noting 10 months has elapsed, are there any updates that can be provided regarding the motion passed at the April Council meeting regarding the Local Government Financing Facility?

  2. What has been the key insights obtained from discussions with the Office of Local Government, Local Government NSW and other stakeholders (i.e. Banks, non-bank lenders and other financial institutions)?

  3. Has any additional recommendations been identified regarding implementing the contemplated local government financing facility?

 

Chief Financial Officer in Response:

The Delivery Program 2025-26 to 2028-29 and Operational Plan 2025-26 Progress Report presented at the 9 February 2026 Finance, Community and Services (FC&S) Committee meeting included the following update in relation to the Local Government financing facility motion. 

“In Progress; Letter has been sent to the OLG regarding a Local Government Financing Vehicle (LGFV) and we are awaiting a response.  The letter noted that the NSW Treasury Corporation (TCorp) currently provides loans to local governments at competitive rates and serves as the central borrowing authority for the State.  In the letter Council asked the OLG: a) Whether OLG is currently exploring or would consider supporting the development of a NSW-based collective borrowing facility for local councils, similar to the Victorian LGFV; b) If so, what role councils such as Woollahra might play in shaping or participating in such an initiative; c) And whether legislative or regulatory frameworks in NSW would support this form of cooperative financing vehicle.”

There are no further updates beyond that provided at the 9 February FC&S Committee meeting.

Councillor Ardouin asking:

  1. Are there any updates that can be provided regarding the extent to which Council has progressed adoption of the new ERP? If delays have been encountered, please update Councillors on the reasons for such delays?

  2. What opportunities has Council identified in incorporating AI into its operational procedures?

  3. To what extent is Council implementing strategies to leverage the opportunities described above to increase efficiency throughout its operations?

Manager - Information & Digital Transformation in response:

  1. Response:
Council’s 2025–26 Operational Plan commitment is to progress digital transformation initiatives, including investigation of a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system and emerging technologies.

In line with that commitment, Council has issued a formal Request for Proposal (RFP) to market. The RFP closes on 11 March 2026. 

While the broader ERP replacement initiative has been under consideration and planning in various stages for several years, this reflects the scale and complexity of the undertaking. ERP replacement is a whole-of-Council transformation program, impacting finance, procurement, asset management and maintenance, HR/payroll, planning and DA assessment, and Council-wide operational workflows. Delays have primarily related to the need to align the program with broader digital transformation priorities and resourcing capacity, with high demand for foundational ICT and business system improvement projects in recent years.

Positively, the local government Software as a Service ERP market has evolved considerably during this period, with both established vendors enhancing their offerings and new entrants introducing contemporary, cloud-native solutions tailored to the sector.

The current RFP process represents a material step forward. Subject to Council endorsement, implementation is expected to commence in the financial year 2026-2027.

  1. Response:
Significant progress has been made to incorporate AI into operational procedures.

A public-facing AI chatbot, now known as Lara, has been piloted internally and subsequently launched, indexing Council website content, meeting information, and upcoming events. This represents Council’s first operational AI deployment. The solution operates from Council’s secure Microsoft environment and is focused on improving customer self-service and enquiry efficiency, including that of staff who routinely reference information on Council’s website. Usage of the chatbot will be regularly reviewed through both analytical data and user feedback.

Planning is also underway for a structured internal pilot of Microsoft 365 Copilot. The proposed pilot will assess productivity benefits, document summarisation, meeting insights and knowledge retrieval, with defined governance and measurement controls. Planning for the pilot is expected to conclude in March, leading to initial deployment in April 2026. 

In parallel, several additional AI use cases are currently being assessed, including solutions that aim to:

 

  • Enhance indexing and searching of Council and Committee business papers
  • Improve Development Assessment documentation processes
  • Redact private information in DA documentation
  • Transcribe of handwritten local history materials
  • Improve internal IT Service Desk delivery
  • Leverage new AI offerings in existing business systems

  1. Response:
Council is implementing both ERP transformation and targeted AI initiatives as practical mechanisms to improve efficiency across operations.

In relation to ERP, the current procurement process is focused on securing a modern, integrated SaaS platform that will replace several fragmented legacy systems. The intended outcomes include streamlined finance, procurement, and HR workflows, improved asset and works management, reduced manual reconciliation, stronger reporting capabilities, and improved data consistency across the Council. While implementation will occur over multiple years, the program will be structured to deliver phased improvements as modules are deployed.

In relation to AI, Council aims to prioritise practical pilots focusing on measurable productivity gains. These include improving information retrieval, automating manual tasks, and investigating productivity tools within the Microsoft 365 environment to reduce drafting, summarisation and document handling time. These initiatives are intended to reduce administrative overhead, improve response times and support (not replace) staff in their decision-making. 

It is important to note that ERP replacement and most AI adoption initiatives are foundational enablers rather than short-term cost reduction exercises. Efficiencies will accrue progressively through the introduction of improved workflows, reduced duplication of effort, enhanced information accessibility and better data quality across Council.

Recognising that ERP delivery is a multi-year transformation, Council is also progressing complementary system modernisation and automation efforts in parallel, with targeted technology upgrades that aim to deliver efficiencies and service improvements. This includes transitioning legacy on-premises systems to contemporary SaaS platforms, enhancing customer contact centre capabilities with omni-channel functionality and AI-enabled analytics, modernising booking and payment systems to increase self-service options for residents, and improving staff mobility through device and infrastructure refresh programs. These initiatives ensure that operational improvements continue to be realised while the longer-term ERP transformation is delivered.

Collectively, these initiatives represent a continual implementation of several strategies to increase operational efficiency, with benefits expected to continually and progressively accrue.

82/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes that:
  1. On 4 February 2026, the Federal Government announced the proposed divestment of a number of assets from the Defence Estate, including the Victoria Barracks at Paddington (the Barracks).

  2. The Barracks are one of the most significant heritage sites in New South Wales and are foundational to the origin and development of Paddington, with the establishment of the Barracks shaping the suburb that followed.

  3. Any proposed sale, redevelopment or change of use of the Barracks must be approached with great care to ensure its heritage significance is protected and that the historic fabric and character of surrounding areas are not compromised.


  4. The proposed divestment of the Barracks presents a rare opportunity to deliver genuine public benefit, including improved community access to green space, appropriate housing options and enhanced community facilities.

  5. It is a key stakeholder in the future of the Barracks, as any decisions about its use, ownership or management has significant heritage, social, environmental, economic, cultural, planning and infrastructure impacts for the local community.

  6. In November 2025, following community consultation, the City of Sydney published a document entitled Victoria Barracks Guiding Principles (the Guiding Principles), articulating a set of high level principles to help guide the future of the site, including to:
  1. Conserve and enhance its heritage and military significance.
  2. Maximise public accessibility and maintain public ownership.
  3. Enhance and expand green open space.
  4. Prioritise cultural and community uses.
  5. Incorporate diverse housing, including public housing.
  6. Encourage compatible and viable commercial uses.
  7. Encourage environmental sustainability.
  8. Ensure robust planning, implementation and management.

  1. Resolves to:
  1. Write to the Federal Government, through the Minister for Defence, the Minister for Finance and any other relevant Ministers and agencies, requesting that the Government:
  1. Commits to genuine, early and ongoing community consultation prior to any decision to sell or otherwise divest the Barracks.
  2. Formally involves Council in the planning and decision making processes relating to the future use, management or disposal of the Barracks.
  3. Ensures that potential impacts on the local community are fully assessed and transparently considered as part of any divestment decision.
  4. Recognises that the sale of the Barracks must be a carefully considered process that honours heritage, protects amenity and delivers lasting public benefit.
  5. Develops and publishes a clear, transparent framework for community consultation in relation to any sale of the Barracks.
  1. Congratulate the City of Sydney and the Lord Mayor, Clover Moore, on their work in developing the Guiding Principles.

  2. Endorse the Guiding Principles as an appropriate and constructive basis for discussing the future of the Barracks and adopts them as a basis for Council’s advocacy on the future of the site (including in preparing the correspondence referred to in paragraph B (1) (above).

  3. Work collaboratively with the City of Sydney to advocate that any future use, management or divestment of the Barracks is consistent with the Guiding Principles.

  4. Immediately reconvene a meeting of the Oxford Street Working Party to consider the establishment of a Barracks Advisory Forum (or similar group), with proposed functions to:
  1. Provide a structure forum for ongoing dialogue between Council, the City of Sydney, community representatives, local businesses, heritage and planning experts and other key stakeholders regarding the future of the Barracks.
  2. Monitor and review information relating to the divestment process for the Barracks and advise Council on emerging issues, risks and opportunities.
  3. Help articulate community priorities for the site consistent with the Guiding Principles.

  1. Notes that:
  1. On 4 February 2026, the Federal Government announced the proposed divestment of a number of assets from the Defence Estate, including the Victoria Barracks at Paddington (the Barracks).

  2. The Barracks are one of the most significant heritage sites in New South Wales and are foundational to the origin and development of Paddington, with the establishment of the Barracks shaping the suburb that followed.

  3. Any proposed sale, redevelopment or change of use of the Barracks must be approached with great care to ensure its heritage significance is protected and that the historic fabric and character of surrounding areas are not compromised.

  4. The proposed divestment of the Barracks presents a rare opportunity to deliver genuine public benefit, including improved community access to green space, appropriate housing options and enhanced community facilities.

  5. It is a key stakeholder in the future of the Barracks, as any decisions about its use, ownership or management has significant heritage, social, environmental, economic, cultural, planning and infrastructure impacts for the local community.

  6. In November 2025, following community consultation, the City of Sydney published a document entitled Victoria Barracks Guiding Principles (the Guiding Principles), articulating a set of high level principles to help guide the future of the site, including to:
  1. Conserve and enhance its heritage and military significance.
  2. Maximise public accessibility and maintain public ownership.
  3. Enhance and expand green open space.
  4. Prioritise cultural and community uses.
  5. Incorporate diverse housing, including public housing.
  6. Encourage compatible and viable commercial uses.
  7. Encourage environmental sustainability.
  8. Ensure robust planning, implementation and management.

  1. Resolves to:
  1. Write to the Federal Government, through the Minister for Defence, the Minister for Finance and any other relevant Ministers and agencies, requesting that the Government:
  1. Commits to genuine, early and ongoing community consultation prior to any decision to sell or otherwise divest the Barracks.
  2. Formally involves Council in the planning and decision making processes relating to the future use, management or disposal of the Barracks.
  3. Ensures that potential impacts on the local community are fully assessed and transparently considered as part of any divestment decision.
  4. Recognises that the sale of the Barracks must be a carefully considered process that honours heritage, protects amenity and delivers lasting public benefit.
  5. Develops and publishes a clear, transparent framework for community consultation in relation to any sale of the Barracks.
  1. Congratulate the City of Sydney and the Lord Mayor, Clover Moore, on their work in developing the Guiding Principles.

  2. Endorse the Guiding Principles as an appropriate and constructive basis for discussing the future of the Barracks and adopts them as a basis for Council’s advocacy on the future of the site (including in preparing the correspondence referred to in paragraph B (1) (above).

  3. Work collaboratively with the City of Sydney to advocate that any future use, management or divestment of the Barracks is consistent with the Guiding Principles.

  4. Immediately reconvene a meeting of the Oxford Street Working Party to consider the establishment of a Barracks Advisory Forum (or similar group), with proposed functions to:
  1. Provide a structure forum for ongoing dialogue between Council, the City of Sydney, community representatives, local businesses, heritage and planning experts and other key stakeholders regarding the future of the Barracks.
  2. Monitor and review information relating to the divestment process for the Barracks and advise Council on emerging issues, risks and opportunities.
  3. Help articulate community priorities for the site consistent with the Guiding Principles.
  4. Support Council’s advocacy by helping to develop position statements, submissions and communications to State and Federal Governments and other stakeholders in relation to the Barracks.

  1. Provide a copy of the Motion and Council's correspondence to Allegra Spender MP, Alex Greenwich MP, Kellie Sloane MP and the Lord Mayor of Sydney, Clover Moore (with a copy to all City of Sydney Councillors).

Mills Oakley had submitted late correspondence regarding this item. Councillor Woodgate remained in the meeting, participated in debate and voted on the matter.

Motion moved by Councillor Price
Seconded by Councillor Witt

84/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes that:
  1. The land at 101–115 Edgecliff Road, Woollahra (the Subject Site) comprises three Inter War apartment buildings identified as contributory items within the Woollahra Heritage Conservation Area under the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014.

  2. Development Application No. 38/2026 has been lodged for the Subject Site (the DA) and involves, among other things:

  1. demolition with partial retention of the existing Inter War flat buildings;
  2. excavation of two basement levels;
  3. construction of a six storey residential apartment building containing 29 apartments at an approximate cost of $36 million; and
  4. provision of 48 car parking spaces.

  1. According to the Heritage Impact Statement and related documentation prepared for the DA:

 

  1. the contributory value of the existing buildings primarily lies in their collective contribution to the streetscape and historic character of the Woollahra Heritage Conservation Area, particularly at the prominent intersection of Edgecliff Road and Adelaide Street; and
  2. the proposal involves removal of “substantial original fabric beyond the street facing facades”, resulting in a moderate to high physical impact to the existing building fabric, notwithstanding the proposed retention of the street facing facades.

  1. The buildings on the Subject Site are not individually listed heritage items.

  2. The extent of demolition, excavation and new construction has the potential to:

  1. irreversibly diminish the authenticity and integrity of the contributory buildings;
  2. erode the established Inter War streetscape character at the intersection of Edgecliff Road and Adelaide Street; and
  3. adversely affect the heritage significance of the broader Heritage Conservation Area.

  1. Council’s Community Strategic Plan includes Goal 1:
    “Encourage and facilitate high-quality planning and urban design outcomes and spaces.”

  2. Planning Priority 5 of the Woollahra Local Strategic Planning Statement (the LSP Statement) involves:
    “Conserving our rich and diverse heritage.”

  3. Action Item 28 from the LSP Statement is to:
    “Continue to proactively conserve and monitor heritage.”

  4. It endorsed the “Heritage GAP Analysis” in November 2021, including the ongoing action to:
    “Remain vigilant on development and threats to unlisted heritage - continue reviewing development applications and complying development certificates to minimise loss of unlisted heritage and issue Interim Heritage Orders under s25 of the New South Wales Heritage Act 1977. Ensure there are resources to undertake ad hoc heritage assessments in the event of a threat.”

  1. Resolves to:
  1. Request the General Manager to obtain urgent advice from Council’s heritage staff on whether an Interim Heritage Order (IHO) over the Subject Site (in whole or in part) is warranted.

  2. Request that this advice be reported back to Council as a matter of urgency.

The Motion was put and Lost.

Councillor Price asking:

  1. I refer to Council’s:

  1. Meeting of 22 September 2022, where it resolved to proceed with the sale of the road reserve adjoining 30 Wyuna Road, Point Piper (the Sale Site) for the purchase price of $2,993,636 (ex. GST); and

  2. Meeting of 8 May 2023, where it resolved to:

  1. Grant landowner’s consent for the lodgement of a Development Application for certain construction works on the Sale Site; and

  2. Provide that the Contract for Sale be conditioned so that no construction or removal of vegetation can commence on the Sale Site until after settlement is finalised and all costs have been paid by the owner of 30 Wyuna Rd, Point Piper.

  1. Can the General Manager please update the community on the current status of the sale and the DA.

Manager - Property & Projects in response:

Following Council’s resolution of 22 September 2022, the sale documentation for the portion of roadway at 30 Wyuna Road was finalised and issued to the owner for execution.

Although the owner paid the deposit of $299,363, they subsequently decided not to proceed with the purchase. As a result, Owner’s Consent could not be provided for any DA lodgement relating to works on the portion of roadway proposed for sale.

 

No building works associated with the building extension plans (considered at the Council meeting of 8 May 2023) have been undertaken. Only works permitted under the previously approved DA for the existing building, such as retaining walls, driveway works and stair access have occurred.

Late last year, the owner advised that they now wished to proceed with the purchase. The process was restarted and contracts have since been formally exchanged in accordance with Council’s 22 September 2022 resolution. Settlement is anticipated to occur within four to six months, during which time Council remains the legal owner of the land.

The owner has recently lodged a new DA that includes works on the portion of roadway still under Council ownership. They understand that the DA cannot be determined until the Planning Department receives formal Owner’s Consent from the landowner. At this stage, they are seeking only to commence the DA assessment process, not to obtain a determination. Once settlement has taken place and ownership has transferred, they will submit Owner’s Consent.

As Council remains the registered proprietor until settlement, Owner’s Consent cannot be issued unless Councillors specifically resolve to grant consent while the land is still under Council ownership. Council previously granted Owner’s Consent for a DA in May 2023 after contracts had been exchanged, but that was for a different and earlier design scheme.

The new DA will follow the standard assessment pathway, including referrals to all relevant internal departments for technical comments. However, while the assessment may commence, the DA cannot be determined until settlement is completed and the land is legally transferred to the owner.

Councillor Price asking:

I refer to the Community Notice from Transport for NSW dated January 2026 concerning investigation works for the proposed Woollahra Station within the small reserve above the rail corridor on Edgecliff Road, Woollahra (the Reserve).

Can the General Manager please confirm:

  1. The current ownership of the Reserve, its zoning and the land use(s) permitted under that zoning;

  2. If the Reserve is leased or licensed to Council and if so, the key terms and duration of any such lease or licence.

Manager - Property & Projects in response:

The small reserve located above the rail corridor on Edgecliff Road, Woollahra is owned by Transport for NSW. The reserve has a land area of approximately 1,827m².

The land is zoned SP2 Infrastructure and Council holds a licence from TfNSW to use the site at an annual fee of $52 (excl. GST). Council is responsible for maintaining the area, including tree maintenance, grass mowing, and the upkeep of low‑level lighting and a park bench for community use.

 

A/Team Leader - Strategic Planning & Place in response:

Under the Woollahra LEP 2014, roads are permissible without consent on the site.

With consent, the following uses are permissible:

  • Aquaculture;
  • Community facilities;
  • Environmental protection works;
  • Recreation areas; and
  • Any other purpose that is labelled on the land zoning map (for this site, the label is Rail Infrastructure Facilities).
