255/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council notes:

  1. Development application DA30/2021 proposed the following works at 780-786 New South Head Road Rose Bay (“the site”):
  1. the partial demolition of the existing residential flat building;
  2. site remediation;
  3. alterations and additions to an existing 2-3 storey residential flat building including:
  1. new enlarged side wings with flat roof forms; and
  2. an additional floor level partially within a proposed altered roof level presenting as 2 storeys to New South Head Road, 4 storeys to the rear and 3-4 storeys to the adjacent side properties.
  1. the proposed development involves 6 units consisting of 2 x 3 bedroom units at lower ground floor level, 2 x 3 bedroom units at ground floor level and 2 x 4 bedroom units split over Levels 1 and 2.
  2. two additional excavated basement levels to the southern section of the site and extending under the southern section of the existing building are proposed containing 12 resident car spaces, 1 motorcycle parking space, 7 vertical bicycle spaces parking, storage, services and 1 car wash bay/visitor car parking space.
  3. the reconstruction of the section of roof indicated as not being proposed to be demolished on the demolition plan to original details and the construction of new sections of roof to match reconstructed roof details.
  4. car lift to the south-eastern corner of the site accessed via an altered existing
  5. driveway crossover is proposed to provide vehicular access to the basement levels.
  6. a communal open space area and stone planters are proposed to the front section of the site.
  7. landscaping works.

  1. On 17 June 2021 Council refused consent for the proposal on six grounds including that the proposal involves excessive excavation contrary to Woollahra LEP 2014 and WDCP 2015. The applicant subsequently lodged an appeal of the Council’s determination.

  2. On 28 October 2021 the Land and Environment Court granted development consent for an amended proposal.

  3. Council required conditions to be imposed on the development consent to safeguard the safety of the existing structures and adjoining lands. These included requirements for:
  1. Demolition of buildings and structures must comply with Australian Standard AS 2601—2001: The Demolition of Structures;
  2. A professional engineer (structural engineer), to certifying the adequacy of the existing supporting structure to support the additional loads proposed; 
  3. Detailed professional engineering plans and/or specifications for all structural, hydrogeological and geotechnical works; 
  4. Geotechnical / Hydrogeological Monitoring Programs and adherence to the recommendations of the Geotechnical / Hydrogeological Monitoring Program; and 
  5. That the building be brought into total conformity with the BCA including current engineering requirements.

  1. Council was first advised on 16 February 2026 of the catastrophic building failure at the development that had occurred on 12 February 2026. The front bay and the central part of the front elevation to the dwelling had collapsed, taking with it internal floors and a portion of the roof.

  2. The Principal Certifier, Safe Work NSW and Building Commission Officers were previously alerted, attended the development and Orders were issued by Safe Work NSW to undertake immediate make safe recommendations to stabilise the building and formulate a solution for rectification works. A Written Direction Notice was also issued by the Principal Certifier for the development. 

  3. Councillor Price asking:

To the Director of Planning and Place. Can the Director please confirm:

  1. That the Unicorn Hotel, Paddington and its interiors are listed as a local heritage item in Schedule 5 of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014.

  2. That the Unicorn Hotel is located within the boundaries of the Paddington Heritage Conservation Area (HCA) and listed as a contributory item within the HCA.

  3. If any unauthorised works have been carried out at the Unicorn Hotel and if so, provide particulars of those works.

  4. If Council has issued any stop work orders to the owner of the Unicorn Hotel?

  5. What (if any) further action Council Officers and/or the owner of the Unicorn Hotel has taken with respect to any Stop Work Orders.

Manager - Strategic Planning & Place and other staff in response:

  1. This is correct. It is listed as ‘Unicorn Hotel and interiors’ item I689 in Schedule 5 of the Woollahra LEP 2014

  2. The Paddington HCA does not list contributory items. The wording of the section on contributory buildings implies that heritage items, by virtue of being items, are not contributory buildings. This is also reflected in other parts of the DCP, such as the Woollahra HCA. So, while the Unicorn Hotel does contribute to the significance of the Paddington HCA, it is not identified in the DCP under the formal designation of “contributory building” because it is instead a heritage item. 

  3. Demolition of all the existing floors (ground and first floor slabs), internal walls and internal stairs and the entire roof structure have been carried out without development consent where development consent was required. 

  4. Council has issued two (2) Development Control Orders to stop works at the Unicorn Hotel. 

  5. Council’s Compliance and Enforcement Officers have proactively undertaken follow up inspections of the site in relation to the Orders and have confirmed that the developer is in compliance with those Orders.

Councillor Witt asking:

  1. Will Council Staff be making a submission to the draft statewide Community Participation Plan and Discussion Paper to make the planning system faster and fairer? The consultation period is 8th April 2026 - 3rd June 2026. See https://www.nsw.gov.au/have-your-say/statewide-community-participation-plan

  2. Would Council Staff consider putting their submission on the Council website to help inform residents' submissions?
Some of the key changes proposed are very significant. They include:

  • Extending minimum consultation timeframes on state-level strategic planning initiatives like Region Plans and the State Plan from 45 days to 60 days.
  • Standardising the process for notification of Complying Development and giving neighbours 7 days’ notice before any works begin.
  • Standardising and reducing the number of local development application types that need to be exhibited by councils to those with the highest impact.

Manager - Strategic Planning & Place in response:

  1. Yes, staff are preparing a submission to the NSW Government’s draft state-wide Community Participation Plan and Discussion Paper, which are on exhibition from 8 April until 3 June 2026.

    It is intended that the draft submission will be reported to the Environmental Planning Committee of 4 May 2026 and then considered by Council at its meeting on 25 May 2026. If endorsed, the submission will be sent to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure by the closing date of 3 June 2026.

  1. Council staff agree that there are some significant and negative implications proposed within the exhibition documents.

    Accordingly, staff have already updated Council’s Your Say webpage to refer to the public exhibition, so that the information is readily available to our community.  We are in the process of writing to local community groups to advise them of the exhibition of the draft state-wide Community Participation Plan and Discussion Paper.

    Once the draft submission is available, we will include that on Councils website. Once the submission has been adopted by Council we will then update the website.

Councillor Witt asking:

  1. Is Council Staff aware of recent advice re managing dewatering impacts from the NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI) with respect to the 23-31 Dover Road State Significant Development Application (SSDA)?

The DCCEEW advice recommended that in order to properly assess potential cumulative groundwater level drawdown against the NSW Aquifer Interference Policy, DPHI should require an update to the 23-31 Dover Road SSDA groundwater model that includes water extraction from the development at 6-8 Richmond Road, Rose Bay (DA92/2019)?

The advice also said that “an alternative strategy to manage cumulative impacts is to ensure project works (like dewatering) do not occur at the same time, with the existing work approval taking priority.”

In light of this advice, will Council Staff require DAs proposing dewatering for excavation to:

  1. Prepare hydrogeological and geotechnical reports that make reference to or model water extraction from DAs that are currently under construction or have recently been approved in and around the settlement areas of Rose Bay and Double Bay?
and/or

  1. Ensure that construction work involving dewatering in and around the Rose Bay and Double Bay settlement areas is staged so that dewatering does not occur on more than one property at the same time?

With respect to 2 above, will the Council need to request permission from DPHI to stage construction activity in order to minimise the impacts of dewatering on settlement and the aquifer in and around the settlement areas of Rose Bay and Double Bay?

  1. Can Council Staff confirm whether integrated developments need to be assessed against the criteria in the “Minimum requirements for building site groundwater investigations and reporting (Information for developers and consultants, Department of Planning and Environment October 2022)? 
To put this question into context, reference was made to the above cited document in an EI Australia Geotechnical Opinion Letter on Groundwater Considerations for the 2A–6 Conway Avenue SSDA (SSD-101842729).

The EI Australia Opinion Letter recommended that “further groundwater investigations are carried out at the Site in line with DPIE’s Minimum Requirements for Building Site Groundwater Investigations and Reporting 2022, including but not limited to installation of additional groundwater wells, long term groundwater level monitoring (3 months minimum), groundwater seepage analyses and preparation of a dewatering management plan.
 
Monitoring and reporting for the works mentioned are expected to take a total of 4-5months”?

Are all DAs requesting dewatering for excavation expected to demonstrate how they comply with the DPE's Minimum Requirements?

  1. Can Council Staff clarify the role of WaterNSW with respect to referrals for dewatering requests for excavation?

The above advice from DCCEEW also said that “While a key concern for the submission, settlement impacts on buildings are considered outside the scope of the Water Management Act 2000 for advice from DCCEEW Water. The assessment of geotechnical risk, structural impacts on neighbours, and hydrogeological drawdown falls to the consent authority (Council/DPHI), not WaterNSW.”

Does the above advice align with Council's understanding of WaterNSW's role?


Manager - Development Assessment in response (bold):

  1. Is Council Staff aware of recent advice re managing dewatering impacts from the NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI) with respect to the 23-31 Dover Road State Significant Development Application (SSDA)?
The DCCEEW advice recommended that in order to properly assess potential cumulative groundwater level drawdown against the NSW Aquifer Interference Policy, DPHI should require an update to the 23-31 Dover Road SSDA groundwater model that includes water extraction from the development at 6-8 Richmond Road, Rose Bay (DA92/2019)?

The advice also said that “an alternative strategy to manage cumulative impacts is to ensure project works (like dewatering) do not occur at the same time, with the existing work approval taking priority.”

Council’s Planning Team including the relevant Technical Referrals Teams (i.e. Development Engineering and Drainage) are aware of the advice/information from NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI) relating to the SSD Application at No 23-31 Dover Road, Rose Bay.

In light of this advice, will Council Staff require DAs proposing dewatering for excavation to:

  1. Prepare hydrogeological and geotechnical reports that make reference to or model water extraction from DAs that are currently under construction or have recently been approved in and around the settlement areas of Rose Bay and Double Bay?
and/or

Council’s guidelines and requirements for Geotechnical and Hydrogeological Reports to accompany a DA are set out in Attachment 6 of Council’s DA Guideline (see link below). 

https://www.woollahra.nsw.gov.au/files/assets/public/v/3/plans-policies-publications/da-guide-attachment-6-geotechnical-and-hydrogeological-report.pdf

 
  1. Ensure that construction work involving dewatering in and around the Rose Bay and Double Bay settlement areas is staged so that dewatering does not occur on more than one property at the same time?
With respect to 2 above, will the Council need to request permission from DPHI to stage construction activity in order to minimise the impacts of dewatering on settlement and the aquifer in and around the settlement areas of Rose Bay and Double Bay?
 
The staging of any construction work will only be required if:

  • it is recommended and required in any submitted Geotechnical and Hydrogeological Report(s) and subsequently conditioned in any DA consent
  • it is required by the General Terms of Approval for dewatering provided by Water NSW

  1. Can Council Staff confirm whether integrated developments need to be assessed against the criteria in the “Minimum requirements for building site groundwater investigations and reporting (Information for developers and consultants, Department of Planning and Environment October 2022)?
To put this question into context, reference was made to the above cited document in an EI Australia Geotechnical Opinion Letter on Groundwater Considerations for the 2A–6 Conway Avenue SSDA (SSD-101842729).

The EI Australia Opinion Letter recommended that “further groundwater investigations are carried out at the Site in line with DPIE’s Minimum Requirements for Building Site Groundwater Investigations and Reporting 2022, including but not limited to installation of additional groundwater wells, long term groundwater level monitoring (3 months minimum), groundwater seepage analyses and preparation of a dewatering management plan. Monitoring and reporting for the works mentioned are expected to take a total of 4-5months”?

Are all DAs requesting dewatering for excavation expected to demonstrate how they comply with the DPE's Minimum Requirements?

Development Applications (including Integrated Development) lodged with Council are not required to be assessed against the “Minimum requirements for building site groundwater investigations and reporting (Information for developers and consultants, Department of Planning and Environment October 2022)? This is a requirement set out by the DPE for assessing its SSD’s.

 

As stated above, Council’s guidelines and requirements for Geotechnical and Hydrogeological Reports to accompany a DA are set out in Attachment 6 of Council’s DA Guideline (see link below). 

https://www.woollahra.nsw.gov.au/files/assets/public/v/3/plans-policies-publications/da-guide-attachment-6-geotechnical-and-hydrogeological-report.pdf

As such, any DA submitted with Council will be assessed against its own criteria and not the DPEs requirements (i.e. Minimum requirements for building site groundwater investigations and reporting (Information for developers and consultants, Department of Planning and Environment October 2022).


  1. Can Council Staff clarify the role of WaterNSW with respect to referrals for dewatering requests for excavation? 
The above advice from DCCEEW also said that “While a key concern for the submission, settlement impacts on buildings are considered outside the scope of the Water Management Act 2000 for advice from DCCEEW Water. The assessment of geotechnical risk, structural impacts on neighbours, and hydrogeological drawdown falls to the consent authority (Council/DPHI), not WaterNSW.”

Under the Water Management Act 2000, any Development Application which involves dewatering is constituted as Integrated Development and requires the referral and concurrence (i.e. General Terms of Approval) of Water NSW.

Does the above advice align with Council's understanding of WaterNSW's role?

Yes.

260/2026 Resolved without debate:

THAT Council:

  1. In accordance with section 178 (1) (b) of the NSW Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 (Regulation) having considered all tender submissions received for the lease and operation of Dunbar House, Watsons Bay and having regard to all the circumstances, decline to accept any tender submissions on the basis that, while the tenders demonstrate varying strengths, none of the submissions, as tendered, achieve an optimal balance between commercial return, capital investment, operational capability, and long term sustainability required for the lease of this Council owned asset and that further negotiation is required to achieve an outcome that is in Council’s best interests.

  2. In accordance with section 178 (3) (e) of the NSW Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, resolve to enter into negotiations with Ripples Watsons Bay Pty Ltd, as part of Prophetable Hospitality Pty Ltd, trading as SRG Hospitality (ABN 40 694 322 695), with a view to entering into a contract for the lease and operation of Dunbar House, Watsons Bay, on the basis that:

  • Ripples Watsons Bay submitted the highest‑ranked tender when assessed against the qualitative and risk‑based evaluation criteria;
  • the proposal includes a significant commitment to tenant funded capital investment and demonstrated operational capability in comparable venues; and
  • negotiation is required to improve the commercial terms, including base rent and turnover rent provisions, to achieve a financially sustainable outcome for Council.

  1. Should negotiations with Ripples Watsons Bay Pty Ltd not result in an acceptable outcome, authorise the General Manager to enter into negotiations with the second highest ranked tenderer, Catering HQ Services Pty Ltd (ABN 11 646 445 463), in accordance with section 178 (3) (e) of the Regulation.

  2. Ensure that any negotiated lease includes a binding commitment to undertake capital works at a value no less than that proposed in the respective tender submission, subject to the receipt of all necessary approvals, including development consent where required.

  3. Receive a further report following the completion of negotiations referred to in paragraphs (B), (C), and (D) above.

The Motion was put and Carried.

228/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes the large volume of correspondence being sent by the Woollahra community to Councillors in relation to concerns with the NSW Government's housing policies, in particular the Low and Mid-Rise Housing Policy (LMR Policy).

  2. Thanks the community for their ongoing interest and advocacy in relation to the NSW Government's LMR Policy, in particular the concerns raised regarding Rose Bay, Double Bay, Woollahra and Paddington.

  3. Notes the significant advocacy undertaken by Council and Councillors in response to the NSW Government's policies, in particular to the LMR Policy and the State-led rezoning of Woollahra and Edgecliff, including as set out in the background to this motion.

  4. Thanks Council staff for their ongoing work in response to the significant housing reforms, imposed by the NSW Government without adequate consultation with councils and the community.

 

  1. Notes the concerns held by Council and the community regarding the lack of strategic planning associated with the LMR Policy, and that our advocacy efforts have been consistently ignored, including the NSW Government’s complete failure to consider and address the:
  1. Short term potential impacts of LMR Policy related construction and excavation, including geotechnical, hydrological and hydrogeological issues on surrounding properties;
  2. Long term concerns about poor design, environmental outcomes and pressures of increased population on current infrastructure; 
  3. Complete disregard for heritage and local character;
  4. Total lack of assessment and planning for transport, health, recreation, traffic and services to support an increased population; 
  5. Concerns that councils have with LMR Policy applications that are assessed through the State Significant Development pathway, where local controls in development control plans do not have any weight; and
  6. Ad-hoc nature of Housing Delivery Authority applications that are not assessed under any cohesive strategic planning framework. 

  1. Notes that a significant number of relatively affordable units are being replaced by luxury units enabled by the LMR Policy.

  2. Notes that  while Council is closely monitoring alternative proposals to LMR planning schemes, Woollahra Council has received no indication that such a proposition would be attractive to or agreed by the NSW Government, and has instead received a very strong indication that LMR policy changes will not be considered.

  3. Notes that while a government can elect to change its mind, and that a policy on the shelf could have value in such an event, this is not a low-cost exercise to carry out.  Resources are already near capacity in managing the State-led rezoning around Woollahra Station, and in managing the impact of LMR and other NSW Government planning reforms as they apply to Woollahra Council.

  4. Notes the following information on the NSW Government’s five year housing target and recent housing delivery data for the Woollahra Local Government Area (LGA), that:
  1. The NSW Government’s five year housing target of 1,900 new dwellings to be delivered for the period of July 2024 to June 2029 was introduced with no consultation with Council or the community;
  2. Notwithstanding the completion targets, Council is not responsible for constructing homes but provides an assessment function for the market to do so;
  3. 188 new dwellings were constructed during the 2024/2025 financial year; and 
  4. There were 959 new dwellings approved in the Woollahra LGA during the 2024/2025 financial year, where construction has not been completed. 

  1. Notes that Council's data on the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure’s (DPHI) Council League Table shows that:
  1. The average approval timeframe has significantly reduced over the past two years with the number of assessment days:
  1. reduced by 26.7% to 129 days for 2024/2025; and
  2. reduced by a further 27% to 94 days for 2025/2026 (up to March 2026), well below the NSW Government’s target of 105 days. 
  1. The number of medium/high density development applications and total development value demonstrates that Council is making a significant contribution to the housing delivery pipeline with the data for the 2025/2026 financial year to 30 March 2026 showing that the Woollahra LGA is: 
  1. Third in NSW in terms of total development cost, with $585M; and

 

  1. Tenth in NSW in terms of development applications lodged for medium/high density development with 88 applications.
  1. The strong figures above have been delivered despite Council being the 7th densest LGA in NSW with 77.8% of dwellings being medium or high density (compared to 46% for Greater Sydney).

  1. Notes the Edgecliff Commercial Centre Planning and Urban Design Strategy and the Double Bay Centre Planning and Urban Design Strategy:
  1. Will deliver 615 and 300 net additional dwellings respectively;
  2. Have both been submitted to the DPHI on 27 February 2025 and 5 May 2025 respectively; and
  3. That there has been no response from the DPHI in relation to either.

  1. Notes the letter received on 23 April 2026 from the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces refusing Council’s request to remove Double Bay and Rose Bay Centres from the LMR Policy, despite concerns about issues such as potential hydrological and flooding risks that were not appropriately investigated prior to the policy’s commencement; and

  2. Resolves to write to the Premier of NSW, the Member for Vaucluse, the Member for Sydney, and the Federal Member for Wentworth in order to provide them with a copy of this resolution.

The Motion was put and Carried.

(Councillor Witt/Councillor Torsten)

273/2026 Recommendation:

THAT Council: 

  1. Note the report regarding development in moderate to high-risk flooding areas.

  2. Note Council's strong concerns that the State Government’s Low and Mid Rise (LMR) Policy did not appropriately investigate flooding risks prior to the policy’s commencement.

  3. Request that staff proceed to undertake new flood studies for the Rose Bay and Double Bay catchments.

  4. Acknowledge that new flood studies will take at least 12 months to complete and development applications (DAs) are currently being assessed in the flood prone areas of Rose Bay and Double Bay.
     
  5. Request staff consider whether the scenario modelling for overland flood behaviour can be fast-tracked or staged so interim results are available sooner.

  6. Notes staff frequently require site-specific flood studies for LMR DAs in Rose Bay and Double Bay where appropriate, and requests staff consider requiring site-specific flood studies for all LMR DAs in Rose Bay and Double Bay in accordance with "Understanding and managing flood risk: Flood risk management guideline FB01" (DPE, 30 June 2023), that "incorporate an extended area to include upstream, downstream and adjacent properties."

  7. Note that staff have commissioned a study into the cumulative effect of LMR developments on the groundwater conditions of Rose Bay and Double Bay separately to these flood studies.

  8. Requests the General Manager provide a summary of the controls in the DA Guide, LEP 2014 and DCP 2015 in comparison to "Understanding and managing flood risk: Flood risk management guideline FB01”, as late correspondence to the Council meeting of 25 May 2026.

The Motion was put and Carried.

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, is satisfied that the applicant has demonstrated under Part 4.6 of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 that compliance with the Floor Space Ratio development standard under Clause 4.4E of Woollahra LEP 2014 is unreasonable or unnecessary in the circumstances, and there are sufficient environmental planning grounds to justify the contravention of the development standard.

AND

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, grant development consent to Development Application No. 375/2025/1 for alterations and additions (to the approved CDC No. 137/25/01 for a new dwelling house and pool) including a new basement level for two cars, plant room, storage and internal stair access on land at 27 Lennox Street BELLEVUE HILL, subject to the conditions of consent in Attachment 2. 

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions).

326/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Endorse the proposed amendments to the current Code of Meeting Practice (the Code), as included in Attachment 1 to this report, for the purpose of placing the draft revised Code (incorporating any changes resolved by Council at this meeting) on public exhibition for a minimum of 28 days, subject to the following amendments to the following items outlined in Attachment 1:
  1. Item number 2 to be removed.
  2. Item number 4, delete the words "as the item will be formally debated in the actual Council or Committee Meeting, once the Public Forum has closed".
  3. Item number 6, to be adopted as printed, however during the exhibition period request staff consider implementing guidelines on petitions similar to the City of Sydney.
  4. Item number 7, clause 3.3.1 be changed to require late correspondence to be submitted by 10am of the day of the meeting and that staff shall endeavour to distribute late correspondence by midday on the day of the meeting to allow Councillors and public greater time to review and respond to the agenda.
  5. Item number 7, amend the words "As a minimum, any late correspondence must include a responsible person’s name, contact number and or email address." to read "As a minimum, any late correspondence must include a responsible person’s name, contact number, email address, residential suburb and LGA address or where relevant from a business, the business suburb of the correspondent".

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Dixson, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Price, Councillor Regan, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Zeltzer

Note:

(Councillor Dixson)

279/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council: 

 

  1. Notes the information and clarification provided in this Mayoral Minute on the Woollahra Preschool.

  2. Reiterates its commitment to providing ongoing quality and affordable childcare through the Woollahra Preschool, as resolved on 23 March 2026.

  3. Thank staff, parents and teachers for attending the community forum on 13 May 2026 about Woollahra Preschool.

  4. Request the General Manager provide further information to Councillors at the Extraordinary Council meeting to be held on Tuesday 9 June 2026, on the NSW Government’s Expanding Quality Access Program fund (the Grant) in relation to the timing of when applications are due and when grant applications are likely to be approved or otherwise. This is due to the fact that the closing date for the Grant has now been pushed to 30 November 2026, with little clarity available on when such applications might be determined. 

  5. Requests the General Manager undertake a survey of all currently enrolled families and all families on the active waitlist for the Woollahra Preschool in order to gain the views of families with the survey to include, as a minimum, the following matters:
    1. A brief factual summary of the proposals covering both Council's position and the key concerns raised by families. 
    2. Views on expansion of the preschool.
    3. What form of expansion would be supported.
    4. Views on Council applying for the Grant mentioned in part D above.
    5. Affordability.
    6. What is valued most about the Woollahra Preschool by families.

  6. Requests that the results of the Survey set out in Part E be presented to Council before any decision is made to continue with the Grant application. 

  7. Requests the General Manager undertake appropriate work to identify if and how Council might be able to finance expansion of the existing preschool service at the current location.

  8. Requests that the General Manager report to an August 2026 Committee and or Council meeting on the following:
    1. The results of the survey, as set out in Part E of this Mayoral Minute. 
    2. The results of the information identified in Part G of this Mayoral Minute.
    3. Information regarding the number of licensed placements at comparable preschools, as presented at the community forum on 13 May 2026.
    4. Information relating to the timing around building and related works that would be required in order to expand the preschool service.
    5. In relation to the extension of operation from 41 to 48 weeks a year (assuming Council resolves to proceed with the Grant application after considering the results of the information set out above:
    6. Confirm if the additional 7 weeks per year is optional for parents and that parents will only pay for the weeks used, in addition to details around when (if feasible), parents will need to notify the preschool about whether or not their children will attend the additional 7 weeks per year.
    7. Whether, if a family chooses not to use the additional 7 weeks per year, this space can be filled by another child during that period.
    8. Further explanation about the possible impact of changing Councils funding source for the preschool, if Council is approved for, and resolves to accept, the Grant (referred to in Part ,D of this Mayoral Minute), including that Council become approved to administer the Child Care Subsidy (CCS) by 1 July 2028, and that parents would need to register for CCS.

  9. Notes that a traffic and pedestrian safety assessment would be required for any expansion scenario given that the current site already is currently licensed for 80 children per day, and any expansion of the preschool might extend the preschool to approximately 140 children per day.

  10. Notes the ways the community can continue to engage with Council on this matter, including: 
    1. Speaking at Committee Public Forums, subject to application as per the instructions included on Councils web site;
    2. Submitting written feedback on the draft 2026-2027 budget and Operational Plan by 31 May 2026; 
    3. Providing late correspondence in relation to this issue at upcoming Committee and or Council meetings where the preschool is to be discussed; and 
    4. Participating in the survey as set out in paragraph E.

 

  1. Requests that the General Manager provide a copy of this motion, including the discussion included below to:
    1. Current families and families on the waitlist for Woollahra Preschool;
    2. The attendees of the community forum on 13 May 2026;
    3. Any submitters of late correspondence in relation to this issue at this Council meeting;
    4. Participants of any formal Council Committee Public Forums in relation to this issue; and
    5. Woollahra Preschool staff.

The Motion was put and Carried.
 
Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

Note: Seconder not required for a Mayoral Minute.

(Councillor Dixson)

306/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes the updates contained in this Mayoral Minute in relation to Paddington’s Victoria Barracks (the Barracks).

  2. Reaffirms its endorsement of the Guiding Principles in relation to the Barracks.

  3. Requests the Mayor write to the Assistant Minister for Defence, the Hon Peter Khalil MP to:
  1. Thank the Assistant Minister for including Council in the ‘Round Table’ meeting of 8 May 2026 (the Round Table);
  2. Request that Council continue to be involved in any future deliberations and ongoing consultation;
  3. Reiterate Council’s concerns raised at the Round Table;
  4. Call for the need to ensure binding heritage protections and planning controls are developed and in place prior to any divestment;
  5. Consider exploring enacting bespoke legislation to protect the Barracks and establish a public Authority or Trust to manage the future use of the Barracks; and
  6. Seek transparency regarding the timeline, scope and structure of further community input and feedback (in addition to and separate to the ‘Expression of Interest’ process).

 

  1. Request the General Manager includes the Barracks as a standing priority agenda item for the Oxford Street and Paddington Working Party (OS&PWP) and that regular meetings of the OS&PWP are convened.

  2. Utilise Council’s communication channels to actively promote and keep the community informed of developments.

  3. Provides a copy of the above correspondence to the Member for Vaucluse, Kellie Sloane MP, Member for Wentworth, Allegra Spender MP, the Member for Sydney, Alex Greenwich MP and the Rt Hon Clover Moore AO Lord Mayor of Sydney.

  4. Support a coordinated and collaborative approach to advocacy with other councils, including Mosman, the City of Sydney, Parramatta, and Borough of Queenscliff, for the protection of defence land and its retention in public ownership, the Guiding Principles as adopted by Council, and encourage community participation in the Commonwealth consultation process, including submissions to the Department of Defence and the Department of Finance.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

Note: 
Late correspondence was tabled by Emilio Andari (Council's Manager Engineering Services).

Councillor Regan asking:

I refer to the QWN I submitted on 11 June 2024 (Attachment 1 and below) and thank staff for the response: 

Could Council please provide an update in relation to the Notice of Motion that was passed on 15 November 2023 in relation to the Park'n'Pay app (see Attachment 2 and link below). 

https://woollahra.infocouncil.biz/Open/2023/11/CO_20231115_AGN_AT.PDF#page247

 


Specifically could Council:

  1. confirm that the actions contemplated in item B and item C of the resolution were initiated and whether any feedback was received as a result; and

  2. provide an estimate of timing for production of the report contemplated in item A of the resolution; and

  3. provide an update on the current status of the Park n Pay app including as to whether it is still in operation, whether Council is still utilising it, how extensively it is used by Council and whether there is any update from the State Government as to the ongoing status of operation and use of the Park n Pay app.
 
Manager Engineering & Services in response:

Council staff have commenced preliminary investigations on the types of smart parking systems in which the public may use to pay for on-street parking. This investigation also considers the current utilisation of Park’n’Pay and the costs/benefits associated with this application. To complete the investigation and prepare a report on the various types of smart parking systems will take approximately 3-4 months.

Discussions between Council staff and other Councils on whether the Park’n’Pay application is still being served within their communities have been raised and it was noted that many of the other Councils in which have the Park’n’Pay application, still use this application. A decision has not yet been made by NSW Government on when Park’n’Pay will no longer be a government initiative. A request put forward from the Councils part of SSROC has not been made as yet, however at the last roundtable event held between Council staff and NSW Government representatives, the insights from various Councils raised were;

  • Clear support for continuation of Park’nPay
  • Use of parking data from the Park’nPay app informs broader council opportunities
  • Importance of new accessibility features
  • One single application preference between LGAs to help customers
  • Several councils have parking strategies tied to Park’nPay
  • Uncertainty regarding future of Park’n'Pay limiting ability to get next horizon of greater onboarding

As for the Woollahra Municipality, the Park’n’Pay application is still effectively utilised. Since the launch of the application to Woollahra in 2022 the use of this application has been steady with an approximation of 10% for all transactions made through Park’n’Pay for our metered parking areas. 

Councillor Regan asking - Follow on Question:

A resident has been in touch with the office of Kellie Sloane MP Member for Vaucluse, NSW Liberal Leader, NSW Leader of the Opposition in relation to the Park n Pay app and has been provided with the following response:

(Email extract from the office of Kellie Sloane MP, Member for Vaucluse)
Thank you for your email regarding the limited parking availability in the area and the current status of the Park’nPay app with Kellie’s office.
 

 


The Minister for Service and Digital Government has recently provided a response to Kellie following the representations she made on your behalf. Please find the response attached for your reference.
 
As the Minister states, the previous Liberals and National Government initiated the app. In the 2023 Budget, the current Government considered discontinuing the app but received criticism regarding this decision ultimately meaning the app has remained.
 
I hope the information provided is helpful. I would welcome your thoughts once you have had the opportunity to review it, particularly if you have any questions or would like to discuss the matter further.
  
Please let me know if there is anything further we can do to assist.
 
(Email extract from the office of The Hon. Jihad Dib MP, Minister for Customer Service and Digital Government)

Thank you for your correspondence on behalf of your constituent, XXX , regarding the Park’nPay application and its status.
 
To clarify, under this Government, Park’nPay has not been discontinued and remains operational. This is despite the previous government developing the app in a manner that attracted serious criticism from the NSW Audit Office but failed to provide any ongoing funding.
 
While Park’nPay has provided useful functionality in specific contexts, responsibility for parking management and enforcement sits with local councils. Councils are not dependent on a NSW Government platform and can continue to implement parking management approaches, including digital solutions available in the market, that best meet local needs.
 
Thank you again for raising this matter.

The resident is now inquiring as to whether Council can use the Park'n'Pay app to manage the 10 minutes free parking location at St Stephen's daycare centre in Bellevue Hill as a “free parking + time limited” location on the Park n Pay database, a matter that has been raised with Council staff in the past but has not been actioned.

The request is to install a sign stating that any vehicle parked in this location must use the Park'n'Pay app to park at that location to permit better tracking of the 10 minutes free parking and enforcement by Council rangers, limiting the need for chalk marking. Can Council staff provide a response as to whether this is achievable in this location and, if so, when this may be actioned?


Manager - Engineering Services in response:

Answers provided as late correspondence.

Note:

Councillor Jarvis asking:

Noting:
 
  1. That in the Council agenda 8.12.25 it was stated 'In May 2020, the NSW Department of Planning, Industry and Environment (DPIE) and Transport for NSW (TfNSW) launched the Streets as Shared Spaces program to help local councils create more public space in response to COVID-19' .... 'The proposed O'Sullivan Road Recreation Path aligns with the strategies, goals and objectives identified in the following State and Council Policies and Procedures:
 
  • Woollahra 2032
  • Woollahra Active Transport Plan (2023)
  • Woollahra Disability Inclusion Action Plan
  • NSW Government's Future Transport 2056
  • NSW Government’s Principal Bicycle Network.
  
In December 2020 time TfNSW had released a Cycle Design Toolbox https://standards.transport.nsw.gov.au/search-standard-specific/?id=TBA%20-%200001800:2022 s3.4.3 headed 'Main Design Consideration states that 'Shared paths are not suitable in the following environments...locations with high bicycle or  pedestrian activity, sections with relatively high cycling speeds.....The desired minimum width of a shared path is 4.0m allowing for safe overtaking and pedestrian interactions. Wider paths should be considered in environments where...higher numbers of people walking of cycling are expected ...' Yet that was not noted in policy implications or apparently discounted.
 
  1. Council engaged specialist consultants, Northrop Consulting Engineers, to prepare the concept design and Review of Environmental Factors for the O'Sullivan Road Recreation Path.
 
  1. The design makes provision of a shared path along O'Sullivan Road where localised road narrowing exists, and a shared path through the Woollahra Golf Course.
 
  1. That council was advised at its meeting that the shared path will narrow to 2.4m where EV charging stations will be installed and 3 metres where it is shared through the Golf Course.
 
Please advise:
 
  1. Did the consultants have regard to the TfNSW Cycle Design Toolbox? If not, why not?
 
  1. What was the agreed project cost to be charged by Northrop as consultants and/or how much has been charged to date and how much is expected to be paid?
 
  1. Is that funded/ to be funded out of the $4m for the SRV?
 
  1. What justification is provided for not ensuring the path is a minimum width of 4m given it is to be shared by pedestrian, runners, bikes and, on the golf course, on occasion, also cars, trucks and vans?

 


Manager - Engineering Services in response:

Answers provided as late correspondence.

322/2026:

THAT Council:

  1. Reaffirms our unanimous condemnation of the senseless and deplorable terrorist act which took place beside Bondi Beach on Sunday 14 December 2025 targeting members of Sydney's Jewish community.

  2. Acknowledges that the highest priority for Woollahra Council is to ensure the security and welfare of its residents within its Local Government Area (LGA) and to highlight potential dangers when visiting public spaces in adjacent areas such as Bondi -- Australia's most internationally recognised beach -- within the Waverley LGA.

  3. Acknowledge that the coloured concrete blocks lining Campbell Parade and Queen Elizabeth Drive (Image 2091) create a false sense of security for pedestrians and beachgoers walking along the Bondi Beach Promenade from the possible threat of an intentional vehicle assault (IVA) similar to those that have occurred in Tel Aviv (16 killed and 27 injured on 6 July 1989), along the Nice beach promenade (86 killed and 458 injured on 14 July 2016), at the Berlin Christmas markets (12 killed and 48 injured on 19 December 2016), on the Bourke Street mall in Melbourne (six killed and 27 injured on 20 January 2017), on the Barcelona pedestrian mall (14 killed and 101 injured on 17 August 2017), in Toronto, Canada (10 killed and 15 injured on 23 April 2018) and in many other cities around the world. 

  4. Acknowledges our concern that any vehicle up to 3m wide can access the pedestrian footpath from the entrance to the Queen Elizabeth Drive parking area and drive down between the mural wall and the skate park (Image 2090) and baseball court (Image 2093) then the full length of the Bondi Beach Promenade completely unimpeded by any concrete block or traffic control device. Unauthorised vehicle access is facilitated by a driveway leading onto the footpath near the Campbell Parade roundabout.

  5. Acknowledges our concern that there is a 2.55m gap in the concrete blocks (Image 2094) at the northeastern end of the promenade which is sufficiently wide enough to drive an average sized car through. Any vehicle unable to exit would be able to reverse the full length of the promenade and potentially create further carnage. The raised speed bump near the Ramsgate Avenue roundabout provides level access to the Bondi Beach Promenade where the line of concrete blocks finishes.

  6. Acknowledges that the incidents of worldwide intentional vehicle assaults causing mass casualty events has risen sharply since 2000 according to the Global Terrorism Database. Perpetrators are inspired by a range of terrorist ideologies or have extremist views, criminal intent, or mental health issues.

  7. Requests that Woollahra Mayor Sarah Dixson writes to Waverley Mayor William Nemish formally detailing the above concerns and urging that the coloured concrete blocks be positioned in such a way as to effectively prevent unauthorised vehicle access to the Bondi Beach Promenade as a matter of urgency. One assumes that this was Waverley Council's original intent when purchasing the numerous concrete blocks. 

 


The Motion was put and Lost.

Late correspondence was tabled by Adrienne Tuart, Amy Denmeade, Andy Rouse, Anthony Shakinovsky, Carmen McLoughlin, David Fisher, David Jacobs, Debbie Seidler, Double Bay Residents’ Association, Elaine Newland, Georgina Clark, Jacqueline Comino, Jacquie Hilmer, Joe Tweg, Joyanne Wilson, Kathy Meyer and Kay Smith.

(Councillor Jarvis/Councillor Torsten)

318/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Note the report regarding development in moderate to high-risk flooding areas;

  2. Note Councils’ strong concerns that the State Government’s Low and Mid Rise (LMR) Policy did not appropriately investigate flooding risks prior to the policy’s commencement; and

  3. Request that staff proceed to undertake new flood studies for the Rose Bay and Double Bay catchments.

  4. Acknowledge that new flood studies will take at least 12 months to complete and development applications (DAs) are currently being assessed in the flood prone areas of Rose Bay and Double Bay.

  5. Request staff consider whether the scenario modelling for overland flood behaviour can be fast-tracked or staged so interim results are available sooner.

  6. Notes staff frequently require site-specific flood studies for LMR DAs in Rose Bay and Double Bay where appropriate, and requests staff consider requiring site-specific flood studies for all LMR DAs in Rose Bay and Double Bay in accordance with "Understanding and managing flood risk: Flood risk management guideline FB01" (DPE, 30 June 2023), that "incorporate an extended area to include upstream, downstream and adjacent properties."

  7. Note that staff have commissioned a study into the cumulative effect of LMR developments on the groundwater conditions of Rose Bay and Double Bay separately to these flood studies.

  8. Requests the General Manager provide a summary of the controls in the DA Guide, LEP 2014 and DCP 2015 in comparison to "Understanding and managing flood risk: Flood risk management guideline FB01”, as late correspondence to the Council meeting of 25 May 2026.

The Motion was put and Carried.
 
Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

THAT Council: 

  1. Note the submissions received in relation to the Draft Concept Design for O'Sullivan Road Recreation Path that was placed on public exhibition from 23 February to 23 March 2026.

  2. Endorse the Concept Design for O'Sullivan Road Recreation Path, as presented in Attachment 1, subject to a further investigation of:

  1. Determining the location of the proposed raised pedestrian crossing, or other pedestrian calming devices.
  2. Line marking on the shared path, to match Newcastle Street & Old South Head Road.
  3. A reduction in the speed limit to improve the safety of all road users.
  4. Implementing automatic pedestrian light timing at the crossing of Old South Head Road and O’Sullivan Road intersection on Saturdays to assist those observing the Sabbath.
  5. Installation of wheel stops at the Easts Rugby Club car park to prevent vehicle overhang onto the new shared pathway. 
  6. The inclusion of lighting for the new separated and shared paths; and if not financially viable, install conduit to future-proof the project.
  7. Provide power to the Old South Head Road bus stop (near the intersection with O’Sullivan Road) for the installation of an advertising bus shelter. Revenue generated from this advertising opportunity to be held in reserve for maintenance and future upgrades of the shared path on O’Sullivan Road, New South Head Road, Old South Head Road and Newcastle Street.
  8. Adjust the traffic lane away from the kerb, on the residential side of the street, outside 217, 219, 221 & 223 O’Sullivan Road. Noting potential additional parking loss on the golf course side of the street.
  9. The inclusion of an access ramp to the shared path at the Latimer Road roundabout.
  10. The design of the fence from Latimer Road to the Woollahra Golf Club car park is not to exceed the current height.
  11. Modify the shared driveway and path on the golf course near Powell Road to allow vehicles to safely open and close the gate without obstructing path users.
  12. Ensuring the load limit of the shared pathway on the golf course can accommodate truck movements where required, so as not to impact the club’s operations.
  13. Investigate changing the street line marking to narrow the traffic lane in order to calm traffic.
  14. During detailed design that staff seek to maximise the width of the shared path where practicable.
  1. Request Council staff to refer the detailed design to the Inclusion Advisory Committee (IAC), before reporting the final design to the Local Transport Forum and Finance, Community and Services Committee.

  2. Proceed with detailed design and procurement for the construction of the O'Sullivan Road Recreation Path, noting that the changes in part 2 will be determined through a further investigation.

  3. Note that Council staff will continue to explore funding opportunities from NSW Government and the Australian Government to implement the project.

320/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Not endorse the Construction Traffic and Pedestrian Management Plan (CTPMP - Reference: 24.345r05v13) for the State Significant Development of property No.136-148 New South Head Road, Edgecliff.

  2. Approve the Works Zone in Darling Point Road, within the existing ‘No Stopping’ zone along the property frontage for a distance of 28 metres operating 7am-6pm Monday to Friday and 8am-1pm Saturday for all construction stages. 

  3. Approve the following changes for structural works stage, only:
  1. Install a second Works Zone within the existing bus zone in Darling Point Road, for a distance of 20 metres operating 7am-6pm Monday to Friday and 8am-1pm Saturday.
  2. Realign the existing Barrier (BL2) line on the approach to the intersection of Darling Point Road and New South Head Road for a distance of 85 metres to maintain a minimum of 3.5-metre-wide travel lane for each direction.
  3. Remove the existing parking on the western side of Darling Point Road, opposite property No.3-17 Darling Point Road, for a distance of 60 metres.
  4. Replace the existing ‘No Stopping’ restrictions on the eastern side of Darling Point Road, near property No.3-17 Darling Point Road, with ‘2P 7am-6pm Mon-Fri Permit Holders Excepted’ restrictions for a distance of 40 metres.

 

  1. Note the approval for Parts B & C are subject to:
  1. A Road Occupancy License (ROL) be obtained from Transport Management Centre (TMC) for any works that may impact on traffic flows on New South Head Road and on Darling Point Road, within 50 metres of the signalised intersection during construction activities;
  2. The applicant must comply with any directive provided by the NSW Police Force; 
  3. All construction vehicles must access and exit the site in a forward direction to minimise disruption to vehicular and pedestrian traffic along the route; 
  4. The applicant must liaise fortnightly with the developers/builders undertaking works for other developments occurring in close proximity (500m or in the same street) to the subject site, in order to minimise the cumulative traffic and parking impacts in the area (e.g. major concrete pours should not occur on more than 1 site on any particular day);  
  5. Construction traffic associated with the development must minimise the use of public roads and public parking facilities (e.g. on-street parking) where feasible; 
  6. Construction works or construction related traffic must not impede access of Council’s waste operation;
  7. Construction works or construction related traffic must not impact on school traffic of the nearby Ascham School, including but not limited to pick-up and drop-off arrangement, student/parent activities requiring access to and/or from school and other day-to-day pedestrian and vehicular activities accessing/egressing the school campus;
  8. Construction works are to be only undertaken within approved hours, as stipulated in Hours of Construction (Conditions D.3-D.7) of Development Consent to mitigate impact of the work upon amenity of the neighbourhood;
  9. SafeWork NSW accredited traffic controller/s must be provided to ensure pedestrian and vehicular access, including emergency vehicle access, are safely maintained at all times within the area impacted by construction activities of the subject site;
  10. The applicant must ensure that no marshalling or queuing of construction vehicles occur on public roads. Arriving vehicles that are not able to use access Works Zone/s must not use any public road as a holding point or layover area;
  11. All works must be undertaken in accordance with the approved landscape plan, arborist report, tree management plan and transplant method statement as applicable;
  12. All parking/traffic changes and associated works arising from the construction of the subject site must be carried out at full expense of the applicant;
  13. The applicant must liaise with Council’s Infrastructure Assets Team to provide a bond to cover the cost of replacing any part of Council’s infrastructure which may be damaged by the construction activities of the subject site, including vehicles access/egressing the site and Works Zone/s.
  14. The applicant must notify affected properties at a minimum of seven (7) business days prior to the commencement of each construction stage, and must clearly demonstrate any parking/traffic changes arising from the construction, including but not limited to: installation of Works Zone, removal of bus stop and associated 'Bus Zone', implementation with 'No Right Turn' restrictions and realignment of existing line marking;
  15. A Community Liaison Officer and/or Site Manager must include their contact details (email and a mobile phone number) in clear and concise signage on-site, with this signage visible to the public at all times, in order to enable members of the community to contact an appropriate person, as required. The Community Liaison Officer and/or Site Manager must liaise with Council’s Traffic and Transport Engineers on a recurring basis to ensure all construction traffic associated with the development site are undertaken in an appropriate manner. These matters should be addressed in the following format by the Community Liaison Officer and/or Site Manager:

 

  1. Maintain and keep on-site a register of complaints received from the local community;
  2. Fully investigate all complaints received;
  3. Notify the complainant of the results and actions arising from the investigation; and
  4. Ensure that the complaints register is available on request to Council staff.

The Motion was put and Carried.

  1. Not endorse the Construction Traffic and Pedestrian Management Plan (CTPMP - Reference: 24.345r05v13) for the State Significant Development of property No.136-148 New South Head Road, Edgecliff.

  2. Approve the Works Zone in Darling Point Road, within the existing ‘No Stopping’ zone along the property frontage for a distance of 28 metres operating 7am-6pm Monday to Friday and 8am-1pm Saturday for all construction stages. 

  3. Approve the following changes for structural works stage, only:
  1. Install a second Works Zone within the existing bus zone in Darling Point Road, for a distance of 20 metres operating 7am-6pm Monday to Friday and 8am-1pm Saturday.
  2. Realign the existing Barrier (BL2) line on the approach to the intersection of Darling Point Road and New South Head Road for a distance of 85 metres to maintain a minimum of 3.5-metre-wide travel lane for each direction.
  3. Remove the existing parking on the western side of Darling Point Road, opposite property No.3-17 Darling Point Road, for a distance of 60 metres.
  4. Replace the existing ‘No Stopping’ restrictions on the eastern side of Darling Point Road, near property No.3-17 Darling Point Road, with ‘2P 7am-6pm Mon-Fri Permit Holders Excepted’ restrictions for a distance of 40 metres.

  1. Note the approval for Parts B & C are subject to:
  1. A Road Occupancy License (ROL) be obtained from Transport Management Centre (TMC) for any works that may impact on traffic flows on New South Head Road and on Darling Point Road, within 50 metres of the signalised intersection during construction activities;
  2. The applicant must comply with any directive provided by the NSW Police Force; 
  3. All construction vehicles must access and exit the site in a forward direction to minimise disruption to vehicular and pedestrian traffic along the route; 
  4. The applicant must liaise fortnightly with the developers/builders undertaking works for other developments occurring in close proximity (500m or in the same street) to the subject site, in order to minimise the cumulative traffic and parking impacts in the area (e.g. major concrete pours should not occur on more than 1 site on any particular day);  
  5. Construction traffic associated with the development must minimise the use of public roads and public parking facilities (e.g. on-street parking) where feasible; 
  6. Construction works or construction related traffic must not impede access of Council’s waste operation;
  7. Construction works or construction related traffic must not impact on school traffic of the nearby Ascham School, including but not limited to pick-up and drop-off arrangement, student/parent activities requiring access to and/or from school and other day-to-day pedestrian and vehicular activities accessing/egressing the school campus;
  8. Construction works are to be only undertaken within approved hours, as stipulated in Hours of Construction (Conditions D.3-D.7) of Development Consent to mitigate impact of the work upon amenity of the neighbourhood;
  9. SafeWork NSW accredited traffic controller/s must be provided to ensure pedestrian and vehicular access, including emergency vehicle access, are safely maintained at all times within the area impacted by construction activities of the subject site;
  10. The applicant must ensure that no marshalling or queuing of construction vehicles occur on public roads. Arriving vehicles that are not able to use access Works Zone/s must not use any public road as a holding point or layover area;
  11. All works must be undertaken in accordance with the approved landscape plan, arborist report, tree management plan and transplant method statement as applicable;
  12. All parking/traffic changes and associated works arising from the construction of the subject site must be carried out at full expense of the applicant;
  13. The applicant must liaise with Council’s Infrastructure Assets Team to provide a bond to cover the cost of replacing any part of Council’s infrastructure which may be damaged by the construction activities of the subject site, including vehicles access/egressing the site and Works Zone/s.
  14. The applicant must notify affected properties at a minimum of seven (7) business days prior to the commencement of each construction stage, and must clearly demonstrate any parking/traffic changes arising from the construction, including but not limited to: installation of Works Zone, removal of bus stop and associated 'Bus Zone', implementation with 'No Right Turn' restrictions and realignment of existing line marking;
  15. A Community Liaison Officer and/or Site Manager must include their contact details (email and a mobile phone number) in clear and concise signage on-site, with this signage visible to the public at all times, in order to enable members of the community to contact an appropriate person, as required. The Community Liaison Officer and/or Site Manager must liaise with Council’s Traffic and Transport Engineers on a recurring basis to ensure all construction traffic associated with the development site are undertaken in an appropriate manner. These matters should be addressed in the following format by the Community Liaison Officer and/or Site Manager:
  1. Maintain and keep on-site a register of complaints received from the local community;
  2. Fully investigate all complaints received;
  3. Notify the complainant of the results and actions arising from the investigation; and
  4. Ensure that the complaints register is available on request to Council staff.

328/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1.  Accept the revised offer submitted by Ripples Watsons Bay Pty Ltd, as part of Prophetable Hospitality Pty Ltd, trading as SRG Hospitality (ABN 40 694 322 695), and approve the granting of a lease for the lease and operation of Dunbar House, Watsons Bay, for an initial term of twelve (12) years with one (1) option to renew for a further five (5) years, on the following key commercial terms :

  • A base rent of $50,000 per annum excl GST in Year 1;
  • A base rent of $100,000 per annum excl GST in Year 2, together with a turnover rent of 7 per cent of annual turnover exceeding $4.0 million;
  • A base rent of $180,000 per annum excl GST from Year 3, together with a turnover rent of 7 per cent of annual turnover exceeding $4.0 million;
  • Fixed annual rental increases of 4 per cent for the duration of the lease term, with the turnover rent threshold increasing by 4 per cent per annum; and
  • A market rent review upon exercise of the option term.

  1. Ensures the lease agreement includes a binding commitment by the lessee to undertake capital works valued at not less than $1.6 million plus GST within the first year of the lease term, subject to the receipt of all necessary approvals, including development consent where required.

  2. Authorises the General Manager to execute all legal agreements required to enter into a lease agreement with Ripples Watsons Bay Pty Ltd. 

The Motion was put and Carried.
 

 

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Dixson, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Price, Councillor Regan, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Zeltzer

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, refused development consent to DA65/2026/1 for Alterations and additions to the existing ancillary tennis centre amenities building (Trumper Park) including the formalisation of hours of operation and patron numbers.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel refused the application for the reasons set out in Attachment (Adopted Reasons for Refusal). The Panel was not satisfied that sufficient information had been provided to enable a detailed assessment of the likely impacts of the proposal in particular in relation to acoustic impacts, patron numbers, BCA compliance and operational management.

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, defer the determination of Development Application No. DA57/2026/1.

The Applicant be requested to submit to the Council:

  • A detailed description of the proposed works including a written request relating to the changes made to the description as originally submitted;
  • A copy of the plans that accurately depict the scope of the proposed works (new roof, new floor slabs, lift and stairs, and new structural columns). This must only relate to works that have not been constructed. 

 


  • All relevant supporting documents to be amended to reflect only these works. This includes but is not limited to an updated acoustic report, updated 4.6 variation, access report and an updated Heritage report.
  • Annotated photographs of the interior of the façade together with detailed drawings must be provided to show that the roof reconstruction will be like-for-like, apart from the now-demolished laundry element. No increase in the height of the roof or change to the slope is permitted.

The above information must be submitted to Council for assessment within 21 days from the date of determination, unless otherwise decided by the Chair.

The application will then be determined electronically by the Panel (as constituted on 4 June 2026) upon receipt of a supplementary assessment report prepared by Council staff.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken a site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence including the submission from Councillor Harriet Price, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, defer the determination of Development Application No. DA57/2026/1 to allow the applicant time to submit additional information that clarifies the scope of the proposal which does not include demolition.

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion

Note: Alexander Tiele, James Lidis, John Phegan and Warwick Richards addressed the Panel.

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, refuse development consent to Development Application No. 347/2025/1 for the part land-based and part water-based proposal consisting of the demolition of the existing building and the construction of a new contemporary two-storey building consisting of retail tenancies, café, restaurant with outdoor dining, marina lounge and administration office, a gymnasium for members of the marina only, boating workshop, carparking for 31 spaces and the removal of two (2) street trees that are on the State Heritage Register on land at 1B New Beach Road DARLING POINT, for the reasons included in Attachment 2, as modified by the Panel. 

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel is satisfied that the application be refused for the reasons set out in Attachment (Adopted Reasons for Refusal), as amended by the Panel.

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, is not satisfied that the written request from the applicant has adequately addressed the relevant matters to be addressed under Clause 4.6 of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 and therefore consent cannot be granted to the development which contravenes the maximum building height development standard under Clause 16(3) of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021.

AND

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, refuse development consent to Development Application No.470/2025/1 for new four storey residential flat building comprising seven apartments above basement car parking, landscaping and associated siteworks, which amends the approved residential flat building under DA77/2015 on land at 635 New South Head Road ROSE BAY, for the reasons detailed in Attachment 2, as modified by the Panel.

AND

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel is satisfied that the application be refused for the reasons set out in Attachment (Adopted Reasons for Refusal), as amended by the Panel.

361/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Receives and notes the Report responding to the Council resolution.

  2. Notes:
  1. Staff will continue to advocate to Sydney Water for stormwater treatment on the Double Bay stormwater channel.
  2. Water quality improvement is one of four priority action areas in its Environmental Sustainability Action Plan (ESAP).
  3. The ESAP includes two targets relating to water quality and fifteen action items.
  4. Improving water quality is a key objective of the Outer Sydney Harbour Coastal Management Program (CMP), and the CMP includes a stormwater and sewerage pollution assessment.

  1. Resolves to update Councillors via a report to the Ecological Sustainability Taskforce:
  1. On a biannual basis regarding the state of beaches in the Municipality, including reporting on water quality targets in accordance with our current testing regime.
  2. On the progress of the CMP and the stormwater and sewerage pollution assessment.

  1. Requests that the Mayor writes to the Member for Vaucluse, Ms Kellie Sloane MP, and the Federal Member for Wentworth, Ms Allegra Spender MP to:
  1. inform them of the water quality issues arising from the Sydney Water channel at Double Bay; and
  2. request their urgent advocacy to Sydney Water to seek a long-term treatment solution.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Dixson, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Price, Councillor Regan, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate
None

353/2026 Resolved without debate:

THAT Council:

  1. Receives and notes the report titled Status Update on Outstanding Resolutions of Council - 31 March 2026.

  2. Notes that there are 35 Council Resolutions outstanding as at 31 March 2026.

  3. Notes that a six‑monthly Outstanding Council Resolutions Update report will be presented to Council in August and February each year.



  1. Notes the change in reporting arrangements, whereby Notices of Motion will, in future, be included in the Outstanding Council Resolutions Update report noted in C.

  2. Resolves to close the following resolutions and incorporate them as actions in other Plans as noted in Attachment 2 or incorporate them as actions in the 2026–2027 Operational Plan, with progress to be reported through the six‑monthly Delivery Program and Operational Plan Progress Report.
  1. 36 - Council Meeting March 2023 Item 12.1.2 Paddington Public Domain Strategy & Technical Manual.  To be completed under Action 1.1.4.1 in Council's Draft 2026-2027 Operational Plan.
  2.  38 - Council Meeting April 2025 Item 14.2 Community communication regarding the Minns Government's Low and Mid-rise Housing Reforms. Items A to C of the resolution have been completed and Item D will be undertaken as part of Action 1.1.1.4 in Council's Draft 2026-2027 Operational Plan.
  3. 39 - Council Meeting November 2025 Item 12.1.1 Heritage significance assessment of places identified by the Darling Point Society. This work has been incorporated into the Heritage Gap Analysis. 

  1. Resolves to close the following resolution on the basis that it is no longer relevant, noting the specific reasons provided:
  1. Council Meeting July 2022 Item 12.2.3 Woollahra Integrated Transport Strategy 2022.  Finalisation of the ITS is not recommended, as its key intent has been addressed through the Active Transport Plan, and further work would not represent an efficient use of resources.
  2. Council Meeting April 2020 Item 16.1 Street Play Initiative as resolved no longer required.
  3. Council Meeting March 2024 Item 16.2 Best Street in Woollahra. Resolved no longer required due to LMR Reforms in that area led by NSW State Government.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Dixson, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Price, Councillor Regan, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate
None

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council as the consent authority, is satisfied under Clause 4.6(3) of the Woollahra LEP 2014, that consent may be granted to the development which contravenes the floor space ratio development standard prescribed under Clause 4.4E of Woollahra LEP 2014, as the applicant has demonstrated that:

  1. compliance with the development standard is unreasonable or unnecessary in the circumstances, and
  2. there are sufficient environmental planning grounds to justify the contravention of the development standard.
AND 

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, grant development consent to DA6/2026/1 for alterations and additions to a dwelling approved under a Complying Development Certificate, including the construction of basement car parking and demolition and reconstruction of a detached second dwelling (Dual-Occupancy) on the site on land at 69 Fitzwilliam Road VAUCLUSE, subject to the recommended conditions as outlined in Attachment 2.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions).

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

 


For the Motion
Against the Motion
