Note: Community Representative, Isabelle Shapiro declared a non-significant, non-pecuniary interest in this item as she previously served as a Councillor at Woollahra Council with Malcolm Young who addressed the Panel. Community Representative, Isabelle Shapiro further declared a non-significant, non-pecuniary interest as they are associated with two members of the public who have made submissions on this item. Isabelle Shapiro further declared a non-significant, non-pecuniary interest on this item as she previously served as a Councillor at Woollahra Council with Councillor Merrill Witt who addressed the Panel and submitted late correspondence on this item.

Note:Andrew Christopher, Rhys Jones, Samuel Jacobson, Katherine Grinberg, Councillor Merrill Witt and Malcolm Young addressed the Panel.

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, refuses development consent to Development Application No. 457/2025/1 for demolition of existing dwelling houses and construction of a nine-storey residential flat building comprising 18 residential units (including affordable housing), three levels of basement parking, landscaping works, and lot amalgamation on land at 52-54 Manning Road DOUBLE BAY, for the reasons at Attachment 2.

 


Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions, late correspondence, and the verbal submissions by the speakers and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel is satisfied that the application should be refused for the reasons set out in Attachment (Adopted Reasons for Refusal), which also address matters raised in submissions. 

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion


David Ryan
Nil
Megan Jones

Lee Kosnetter

Isabelle Shapiro



4/0

Councillor Carmichael:

  • Congratulations to Judge Scott Nash OAM

Councillor Carmichael congratulated Judge Scott Nash who, as part of the King’s Birthday Honours List, was awarded an OAM for his services to local government and the legal profession. Councillor Carmichael acknowledged Judge Nash’s career, particularly his two terms as Mayor of Randwick and his 13 years of service on Randwick Council.


Councillor Woodgate:

  • 78th Independence Day for Israel

Councillor Woodgate thanked and congratulated David Ossip and the NSW Jewish Board of Deputies for organising the 78th Independence Day for Israel. Councillor Woodgate attended this event on the 7th of May 2026 alongside Councillor Jarvis, the Mayor, Councillor Dixson and Kellie Sloane MP, and noted that Councillor Carmichael was an apology.


Councillor Andruska

  • Opening of Emanuel Synagogue Garden
  • Council's Tree Planting Program
  • Paddington Chamber of Commerce
  • Council's Youth Summit

Councillor Andruska advised that he along with Councillor Carmichael recently attended the opening of the new gardens at Emanuel Synagogue in Woollahra.

Councillor Andruska thanked and congratulated staff on Council's tree planting program, noting that many local residents appreciate trees and all of the work being done.

Councillor Andruska congratulated the Paddington Chamber of Commerce on a successful Business Awards night. Councillor Andruska attended this event on the 18th of June 2026 alongside the Mayor, Councillor Dixson and noted the large number of attendees.

Councillor Andruska further thanked and congratulated staff on the recent Youth Summit held at Woollahra Council. Councillor Andruska also thanked all of the young people who attended and extended his appreciation to Vicki Munro (Council’s Manager – Community and Culture) and her staff for hosting the highly successful event.

 

The Mayor, Councillor Dixson:

  • Polish Day Constitution
  • 78th Independence Day for Israel
  • NAIDOC Week
  • Dinner at Emanuel Synagogue
  • Shabbat Dinner hosted by Waverley Council
  • Celebration of Rabbi Kamins
  • Council's Youth Summit
  • 'Advance Australia Where' hosted by Cranbrook School
  • Queen Street West Woollahra Association
  • Citizenship Ceremonies

The Mayor, Councillor Dixson advised that on 5 May 2026, she attended the Polish Day Constitution event and congratulated Consul staff on a very fun event.

On 7 May 2026, the Mayor attended the 78th Independence Day for Israel event and noted that the event was incredibly well-attended.

The Mayor advised that on 28 May 2026 she, alongside Councillor Price and Councillor Torsten attended Council's NAIDOC event where the film 'The Last Daughter' was screened. The Mayor thanked Council's Library staff for organising the event and highly recommends people see the film.

On 28 May 2026, the Mayor attended the Interfaith Dinner at Emanuel Synagogue. The Mayor advised that the dinner included engaging discussions between members of the Jewish faith, Muslim faith and Christian communities.

On 29 May 2026, the Mayor attended the Shabbat Dinner hosted by Waverley Council at the Bondi Pavilion and stated that it was a wonderful event and very well-attended.

On 21 June 2026, the Mayor attended the celebration of Rabbi Kamins. The Mayor highlighted Rabbi Kamins' 40 years of service at Emanuel Synagogue, noting that the Synagogue has been in existence for 80 years, meaning Rabbi Kamins has been part of it for half its history. The Mayor acknowledged the comments of Rabbi Ninio and President Ian Rathmell, that Rabbi Kamins has inspired generations of the community and has focused on unity, not uniformity.

The Mayor added to Councillor Andruska's update regarding Council's Youth Summit, describing it as inspirational.

On 16 June 2026, The Mayor attended 'Advance Australia Where', organised by Cranbrook School. The Mayor shared that young people aged 12 to 17 at the event engaged in complex issues relating to housing, planning, the environment and the economy.

The Mayor congratulated the Queen Street West Woollahra Association for their ongoing work in the business and local community.

The Mayor advised that she recently attended four Citizenship Ceremonies at Woollahra, and congratulated each of the recipients. The Mayor thanked their friends and families, and extended her appreciation to staff for organising the events.

To the Director of Planning and Place:

Can the Director please update the community on the action Council Officers have taken regarding the unlawful demolition of the existing floors, internal walls, stairs and the entire roof structure of the Unicorn Hotel in Paddington. 

A/Manager - Compliance & Enforcement in response:

Council was notified on 26 February 2026 of potential unauthorised works at the Unicorn Hotel, located at 106 Oxford Street, Paddington.

A subsequent inspection of the premises identified that works to the roof area of the building had been undertaken without the benefit of development consent. As a result, a Stop Work Order was issued to the building owner(s) on 12 March 2026.

Further inspections of the site revealed that additional unauthorised building works had been carried out to the lower ground and ground floor levels of the premises, also without development consent. A further Stop Work Order was issued to the building owner(s) on 22 April 2026. Follow-up inspections have confirmed that works have since ceased in compliance with Council’s orders.

Following a review of the circumstances and available documentation, Council issued Orders pursuant to Section 9.23 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, requiring both the building owner(s) and the builders to attend an interview with Council Officers. Both parties have responded to the Orders, and Council’s Building Compliance Officer is currently liaising with the parties and their legal representatives to arrange suitable dates and times for these interviews.

THAT Council:

  1. Note the advice received from the Manager of Property & Projects dated 22 June 2026 at 6:30pm on 22 June 2026 following advice from the independent probity advisors that two of the tenderers, Voyager Tennis and Lyne Park Tennis were disqualified from the tender process as there are reasonable grounds to conclude that both Voyager Tennis and Lyne Park tennis have breached the conditions of the Request for Tender (RFT).

 

  1. Accept the tender submitted by Rod Fahey Tennis School Pty Ltd ACN 117 480 490 as Trustee for the Fahey Family Trust (trading as Tennis Nation by Rod Fahey) for the lease and operation of the Lyne Park Tennis Centre, 550 New South Head Road, Rose Bay.

  2. Accept the proposal from Tennis Nation to demolish the disused toilet block and construct an additional multi-sport court at a cost of $130,000 excl GST to be borne by the lessee.

  3. Enter into a lease with Tennis Nation for an initial term of ten (10) years, with two (2) options to renew of five (5) years each, on the terms outlined in this report, including:
  • Rental of $130,000 (plus GST) in Year 1;
  • $190,000 (plus GST) in Year 2;
  • $360,000 per annum (plus GST) from Year 3 onwards;
  • Additional rental of $10,000, $20,000 and $35,000 in Years 1 to 3 respectively, for the use of the standalone disused toilet block area subject to approval of recommendation C.
  1. Endorses to increase the lease term from that stipulated in Council’s Leasing and Licensing of Council Controlled Land Policy, (in accordance with C above) as a result of the scale of capital investment, financial return and long-term community benefit that will be delivered by the successful tenderer.

  2. Endorse the inclusion of multi-sport court use, including permanent line markings, with tennis to remain the primary use.

  3. Ensures the lease agreement includes a capital commitment of $1,966,345 excl GST and $130,000 excl GST for the use of the standalone toilet area, over the first three (3) years of the lease term, subject to any necessary development approval and provides in-principle support for the proposed capital works.

  4. Authorise the General Manager to finalise and execute all necessary lease documentation and associated agreements.

  5. Further notes Council’s expectation that Tennis Nation will, in good faith, undertake their best endeavours to retain and carry-over the current arrangements with community initiatives and bookings, and to the extent possible to retain current staff of the facility.

Amendment moved by Councillor Witt
Seconded by Councillor Parmegiani

THAT Council:

  1. In accordance with s178 (1) (b) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, declines to accept any of the tender submissions for the lease of the Lyne Park Tennis Centre, known as Tender SC8316.

  2. Council notes the advice of the Manager of Property & Projects and the Independent Probity Advisor regarding the exclusion of tenderers Lyne Park Tennis Centre and Voyager Tennis from the RFT process due to non-compliance with RFT requirements; and noting that section 178(3)(e) provides Council with the specific authority to enter into negotiations with any person, regardless of their status in a tender process.

  3. Council resolves in accordance with section 178 (3) (e) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 to enter into negotiations with the existing operator, Lyne Park Tennis Centre, with a view to entering into a contract in relation to the lease and operation of the Lyne Park Tennis Centre for similar specifications as Tender SC8316, for the following reasons:
  1. Community Preference: Public feedback to the SC8316 tender process revealed strong and widespread community support for both the existing operations and the current operator.

 

  1. Local Management and Continuity: The existing operator is a locally-embedded business with deep community ties, providing a tailored, community-focused management model that ensures a level of local continuity and engagement distinct from a large-scale, multi-venue corporate entity.
  2. Policy Consistency: This approach is consistent with Council’s established precedent at Cooper Park and Trumper Park, where Council prioritised local, community-focused operators to ensure continuity of service and preserve community character. 
  3. Public Interest: Council recognizes that the Lyne Park Tennis Courts are a significant public asset and has a responsibility to weigh community benefits and social value against commercial considerations.
  1. Recommends that Council work with the existing operator, Lyne Park Tennis Centre, to negotiate a new lease that:
  • Endorses the inclusion of multi-sport court use, including permanent line markings for complementary sports on two of the tennis courts;
  • Maintains tennis as the primary function of the Lyne Park Tennis Centre by ensuring it continues to remain the dominant use for the two courts proposed for multi-sport use; and
  • Explores the best use of the disused toilet block to maximise customer safety and enjoyment of tennis and multi-use sports.
  1. Thanks the participating tenderers for participating in the tender process.

The Amendment was put and Lost.
The Motion was put and Carried.

(Councillor Ardouin/Councillor Carmichael)

403/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:
 
  1. Affirms its commitment to making housing more affordable throughout the LGA and acknowledges that increasing supply whilst reducing costs of construction are the key levers to delivering greater housing affordability;

  2. Requests the General Manager to prepare a report to Council no later than December 2026 detailing any further actions Council may take (including costs involved) to bring down the cost of construction across the LGA, including contemplation of:
  1. Streamlining development approval processes to reduce approval timelines;
  2. The benefits and costs of loosening controls on weekend construction to accelerate the construction period for developments;
  3. Strategies to reduce insurance costs for developments, such as working with insurers to understand how Council might de-risk construction activity within the LGA (such as through minimising the risk of excavation-related damage);
  4. Insofar Council’s remit allows, novel ideas to work with industry stakeholders to bring down material and other input costs;
  5. Any options available to Council to increase the supply of labour within the construction sector by collaborating with industry stakeholders to attract and retain talent to the LGA (such as contemplating sponsoring skilled worker visas) or if Council does not have an appropriate mechanism to achieve this, by providing advocacy on labour market reforms through relevant channels (e.g. LGNSW, OLG, ALGA);
  6. Opportunities to work with neighbouring Council's, SSROC, LGNSW and the OLG to develop regional or State-wide strategies which further the objective of the Motion; and
  7. Advocacy on targeted legislative and regulatory reform.

  1. Requests that the Mayor write to the Minister for Planning (Hon. Paul Scully MP) to request that the Minister introduce legislation to explicitly allow Council's to compulsory acquire land for the purpose of increasing housing supply, and/or for the construction of enabling infrastructure in areas that Council has identified as appropriate for further densification.

  2. Requests that the General Manager amend the post-exhibition Draft Woollahra Affordable Housing Policy 2026 to specify that monetary contributions (and any interest earned on unspent contributions) are to be used as recoverable contributions (at a concessional interest rate) to either CHP's or build-to-rent developers for the purpose of new affordable dwelling construction within the LGA. In the case where a recoverable contribution would breach the Investment Order 2011, Council further requests that the General Manager enter in negotiations with ADI's to set-up a pass-through vehicle which would allow Council to indirectly invest monetary contributions in new affordable developments within the LGA.

The Motion was put and Lost.

 

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

404/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Affirms that aspiring to own a home should be a realistic and obtainable goal centred around providing a permanent, secure and quality place to live;

  2. While noting the purpose of the Act to provide affordable rental housing, aspires for the Affordable Housing Contributions scheme to offer a clear bridge for tenants between being a renter and an owner;

 

  1. Requests the General Manager to write to the Deputy-Secretary for Local Government asking for their view as to whether the affordable housing contributions framework would not prevent Woollahra Council from enacting a provision in the Affordable Housing Contributions Policy, which would long-term affordable housing tenants the right to access a shared-equity scheme or to purchase their residence from Council and in turn recycle any proceeds into investing in further new affordable housing (retaining funds within the Affordable Housing Contributions fund); and

Conditional on the Deputy-Secretary (or delegate) responding in the affirmative (i.e. such a scheme as contemplated above would be permissible), requests that the General Manager bring a report to Council as soon as practicable detailing the necessary amendments to the affordable housing contributions scheme and policy to include the right for long-term affordable housing tenants to enter into a shared-equity scheme with council or to purchase their residence from Council and recycle capital to invest in new affordable housing supply (retaining funds within the Affordable Housing Contributions fund).

(Councillor Price/Councillor Torsten)

408/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes:

  1. That the suburb of Woollahra is home to a significant, mature urban forest -  comprising diverse, native and exotic trees, situated across private gardens and public land found between 287-297 Edgecliff Road and 66 Wallaroy Road, Woollahra (the Forest).

  2. The State Government plans to rezone land around Edgecliff and Woollahra Stations for up to 10,000 new homes (the Proposal). The Proposal encompasses an area in a 400 metre radius from Edgecliff Station and a 800 metre radius from the new Woollahra Station.

  3. The Forest is located within:
  • an area of Aboriginal Heritage Sensitivity;
  • the Woollahra Heritage Conservation Area (HCA); and 
  • a 800 metre radius from the new Woollahra Station.
  1. Its Urban Forest Strategy 2024–2050 and the adopted framework to increase tree canopy cover and the critical need to preserve existing canopy on private land.

  2. Its Biodiversity Conservation Strategy 2025–2035, specifically its vision statement and key objectives:

    ‘To protect, restore and improve biodiversity, sustaining a healthy environment … To conserve, restore and improve terrestrial biodiversity and enhance habitat connectivity through our urban forest.’
  1. Its Environmental Sustainability Action Plan 2023 - 2028.

  2. The Memorandum dated 20 March 2026 containing the Answer to the Question on Notice from Cr Torsten, regarding the ‘Woollahra Station Trees’ (tabled as late correspondence at the Council meeting of 23 March 2026).

  3. Its resolution of 24 September 2025 to establish an internal financial reserve of $700,000 to be used for a range of Council-led studies, audits, reviews, and assessments focused on evaluating the potential impacts of the proposed State-led rezoning of parts of Woollahra and Edgecliff.

  4. The Housing Delivery Authority (the HDA) record of briefing dated 17 February 2026 concerning the Expression of Interest No.324141 from the ‘Woollahra Consortium’ regarding the following properties:
  • 287, 289-291 293-295, 295A and 295B Edgecliff Road; and
  • 72A, 74 and 76 Wallaroy Road (the EOI).
 
  1. The following advice from the HDA regarding the EOI:’ The applicant be advised there remain alternative approval pathways in the NSW planning system for development on these sites following the relevant State Led Rezoning.’

  1. Transport for NSW’s (TFNSW) Biodiversity Policy dated 25 February 2026 (No.CP22004.2) (the TFNSW Biodiversity Policy), including its obligations to protect and enhance biodiversity in NSW and in particular, the:

 

‘Goal of achieving a no net loss of biodiversity as a consequence of its infrastructure development activities.’

Note: 
Late correspondence was received from members of the public and is included as an attachment (Late Correspondence – Item 14.2 – Public).

Councillor Silcocks asking:

At the Double Bay Residents Association AGM there were reports of significant damage being caused by construction projects in Double Bay, specifically associated with excavation.

One of the accounts alleged that excavation on one site had resulted in injecting concrete into the sewer pipe, which then solidified and needs to be drilled out.

In the meantime, sewerage is having to be trucked out and Gum Tree Lane is completely blocked off indefinitely.

It’s appreciated that damage to neighbouring properties as a result of construction tends to be a civil matter and even the sewer damage is between the developer and Sydney Water.

However, in the same way that a notifiable incident in the workplace needs to be immediately reported to SafeWork NSW, what mechanism is there, or could there be, for Council to be informed of problems encountered or damage caused on a construction site, especially when it (a) involves critical public infrastructure and (b) can inform the feasibility and safety of future planning controls?

A/Manager - Compliance & Enforcement in response:

  1. We are not aware of any mechanism by which Council must be notified of these kind of circumstances. Council staff agree that this is a civil matter if it is with a private sewer line. However, if the blockage has occurred in the sewer main, Sydney Water would action the solution and charge the party responsible.

  2. As we are made aware of issues relating to construction, such as matters associated with excavation or dewatering, then in consultation with the planners and engineers, we are able to recommend refinements to our planning controls, the DA guide, and/or our conditions.  Where there are matters relating to State policies such as the Low and Mid-Rise Housing Policy, we are advocating to the Department of Planning, Housing & Infrastructure.

Note: 
Late correspondence was received from members of the public and is included as an attachment (Late Correspondence – Item 14.3 – Public).

Councillor Witt asking:

  1. Will the proposed new flood studies for Rose Bay and Double Bay develop a methodology for assessing the "damming effect", which can occur when large boundary-to-boundary basements obstruct subsurface and overland flow paths, causing localised flood impacts upstream or downstream of the site?
 
This question is raised partly in response to the Urban Design referral for 52-54 Manning Road DA (by J Richards-Smith, 6 February 2026). It noted that basement excavation extending to side and front boundaries "significantly reduces opportunities for deep soil planting, efficient groundwater movement and recharge, and natural overland flow in and around the site". It recommended requiring the applicant to demonstrate that the design "will not create a damming effect" (p.13–14). 
 
  1. Will new flood study modelling for Rose Bay and Double Bay take into account cumulative basement footprint scenarios across the Double Bay and Rose Bay floodplain catchments, consistent with the LMR rezoning trajectory?
 
The Urban Design referral quoted above explicitly raised the "cumulative redevelopment scenario" issue (p.4, p.23), that is, a situation where multiple boundary-to-boundary basements across the precinct compound the damming/groundwater displacement effect. 
 
The GHD Hydrogeological and Geotechnical Impacts Assessments for Rose Bay and Double Bay explained that permanent basement structures act as cut-off walls to natural groundwater flow, causing ongoing drawdown or mounding (raising of the water table) that can exceed 0.2 m–0.3 m cumulatively in areas where multiple basements are present. Upstream mounding can also increase flood risks and hydraulic uplift of surrounding structures if pressure is allowed to build.
 
  1. Will the flood study establish flood-planning-area-specific excavation/basement footprint benchmarks, rather than allowing applicants to rely on precedents drawn from non-flood-affected sites? 
 
The Urban Design referral for the 52-54 Manning Road DA noted that comparable excavation precedents cited by applicants "relate to sites outside the flood planning area" and are therefore "not directly comparable to the environmental constraints affecting" sites within it (p.4).
 
  1. Will new or updated flood modelling for Rose Bay and Double Bay be calibrated to reflect the cumulative effect of the LMR-driven development pipeline, not just current ground conditions? 
 
Multiple DAs now in train propose large basement footprints extending to or near site boundaries, substantially reducing deep soil area available for groundwater recharge and overland flow dispersal. 
 
The revised Flood Impact Assessment Report (FIRA) for the 23-31 Dover Road SSDA employed an alternative flood  model, TUFLOW, which produced lower inundation on Dover Road, because it allowed water to spread laterally across neighbouring residential properties that were previously "walled off" under Council's SOBEK modelling.

The revised FIRA explicitly confirmed the TUFLOW model's intent, stating that "major alleviation of depths occurs because floodwater can now pass through residential properties adjacent to Spencer Lane instead of building up on Dover Road.” But this assessment ignored the fact that most of the surrounding area will be redeveloped for medium to high density. 
 
Director - Infrastructure and Sustainability in response:

In May 2026, Council endorsed the undertaking of new flood studies for the Rose Bay and Double Bay catchments. These studies will consider the cumulative effect of LMR developments on flood behaviour. In addition, work is underway on studies of the cumulative impact of LMR development on groundwater behaviour. The specific matters raised in these QON will be referred to the consultants undertaking the studies for consideration and informing of the studies where appropriate.

417/2026 Resolved without debate:

THAT Council:

  1. Note the contents of this report in response to the Mayoral Minute regarding support for local businesses.

  2. Adopt the definition of Small Local Business as outlined in this report, including a gross annual turnover threshold of $3 million per individual premises, noting that this threshold is informed by local sample data and is considered a reasonable and pragmatic benchmark.

  3. Approve the introduction of a Fee Reduction Program for eligible Small Local Businesses holding Footway or Parklet Approvals.

  4. Adopt Option A with a 50% Fee Reduction, as it provides a significant level of support to Small Local Businesses whilst maintaining Council's financial sustainability.

  5. Apply the Fee Reduction for a period of 12 months commencing 1 July 2026, with eligibility determined through an opt-in application process supported by independent financial verification.

  6. Amend the Fees and Charges Schedule for FY2026/27 for inclusion of the Fee Reduction option to reflect Council's decision.

 

  1. Delegate authority to the General Manager to finalise application, verification and administrative arrangements to implement the Fee Reduction Program.

  2. Monitor uptake and financial impact and receive an update as part of the January 2027 budget review on the effectiveness and financial implications of the Fee Reduction Program.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

THAT Council:

  1. Approve the staff selection committee’s (SSC) recommendations for grants under the 2026/27 Council’s Grants Program, as detailed in this report and its related attachments.

  2. Approve the SSC’s recommendations under the 2026/27 Outgoing Sponsorship Program, as detailed in this report and its related attachments.

  3. Requests that the General Manager ensures that:
  1. Any future reports tabled to Council containing the SSC’s recommendations for grant funding contains specific commentary on how the Applicant has addressed Council's Grant Funding criteria concerning recurrent funding (as contained in the following paraphrasing from Council’s Grants Policy (the Policy)):
  • 6.1 (d): Grants can be used as seed funding with the expectation that applicants will grow in skills and capacity and move to self-sustaining practices.
  • 6.1 (f) Applicants that are successful for a grant in three consecutive years will need to demonstrate that they are:

 

  1. taking active and current steps to source alternate and ongoing funding as per paragraph (d) above; and/or
  2. continuing to try new and innovative ideas as part of each annual application; and/or
  3. continuing to attract new local participants who will benefit from their proposal.
  1. Successful grant recipients comply with paragraph 6.3(e) of the Policy to ‘Notify Council of any associated events, so that the Mayor or his/her representative and Councillors can attend, as well as provide appropriate photographs and testimony to be used for promotional purposes.’ 
  1. Note that successful grant recipients will be invited to a Grants Awards Presentation to be held on Thursday, 20 August 2026 at 2:00 pm, hosted by the Mayor, Councillor Dixson.

(Councillor Witt/Councillor Regan)

 

409/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council: 

  1. Requests the General Manager seek advise on the feasibility of commissioning a cumulative impact assessment of the expected increase in traffic volumes from developments proposed under the Low and Mid-Rise (LMR) Housing Policy in and around the Rose Bay Town Centre.

  2. Notes that LMR DAs currently lodged either with the Council or the Department of Planning Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI) as State Significant Development Applications (SSDAs) propose an additional 568 car parking spaces, with further car parking spaces proposed for the SSDA seniors housing development at 20-30 Wilberforce Avenue and 33-37 Dover Road, Rose Bay (156 car spaces), the SSDA seniors housing development at 32-42 Wilberforce Avenue and 41-55 Dover Road, Rose Bay (105 independent living units, estimate 200+ parking spaces) and the SSDA for 36-56 Dover Road and 11-31 Hamilton Street Rose Bay (313 unit residential flat building with 298 car spaces).

  3. Notes that a cumulative traffic assessment for the Rose Bay area would assist SSDA/DA applicants and Council Staff to prepare and/or assess whether Traffic Impact Assessments (TIAs) conform with the processes and methodology recommended in the Guide to Transport Impact Assessment published by Transport for NSW.  It states that:
  • The needs of all road users are considered and, where necessary, appropriate facilities (e.g. separated cycleways, footpaths, bus lanes, pedestrians crossings, intersection widening or upgraded intersection controls) are provided; 
  • A development should be considered within its physical and strategic context and not in isolation from nearby developments, including buildings already constructed, under construction or approved developments in the area of influence; 
  • Nearby features such as intersections, footpaths and other driveways, as well as active transport facilities should also be considered; 
  • Road safety is treated as a priority in the planning process; and
  • Environmental impacts (both natural and built) are given consideration.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, is not satisfied that the matters required to be addressed under Clause 4.6(3) of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 have been demonstrated and that consent may not therefore be granted to the development application, which contravenes the Minimum Lot Size development standard under Clause 4.1 of Woollahra LEP 2014.

AND

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, refuse to modify development consent to DA 365/2024/1 for alterations to existing dwelling at No. 364 Edgecliff Road (Lot 1), demolition of existing rear dwelling and construction of a new residential flat building at No. 364A Edgecliff Road (Lot 2) and site remediation on land at 364 Edgecliff Road WOOLLAHRA, for the reasons at Attachment 2.

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, refuse to grant development consent to DA1/2026/1 for Alterations and additions to Unit 42 of the existing shop top housing development on land at 42/18 Bay Street DOUBLE BAY, for the reasons for refusal in Attachment (Adopted Reasons for Refusal).

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. The Panel is satisfied that the application be refused for the reasons set out in Attachment (Adopted Reasons for Refusal).

1. Owner's Consent

The architectural drawings demonstrate that the common property i.e. external walls and the slab between the two levels of Apt 42, will be breached by the proposed stairwell and new additions, therefore land owner's consent from the Owners Corporation is required. No consent from the Owners Corporation was submitted.

Motion moved by Councillor Jarvis
Seconded by Councillor Zeltzer

THAT Council:

  1. Note the correspondence received from Homes NSW regarding the allocation of Woollahra Housing SEPP developer contributions to the Women’s Housing Company for the purchase of affordable housing in Maroubra.

  2. That Council reaffirms its decision of April 2025 that contributions be allocated in our local LGA.

Amendment moved by Councillor Andruska
Seconded by Councillor Carmichael

THAT Council:

  1. Note the correspondence received from Homes NSW regarding the allocation of Woollahra Housing SEPP developer contributions to the Women’s Housing Company for the purchase of affordable housing in Maroubra.

  2. Note that the allocation is consistent with the Ministerial Direction issued under Section 7.33 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, which permits expenditure within the originating local government area or an adjoining local government area.

  3. Note Council officers’ previous engagement with Homes NSW regarding opportunities to deliver affordable housing within Woollahra or adjoining local government areas.

  4. Request that Homes NSW continue to consult with Council regarding the future use of Housing SEPP affordable housing contributions generated within the Woollahra LGA.

 

The Amendment was put and Carried.

The Amendment became the Motion.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Woodgate:

  • Rose Bay Rotary Club
  • National Tree Day

Councillor Woodgate advised that on 23 July 2026 he represented the Mayor at the Rose Bay Rotary Club changeover dinner. Councillor Woodgate thanked the club's President Dr. Mendelsohn, and praised the club for having raised funds to fit out all police cars in the Eastern Suburbs Police Area Command with defibrillator kits.

Councillor Woodgate further advised that on 26 July 2026 he, along with the Mayor, Councillor Andruska and Councillor Jarvis, participated in National Tree Day. Councillor Woodgate noted that he also represented the Mayor at the Royal Sydney Golf Club, where students from Cranbrook School, Kambala and Rose Bay Secondary College planted 1,000 native trees on the golf course. Councillor Woodgate further advised that members of the Royal Sydney Golf Club had planted an additional 1,500 native plants and congratulated them on their efforts.

 

Councillor Jarvis:

  • Office of Local Government Webinar
  • Unveiling of 'In Them We See Ourselves' Public Artwork
  • Public Art Panel
  • National Tree Day
Councillor Jarvis advised that on 26 July 2026 she participated in a webinar hosted by the Office of Local Government in relation to recent reforms.

Councillor Jarvis further advised that she, along with the Mayor, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Witt and Councillor Mitchell recently attended the unveiling of the 'In Them We See Ourselves' public artwork in Christison Park. Councillor Jarvis acknowledged the attendance of community members at the event.

Councillor Jarvis advised that on 4 July 2026 she had the pleasure of Chairing the Public Art Panel Meeting.

Councillor Jarvis advised that, on 6 July 2026, she participated in National Tree Day by planting trees in Cooper Park.


Councillor Andruska:

  • National Tree Day
  • Library Reading Day

Councillor Andruska reported that on 26 July 2026 he participated in National Tree Day, and that on 28 July 2026 he will be taking part in the library reading day for children at Double Bay Library.


Councillor Mitchell:

  • Unveiling of 'In Them We See Ourselves' Public Artwork

Councillor Mitchell advised that she recently attended the unveiling of the 'In Them We See Ourselves' public artwork in Christison Park. Councillor Mitchell noted the Mayor's attendance and that of Will Nemesh, Mayor of Waverley.


Councillor Torsten:

  • NAIDOC Week

Councillor Torsten advised that he spoke on the Mayor's behalf at the 50th Anniversary of NAIDOC which also combined with the 20th Anniversary of Bushcare. Councillor Torsten noted how well the events were attended by members of the public and thanked Council library staff for organising the event.

 

The Mayor, Councillor Dixson:

  • Citizenship Ceremonies

The Mayor reminded Councillors of the two upcoming Citizenship Ceremonies to be held at Council and encouraged them to join her in hosting the ceremonies.

467/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Receives and notes the report titled Costs for Local Government Elections - Principles Paper.

 

  1. Endorses in principle the draft response to the NSW Electoral Commission survey as included in this report.

  2. Delegates authority to the General Manager to finalise and lodge the survey response to the NSW Electoral Commission.

  3. Notes the total expenditure on the election of Councillors in NSW runs to around $120m or almost $100,000 per Councillor and recommends that if the public purse is expected to see the value in and continue to fund democracy at the local level, then the State Government refrain from constantly removing locally elected officials from the running of local municipalities in terms of such fundamental matters as approving development applications and developing their own local strategic plans.

The Motion was put and Carried.

The Mayor further declared a significant, non-pecuniary interest in this item, as the Mayor's mother owns a property on Victoria Road. The Mayor left the meeting during this item, did not participate in debate, and did not vote on the matter.

Note: The Mayor vacated the Chair at 7:50pm. Councillor Carmichael, as Deputy Mayor assumed the Chair.

Note: The Council added new Part E ahead of the vote.

(Councillor Woodgate/Councillor Regan)

471/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:
  
  1. Approves in principle the proposed traffic calming measures, including a pedestrian refuge with kerb extensions in Cranbrook Road at Victoria Road, Bellevue Hill as shown in Attachment 1.

 

  1. Notes that consent for Development Application No. 390/2019/1 includes a condition for the applicant to develop, fund and implement Local Area Traffic Management (LATM) regarding safety and efficiency, to the satisfaction of Council's Engineering Services Department.

  2. Resolves that no action be taken before the expiry date of the development consent on 12 April 2028 or when physical commencement has occurred, whichever is sooner.

  3. Notes that a detailed design for the proposed traffic calming measures, together with community consultation feedback will be presented to a future Local Transport Forum meeting for review and consideration.

  4. Requests that staff investigate:
  1. During the Aston Gardens parking restrictions trial investigate and report on implementing similar restrictions on the following streets in part or full so as to encourage staff and students of Scots College to utilise alternative transport options or for the College to provide off street parking: Cranbrook Lane, Cranbrook Road, Carrington Avenue, Ginahgulla Road, Victoria Road, Kambala Road, Sheldon Place, Rupertswood Avenue and  Drumalbyn Road.
  2. Means by which parking permits may be restricted to the residents of rateable properties, or those that elect to pay rates on or in proximity of these streets.
  3. Notes that any parking restrictions will require community consultation with residents prior to implementation.
  4. Requests the General Manager write to the Headmaster of the Scot’s College, Dr Ian Lambert to advise him of this motion and the investigation of parking restrictions in the vicinity of the school and to ask what strategies or actions the school is taking to reduce the parking burden on Local roads.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Ardouin, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Regan, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Zeltzer
None

Note: 
The Council amended Part G (ii) and Part H ahead of the vote.

(Councillor Witt/Councillor Parmegiani)

473/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes that DPHI has approved SSD-86122958 (9-storey, 54 units, 110 basement car spaces) for 2-16 Spencer Street, Rose Bay, notwithstanding Council Staff's 2 April 2026 Response to Submissions (RTS)advice that Council's objections of 1 December 2025 remain unresolved, including:
  1. the fact that the applicant's Transport Impact Assessment failed to address cumulative traffic impacts from the proposed multiple Low and Mid-Rise (LMR) developments in Rose Bay;
  2. the approved 110 car spaces exceed Council's 50-space development control limit for accessible areas, relying instead on Housing SEPP minimum parking rates for affordable housing and the applicant's likely understated traffic projections during peak hours;
  3. The DPHI Assessment Report’s lack of engagement with Council's household-by-household affordability modelling, which found that none of the 24 household types assessed can afford the proposed affordable apartments (DPHI Assessment Report, pp 42–
  1. Notes that Council's RTS advice found that the applicant's hydrogeological and geotechnical memo failed to adequately address cumulative groundwater/settlement and floodwater impacts arising from proposed Low and Mid-Rise (LMR) developments across Rose Bay; to date numbering 20 LMR SSDAs/DAs and heavily clustered around the Wilberforce Avenue/Dover Road/Carlisle Street corridor and in Spencer Street itself ‐1 SSDA and 2 DAs. (See attachment).

  2. Notes that the DPHI commissioned PSM to assess the hydrogeological and geotechnical risks of the 11-metre, three-level basement excavation proposed for the 2-16 Spencer Street SSDA, and in doing so it:
  1. established its own assessment criteria rather than applying Council's 2024 DCP, which was recently updated to incorporate the recommendations of the July 2024 GHD Rose Bay - Hydrogeological and Geotechnical Impacts Report (GHD Rose Bay Report); 
  2. used its desktop analysis of the 2-16 Spencer Street SSDA (located in "Zone C" of the GHD Rose Bay settlement map) and the GHD Rose Bay Report to conclude that Council's 0.3m drawdown control at the site’s boundaries is a "conservative limit" for the hydrogeological vulnerable areas of the Rose Bay settlement area (Zones A and B), and that localised site-specific studies could be used to increase the limit to 1.0m (p 14); and
  3. concluded that vibration limits could be raised to 5–10mm/s peak velocity, noting that Council's current adopted limits are more consistent with protecting human comfort levels than preventing damage to structures (p 16). 

 

  1. Notes that the PSM Review:
  1. provides no cumulative groundwater modelling, despite GHD's own finding that such modelling is required where extensive deep basements block significant portions of the flow path;
  2. identifies no mechanism to monitor or enforce recommended "in perpetuity" tanking conditions across multiple, separately-owned developments; and
  3. claims that cumulative excavation impacts in Rose Bay are unlikely and can be effectively managed by conditions by relying on GHD’s assessment that risks of groundwater flow are “much lower” in Rose Bay than in Double Bay, without reference to recent excavation-related damages (p 15).
  1. Notes that the PSM Review dismisses residents’ concerns about excavation damage without:
  1. engaging with the General Manager's 17 September 2025 correspondence to the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces, which set out numerous resident representations of property damage; and
  2. referencing and/or investigating recent documented evidence of excavation-related harm, including multiple Stop Work Orders at 6-8 Richmond Road because of structural damage to the neighbouring inter-war flat buildings, the partial collapse of a house at 64 Wilberforce Avenue, and the recent partial collapse of the heritage-listed "Hillcrest", which was attributed to “flawed geotechnical advice” by the builder.
  1. Notes that PSM Review Table 3 rates the applicant's (Rapid Geo) documentation "INSUFFICIENT" on 10 of 13 assessment criteria, including groundwater level establishment, ground movement and damming effects.

  2. Requests that the General Manager write to the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces to:
  1. formally object to the approval of SSD-86122958;
  2. question the adequacy of relying on a so-called “independent peer reviewed” report, informed only by a desktop review of the GHD Rose Bay Report and a desktop assessment of the applicant’s geotechnical and hydrogeological reports for the 2-16 Spencer Street SSDA, to conclude that cumulative groundwater and settlement impacts from multiple basement excavations across the precinct are acceptable;
  3. seek an explanation explain why DPHI is commissioning third parties to contradict Council's controls and expert advice; and
  4. request that no further LMR SSDAs be approved until Council's precinct-wide cumulative hydrogeological and flood risk studies are complete. 

  1. Requests that the General Manager seek legal advice from Council's General Counsel on Council's options for challenging the approval, including the availability and merits of Class 4 judicial review proceedings.

  2. Requests that the General Manager's correspondence seek clarification on what indemnity or insurance mechanism is available to surrounding owners — including strata-titled apartment buildings — in the event of excavation or dewatering-related structural damage.

  3. Requests that a copy of this resolution and the above requested General Manager correspondence be forwarded to the Member for Vaucluse and the Member for Wentworth.

The Motion was put and Carried.

 

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

Councillor Andruska, Councillor Carmichael, Councillor Dixson, Councillor Jarvis, Councillor Mitchell, Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Regan, Councillor Silcocks, Councillor Torsten, Councillor Witt, Councillor Woodgate, Councillor Zeltzer
Councillor Ardouin

Councillor Torsten Asking:

The old brick amenities block and change rooms situated in Lough Park, Double Bay has served the local sporting clubs well for many years but it now appears that it is in need of an upgrade to meet the significant influx of new residents to the Woollahra and Double Bay area under the State Government LMRs.

Also, Residents have voiced their concerns that the current change rooms lack sufficient toilet facilities during popular sporting events - especially during the summer period. I have been told by Residents that the shower facilities are rarely ever used since players tend to live locally and prefer to shower at home. This would maximise the utility of the existing amenities block without the need for extensive renovations nor the enlargement of the building's footprint.
 
Please advise if Council has any plans to upgrade these facilities and if there are funds available to do so, including the conversion of the shower cubicles in the male and female change rooms into extra toilets when the adjacent grass netball courts are upgraded. 

Manager Open Spaces & Trees in response:

Response provided as late correspondence.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, modify development consent to DA 215/2011/1 for Staged Development consisting of the following:

  • Demolition of the existing dwelling house and ancillary structures at 88 Newcastle Street;
  • Demolition of the existing dwelling house and ancillary structures at 94 Newcastle Street;
  • Demolition of the former St Paul’s Anglican Church and former Parish Hall (Possums Pre-School) at 96 Newcastle Street; removal of existing landscaping and trees;
  • Retention of the existing Greek Orthodox Church at 90-92 Newcastle Street;
  • Construction of a new 34 place Childcare Centre;
  • Construction of a new 4 storey residential flat building (RFB) comprising of 19 residential units with basement car parking, landscaping and siteworks;
  • Consolidation of the existing allotments into one allotment on land at 88 Newcastle Street ROSE BAY, subject to the conditions in Attachment 2 with an additional condition B.16 in relation to Archaeological Features - Unexpected Findings.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions).

 



Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion

Note:Expert Heather Warton declared a non-significant, non-pecuniary interest in this Item, as she is friends with the Applicants Planner/speaker Sarah Roach who was registered to speak. Heather Warton left the meeting during item 4.1, did not participate in debate, and did not vote on the matter.

Note: Jennifer Gamble, Jacqueline Pillemer, Anthony Tregoning, Malcolm Young, Grant Roe and addressed the Panel.

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, modify development consent to DA 36/2025/1 for extensive alterations and additions to the existing dwelling house including new site access and front fence, basement parking, pool, cabana, landscaping and associated works on land at 11 Pine Hill Avenue DOUBLE BAY, subject to the conditions in Attachment 2.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has considered the submissions and late correspondence and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel noted in particular, issues raised in written and oral submissions about construction impacts, especially relating to excavation and traffic. The Panel was satisfied that the given the nature and extent of the proposed construction works relative to those of the approved development, the current consent conditions are sufficient to address the concerns raised.

 

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the modified development is substantially the same as the original development and the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions).

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion


David RyanNil
Sandra Robinson
Luise Elsing



3/0

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council as the consent authority under section 4.16 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, grant deferred commencement development consent to DA487/2025/1 for demolition of the existing dwelling house and construction of a six-storey residential flat building containing six apartments above basement parking, with a communal roof terrace, landscaping and associated site works at 1 Richmond Road, Rose Bay, subject to the deferred commencement and conditions contained in Attachment 2.

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the written and oral submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions).

Note:Expert Sandra Robinson declared a non-significant, non-pecuniary interest in this item, as she acts as a planning consultant for Sydney Grammar School (adjoining the development site) and prepared a submission (non-objection/comment) to original DA 477/2019. Sandra Robinson left the meeting during item 4.3, did not participate in debate, and did not vote on the matter.

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, on behalf of the Sydney Eastern City Planning Panel, as the consent authority, refuse to modify development consent to DA 477/2019/1 approved for first stage of the development of White City including multi-purpose sporting facilities and registered club facilities and site remediation on land at 30 Alma Street PADDINGTON, for the reasons in Attachment 2.

 

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence (including the applicants request for deferral), and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The majority of the Panel is satisfied that the application be refused for the reasons set out in Attachment (Adopted Reasons for Refusal).

In the minority, the Chair, David Ryan, considered that refusal of the application primarily on heritage impact grounds, was not warranted. The Chair, David Ryan considers that in the context of the full extent of the historically important arches, the impact of a relatively lightweight and largely transparent structure, though which the one impacted arch would remain visible, was not an unacceptable impact, and that conditions involving removing or reducing the proposed corner post (without affecting the structural integrity of the wall), could further mitigate any such perceived impact.

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion


Heather Warton
David Ryan
Luise Elsing



2/1

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Councillor Torsten:

  • Thanks to Infrastructure & Sustainability Division - Cooper Park North Playground

Councillor Torsten thanked Director Tom O'Hanlon's team for installing the new fence around the Cooper Park North Playground, noting that the upgrade has been very well-received by the community.


Councillor Jarvis:

  • Committee for Sydney's Breathable Density
  • Vale - Hylda Anne Rolfe - Former Mayor and Alderman of Woollahra
Councillor Jarvis advised that on 13 July 2026, she attended the Committee for Sydney's Breathable Density. Councillor Jarvis reported on Sydney's Breathable Density Plan which, amongst other matters suggests that disused Government infrastructure may be allocated to public space.

Councillor Jarvis further advised that on 23 August 2026, she along with Councillor Witt attended the celebration of the life of former Woollahra Mayor,  Hylda Rolfe. Councillor Jarvis recounted a number of personal stories shared by those in attendance, and spoke of the valuable advice she had received from the former Mayor over time. Councillor Jarvis expressed her condolences to the family.


Councillor Woodgate:

  • Tree Champion Award

Councillor Woodgate advised that on 12 August 2026 he represented the Mayor by presenting the Tree Champion Award at Cranbrook Junior School, which recognised the efforts for planting native trees. Councillor Woodgate congratulated the school and extended his thanks to Council's Urban Forest Strategy team for starting this initiative.


Mayor, Councillor Dixson:

  • Tree Champion Award
  • Youth Photographic Award & Short Film Prize

The Mayor, Councillor Dixson congratulated staff on initiating the Tree Champion Award, which included Bellevue Hill Public School. The Mayor spoke of her visit to the school and commented on how the project had energised so many children.

The Mayor reminded Councillors about the Youth Photographic Award & Short Film Prize, soon to be held at Woollahra Gallery. The Mayor stated that every year, the gallery filled with young people expressing their creativity, and encouraged everyone to visit the gallery and show support to the participants.

THAT Council: 

  1. Receive and note The Sydney Plan released on 13 August 2026.

  2. Note that The Sydney Plan represents a significant shift in metropolitan planning that includes the following key points:
  1. Sydney must accommodate substantially more people;
  2. Existing developed eastern suburbs must accept a greater share of housing growth;
  3. Councils must demonstrate feasible housing supply rather than simply protecting existing character;
  4. Infrastructure and environmental outcomes must be delivered alongside growth; and
  5. The State is prepared to intervene where Councils do not align with these objectives.

Note: 
This item was considered ahead of item 13.1.7 - Evidence-based Planning for Growth - Council Staff Alternate Approach to the State-led Rezoning of parts of Edgecliff & Woollahra.

(Councillor Woodgate/Councillor Robertson)

565/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Notes the Woollahra Council Urban Forest Strategy.

  2. Notes our target to achieve 30% canopy by 2050 requires approximately 5,000 trees to be planted on private land.

  3. Notes the importance of planting established trees to achieve shade canopy at a faster rate, a strategy that Council has adopted with its street tree plantings.

  4. Notes that schools in Woollahra are typically non-publicly accessible land, and that they are located on large sites.

  5. Requests the General Manager include in the next biannual Urban Forest Strategy progress report consideration of how Woollahra Council can further incentivise schools to plant more canopy trees. Specifically investigating a one-for-one tree program, whereby Council supplies and installs one tree on school grounds for each tree independently funded and planted by schools through internal budgets or fundraising activities. The investigation shall include: 
  1. Consideration of funding limits.
  2. Eligibility criteria and consideration of how to prioritise schools with the lowest canopy cover, high heat exposure and planting capacity. 
  3. Scope and installation considerations.
  4. Ongoing maintenance responsibilities. 
  5. A suitable funding source for this initiative.

The Motion was put and Carried.

In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

Councillor Parmegiani, Councillor Witt, and Councillor Jarvis asking:

Woollahra Council's Delivery Program 2025-2026 to 2029-2029 and Operational Plan Progress Report was presented to the Strategic and Corporate Committee meeting on 10 August 2026. 

The Progress Report notes on 3.2.1.2, "In the last 6 months the Outer Sydney Harbour Catchment Management Program has progressed to Stage 3 of 5 stages. Technical reports have been completed and staff workshops held addressing coastal hazards, water quality, recreation and access".

It would be helpful for Woollahra Councillors to understand coastal hazards in the Woollahra municipality, including the risks of flooding, inundation and coastal erosion. Such information is crucial to Councillors' decision-making on zoning and other issues.

 

When will the technical reports on coastal hazards, water quality, recreation and access be released to Woollahra Councillors?

Director - Infrastructure and Sustainability in response:

Staff would have preferred to present these reports to a Councillor briefing but as this is no longer permitted, it is proposed to present the technical reports as a Confidential report to a Strategic and Corporate Committee in October.

The Mayor, Councillor Dixson, declared a non-significant, non-pecuniary interest in this item, as her son is on the waitlist for Woollahra Preschool, and that she knows parents who have children currently at the preschool or who are presently on the waitlist. The Mayor remained in the meeting, participated in debate and voted on the matter.

Note:

(Councillor Torsten/Councillor Woodgate)

558/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Note the staff assessment of the NSW Government’s Expanding Quality Access Program (EQAP) proposal and the associated planning, financial, operational and workforce risks identified in this report.

  2. Note the outcomes of the Woollahra Preschool Expansion Options Survey undertaken between 22 June and 8 July 2026, including community support for increased preschool access and the differing views regarding expansion at the existing Hugh Latimer Centre site.

  3. Determine not to proceed with the current EQAP-funded proposal to expand Woollahra Preschool at the existing Hugh Latimer Centre site.

  4. Request the General Manager table a further report on alternate options to increase preschool access across the Woollahra LGA to a Strategic & Corporate Committee meeting in April 2027.

  5. Request the General Manager to write to the Premier and Minister for Education to explain that:
  1. the guidelines for the EQAP place an unfair and risky financial burden on councils, which are required to expend substantial funds upfront with no certainty of grant outcome;
  2. Council cannot meet the current demand for pre-school spaces at the current location.

The Motion was put and Carried.

 

Note:
In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

For the MotionAgainst the Motion

559/2026 Resolved:

  1. Notes the progress report on the Swimmable Harbour proposal at Yarranabbe Park, including the outcomes of discussions with Professor Bruce Thom and additional water quality investigations undertaken since Council's resolution of 24 February 2025.

  2. Endorse the undertaking of further investigations, including a Human Health Risk Assessment and additional water quality monitoring, noting that:
  1. the investigations are required to determine whether the site is suitable for swimming;
  2. no decision has been made regarding construction of a swimming enclosure; and
  3. any future consideration of project delivery would be subject to separate Council endorsement and the identification of substantial external funding assistance.
  1. Notes the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure's recently published ‘Sydney Plan’ and its ‘Open Space Toolkit and Action Plan’ focusing on improving access to public open spaces including ‘creating more places to swim and be by the water.’

  2. Notes that a further report will be presented to Council in February 2027, following completion of the Human Health Risk Assessment outlining the findings, project implications and recommended next steps.

The Motion was put and Carried.

Councillor Jarvis asking:

The opening lines of Minister Scully's media release dated August 25 2026 state: "The Minns Labor Government will deliver Sydney’s first new heavy rail station in more than a decade – enabling up to 10,000 new homes by rezoning land around Woollahra and Edgecliff stations, right next to the CBD, to tackle the housing crisis and rebalance growth across the city." https://paulscullymp.com.au/news/media-releases/next-stop-woollahra-train-station-delivering-up-to-ten-thousand-new-homes-in-the-heart-of-sydney/. 


  • What, if any, assurance has the NSW Government, Premier, Minister or its agencies given to assure the Council and/or public that any State-led zoning for Edgecliff and Woollahra Station is subject to delivery of Woollahra Station, the first new heavy rail station in more than a decade?

The staff report presented to the August 17th meeting of Woollahra Council's Strategic and Corporate Committee states : "According to information which is publicly available, preliminary site investigations have been completed, and the project is currently in the procurement phase for design and construction. Construction is currently anticipated to commence in 2027, with completion targeted for 2029, subject to approvals and funding." 

  • What more detailed information is available about that?

  • Are there any links relevant to the seeking of procurement eg tenders or RFQ? 

  • Has any additional advice been provided that staff is aware of?

  • Has any advice been given concerning approvals or funding mentioned in the report? 

The staff report also states "Until detailed design information is available it remains difficult to fully assess the transport, public domain social infrastructure and place-based implications." 

  • Is it the intention that the reports of our consultants presented to the meeting be updated upon the receiving detailed design information? 

Director - Planning & Place in response:

Response to be provided as late correspondence.

Councillor Jarvis asking:

The STC traffic report dated July 2026 presented to the August 17th meeting of Woollahra Council's Strategic and Corporate Committee concerns a study area apparently limited to 400m from the Edgecliff Station and 800m from the proposed Woollahra Station but states in relation to existing transport capacity  'less than 7% capacity is available on New South Head Road in the peak traffic direction'. And that 'planned and proposed developments across the wider region are expected to place additional demand in the transport network'.

  • What analysis has been done on the demand along New South Head road from traffic extending beyond the study area to the east up to and including  Watson Bay? Please provide.

  • In particular what is the likely impact of additional traffic generated to and from the State led Low-Mid Rise Housing zone MR in Rose Bay along  New South head Road and Old South Head Road. 

  • In particular what information exists about the impact of additional traffic generation to and from the Bondi Junction Master Plan.

  • Has there been any analysis of the traffic impact on Old South Head Road?  
  • What measures are proposed or recommended to improve capacity along New South Head Road and Old South Head Road? 

In relation to rail services the STC traffic report says that there is existing capacity on the existing rail services, using the example that for city bound services departing from Kings Cross less than 50% of seats are occupied in the morning peak hour. 

  • Is there any information about seats occupied departing Bondi Junction and Edgecliff, mindful that passengers disembark and embark at Kings Cross.  

  • From where is the Kings Cross example sourced? 

  • Maybe from the 2016 travel to work data (footnote 1 on that page doesnt correlate to a number 1 above)? 

  • Is there any current information available?

  • What data can be or has been obtained from TfNSW? 

Please provide a copy of the rapid transport appraisal completed by STC in March 2026 that assessed ' the capacity to support state-led uplift beyond the anticipated growth from state led uplift' i.e. State Significant developments applications, low and mid-rise housing predictions, the Double Bay planning proposal and Bondi Junction Master plan'.

Response to be provided as late correspondence.
