650/2026 Resolved:

THAT Council:

  1. Endorse the submission at Attachment 1 of the report to the Council meeting of 30 September 2026, subject to the amendments identified by the Council at that meeting.

 


  1. Recommend to the NSW Government that the exhibited Edgecliff-Woollahra State-led Rezoning Proposal must not proceed, as it fails to demonstrate that the proposed scale and distribution of uplift is independently evidence-based, appropriately designed, feasible, infrastructure-led or capable of delivering the housing, infrastructure and public benefits relied upon to justify the unprecedented extent of change proposed. This is based upon Councils comprehensive submission that has been informed by extensive technical evidence, including:
  1. Edgecliff and Woollahra - Alternative Approach to the State Led Rezoning;
  2. Edgecliff and Woollahra – Traffic and Transport Review (SCT);
  3. Independent review of the exhibited Urban Design Report – Six Degrees Urban;
  4. Independent review of the exhibited Economic Impact Assessment – Savills;
  5. Edgecliff and Woollahra - Social Infrastructure Needs Study (Cred);
  6. Urban Design assessment - Council staff;
  7. Overshadowing and solar access impact assessment - Council staff;
  8. Heritage assessment – Council staff;
  9. Social and community infrastructure – Council staff;
  10. Public open space – Council staff;
  11. Geotechnical assessment – Council staff;
  12. Flooding and stormwater – Council staff;
  13. Trees and urban greening – Council staff; 
  14. Traffic, transport and parking - Council staff;
  15. Biodiversity and climate resilience - Council staff;
  16. Contamination - Council staff;
  17. Lack of cumulative impact assessment - Council staff;
  18. Loss of housing diversity and affordable housing - Council staff;
  19. Affordable housing provision – Council staff; and
  20. Health and emergency services submissions made by Professors, Doctors and Medical Specialists.
  1. Reaffirm Council’s position that any future planning framework for the Woollahra LGA should review the status of the Edgecliff Centre, focused on the opportunity for uplift and housing as a priority; and build on Council's adopted strategic planning work, including the Edgecliff Centre Planning and Urban Design Strategy (endorsed by Woollahra Council in April 2024) and Housing Strategy to ensure that growth is evidence-based, appropriately located, infrastructure-supported and responsive to local character and community needs.

  2. Recommend to the NSW Government that it should use the methodology in Council’s Alternative Approach and the underlying planning and urban design principles as the basis for the first stage of any future rezoning, subject to further investigation, refinement and extensive public consultation. The underlying planning and urban design principles are:
  1. Elevating the harbour setting and its natural, cultural and ecological systems;
  2. Recognising and responding to established patterns of development, subdivision and urban morphology;
  3. Delivering street-based design outcomes that reinforce the public domain and established street structure;
  4. Responding to block alignments and preserving framed views to the sky;
  5. Responding sympathetically to heritage fabric, heritage settings and established character; and
  6. Maintaining breathing space between buildings and allowing towers to be viewed in the round.
  1. Recommend to the NSW Government that any future rezoning must be implemented through a staged statutory framework rather than a single, broad-based uplift across the entire Precinct.

 


  1. Require the NSW Government to prepare a deferred rezoning mechanism, or an equivalent enforceable statutory mechanism, to prevent additional development capacity from becoming available until all infrastructure and public-benefit obligations associated with that capacity are funded, programmed and legally committed.

  2. Require the NSW Government to confirm the feasibility, full funding, delivery responsibilities and binding delivery program for Woollahra Station and all supporting transport, utility, open-space, social and community infrastructure before any rezoning is finalised.

  3. Require the NSW Government to identify, secure, fund and program all land required for public open space, community facilities, roads, pedestrian connections, cycling connections and other public infrastructure, to ensure that public benefits are not dependent upon uncertain future site amalgamations, private redevelopments or voluntary negotiations with landowners.

  4. Require the NSW Government to prepare and publicly exhibit a comprehensive Infrastructure Funding and Delivery Strategy before any rezoning proceeds. The Strategy must:
  1. Identify all infrastructure and public benefits required to support the proposed growth;
  2. Provide robust and independently verified costings;
  3. Identify secured funding sources and every remaining funding shortfall;
  4. Assign binding delivery responsibilities to identified agencies;
  5. Establish clear delivery timeframes and sequencing;
  6. Identify all land acquisition requirements and associated funding;
  7. Include realistic cashflow and revenue forecasts based on credible housing-delivery assumptions;
  8. Establish transparent governance, monitoring, reporting and accountability arrangements; and
  9. Include enforceable contingency measures if development, revenue or infrastructure delivery does not occur as forecast.
  1. Require the NSW Government to include clear, measurable and legally enforceable infrastructure delivery triggers linked to specified levels of dwelling and population growth before any rezoning progresses.

  2. Require the NSW Government to prepare and publicly exhibit a detailed reconciliation for the proposed infrastructure including the:
  1. Infrastructure identified in the exhibited proposal;
  2. Infrastructure identified through Council’s evidence base;
  3. Infrastructure accepted as necessary by responsible government and delivery agencies;
  4. Infrastructure that is funded and programmed; and
  5. Infrastructure that can realistically be delivered.

 


  1. Require the NSW Government to protect existing housing diversity and secure substantially stronger affordable-housing outcomes by: 
  1. Comprehensively quantify the loss of existing smaller, diverse and relatively affordable housing;
  2. Introduce binding statutory controls to prevent a net loss of dwellings through redevelopment;
  3. Substantially increase the proposed affordable-housing contribution requirements;
  4. Requiring affordable housing generated by the rezoning to be retained as affordable housing in perpetuity;
  5. Requiring all monetary and in-kind affordable-housing contributions arising from the rezoning to be spent or delivered within the Woollahra LGA;
  6. Identifying and reserving dedicated key sites for affordable housing in accessible locations within the Precinct, particularly around Edgecliff Station and the proposed Woollahra Station;
  7. Demonstrating that the proposal will produce a genuine net increase in housing diversity and affordability; and
  8. Preventing increases in height and floor-space ratio from being used principally to deliver fewer, larger and substantially more expensive apartments.
  1. Require the NSW Government to undertake and publicly exhibit a comprehensive cumulative impact assessment before any rezoning is finalised. The assessment must examine the combined effects of the Rezoning Proposal with:
  1. Existing development capacity;
  2. The increased dwelling and population growth resulting from the LMR and the Infill Affordable Housing provisions
  3. State Significant Development and Housing Delivery Authority pathways;
  4. Planned and government driven growth including in Edgecliff, Double Bay, Rose Bay and Bondi Junction;
  5. Other current and foreseeable State planning reforms;
  6. Approved and proposed major developments; and
  7. Existing infrastructure, transport, environmental, social and community-service constraints across the Woollahra LGA.
  1. Recommends the Rezoning Proposal not proceed unless it is amended to prioritise retention of existing urban forest, vegetation and habitat connectivity, avoid encroachment into Trumper Park, strengthen threatened species protection, reduce built form impacts near key habitat areas, and include enforceable biodiversity controls.

  2. Require the NSW Government to undertake genuine and transparent public consultation, including a substantially longer, properly resourced and genuinely consultative public exhibition process. This must also demonstrate how the recommendations of its own consultants, the State Design Review Panel and all submissions have informed the final rezoning framework. Where recommendations have not been adopted, modified or have been departed from, the NSW Government must provide a clear and transparent explanation of the reasons for doing so.

  3. Require the NSW Government to obtain and publish formal advice and binding delivery commitments from all relevant infrastructure and service agencies named here that confirms these agencies ability to provide the relevant infrastructure required to service the proposed increased population as a result of the rezoning proposal and prior to any rezoning being finalised: Transport for NSW, Sydney Water, Ausgrid, NSW Health, the Department of Education, NSW Ambulance, Fire and Rescue NSW, the NSW Police Force, the NSW State Emergency Service, Heritage NSW and the Heritage Council of NSW.

  4. Require the NSW Government to undertake and fully fund the preparation, public exhibition and finalisation of all necessary amendments to the Woollahra Section 7.12 Development Contributions Plan before any rezoning commences.

  5. Require the NSW Government to ensure that any Rezoning Proposal is referred to the Independent Planning Commission for review and advice before determination.

  6. In follow up to the meeting held on 15 September 2026 with the Minister for Planning & Public Spaces, request that the Mayor, General Manager and Director Planning and Place request a meeting with the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces as soon as practicable following the public exhibition period of the rezoning proposal, to present Council's concerns, recommendations and supporting technical evidence, and to advocate for substantive amendments to the Edgecliff-Woollahra State-led Rezoning Proposal, the proposed Woollahra Station project and associated infrastructure commitments prior to any final determination, as contained within this Council submission.

  7. Request that the General Manager request that senior representatives of the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure meet with key Council staff following the close of public exhibition of the rezoning proposal, for the purpose of undertaking a detailed review of Council's submission, supporting technical evidence and Alternative Approach, and to discuss potential amendments to the rezoning proposal, Woollahra Station project and associated infrastructure framework prior to any final determination.

  8. Continue to advocate for amendments to the Edgecliff-Woollahra State-led Rezoning Proposal and the proposed Woollahra Station following the closure of public exhibition, including through direct engagement with the NSW Government, Transport for NSW, the City of Sydney, Waverley Council and other relevant agencies, to influencing the final planning framework, infrastructure commitments and station design, if the rezoning proposal is to move forward. This advocacy should seek a genuine subregional planning response that recognises the cumulative impacts of growth across the Eastern Suburbs and inner-east, including Edgecliff, Woollahra, Double Bay, Bondi Junction and surrounding centres, and ensures that future planning decisions are informed by an integrated assessment of housing, infrastructure, transport and community-service capacity rather than consideration of individual precincts in isolation.

  9. Request that this submission, supporting technical evidence, Council report and adopted recommendations be provided to Kellie Sloane MP, Member for Vaucluse; Alex Greenwich MP, Member for Sydney; Allegra Spender MP, Federal Member for Wentworth, Ryan Park Minister for  Health, Regional Health and Mental Health and Sarah Mitchell, Shadow Minister for Health, Regional Health and Mental Health, Prue Car Minister for Education and Early Learning, Make Speakman, Shadow Minister for Minister for Education and Early Learning, Rose Jackson Minister for Homelessness, Natasha Maclaren-Jones, Shadow Minister for Homelessness and Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault, Jodie Harrison Minister of Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault; other Ministers, the Mayor and Chief Executive Officer of Waverley Council; and the Lord Mayor and Chief Executive Officer of the City of Sydney, and that those parties be invited to support Council's advocacy for a more balanced, evidence-based and coordinated subregional planning outcome for the eastern suburbs.

  10. Respectfully request the NSW Government work with Councils to agree realistic housing targets in line with The Sydney Plan and then permit local Councils to use their detailed and intimate knowledge of their local areas to develop strategic plans to meet those targets.

  11. Note the extensive submissions made to Council and the petition tabled.

  12. Thank staff and independent consultants for their considerable efforts in reviewing the exhibition material, preparing Council's Alternative Approach and supporting technical evidence, and assisting in the preparation of Council's submission within the short consultation timeframe.

  13. Recognises the extensive late correspondence that was provided to the Council meeting of 30 September 2026, the petition tabled with 70 signatures, and thank all the community members who attended one of the Council-led Community Activation sessions.

The Motion was put and Carried.

In accordance with Council's Code of Meeting Practice a Division of votes is recorded on this matter.

  10. Public open space – Council staff;
  11. Geotechnical assessment – Council staff;
  12. Flooding and stormwater – Council staff;
  13. Trees and urban greening – Council staff; 
  14. Traffic, transport and parking - Council staff;
  15. Biodiversity and climate resilience - Council staff;
  16. Contamination - Council staff;
  17. Lack of cumulative impact assessment - Council staff;
  18. Loss of housing diversity and affordable housing - Council staff;
  19. Affordable housing provision – Council staff; and
  20. Health and emergency services submissions made by Professors, Doctors and Medical Specialists.
  1. Reaffirm Council’s position that any future planning framework for the Woollahra LGA should review the status of the Edgecliff Centre, focused on the opportunity for uplift and housing as a priority; and build on Council's adopted strategic planning work, including the Edgecliff Centre Planning and Urban Design Strategy (endorsed by Woollahra Council in April 2024) and Housing Strategy to ensure that growth is evidence-based, appropriately located, infrastructure-supported and responsive to local character and community needs.

  2. Recommend to the NSW Government that it should use the methodology in Council’s Alternative Approach and the underlying planning and urban design principles as the basis for the first stage of any future rezoning, subject to further investigation, refinement and extensive public consultation. The underlying planning and urban design principles are:
  1. Elevating the harbour setting and its natural, cultural and ecological systems;
  2. Recognising and responding to established patterns of development, subdivision and urban morphology;
  3. Delivering street-based design outcomes that reinforce the public domain and established street structure;
  4. Responding to block alignments and preserving framed views to the sky;
  5. Responding sympathetically to heritage fabric, heritage settings and established character; and
  6. Maintaining breathing space between buildings and allowing towers to be viewed in the round.
  1. Recommend to the NSW Government that any future rezoning must be implemented through a staged statutory framework rather than a single, broad-based uplift across the entire Precinct.

  2. Require the NSW Government to prepare a deferred rezoning mechanism, or an equivalent enforceable statutory mechanism, to prevent additional development capacity from becoming available until all infrastructure and public-benefit obligations associated with that capacity are funded, programmed and legally committed.

  3. Require the NSW Government to confirm the feasibility, full funding, delivery responsibilities and binding delivery program for Woollahra Station and all supporting transport, utility, open-space, social and community infrastructure before any rezoning is finalised.

  4. Require the NSW Government to identify, secure, fund and program all land required for public open space, community facilities, roads, pedestrian connections, cycling connections and other public infrastructure, to ensure that public benefits are not dependent upon uncertain future site amalgamations, private redevelopments or voluntary negotiations with landowners.

  5. Require the NSW Government to prepare and publicly exhibit a comprehensive Infrastructure Funding and Delivery Strategy before any rezoning proceeds. The Strategy must:
  1. Identify all infrastructure and public benefits required to support the proposed growth;
  2. Provide robust and independently verified costings;
  3. Identify secured funding sources and every remaining funding shortfall;
  4. Assign binding delivery responsibilities to identified agencies;
  5. Establish clear delivery timeframes and sequencing;
  6. Identify all land acquisition requirements and associated funding;
  7. Include realistic cashflow and revenue forecasts based on credible housing-delivery assumptions;
  8. Establish transparent governance, monitoring, reporting and accountability arrangements; and
  9. Include enforceable contingency measures if development, revenue or infrastructure delivery does not occur as forecast.
  1. Require the NSW Government to include clear, measurable and legally enforceable infrastructure delivery triggers linked to specified levels of dwelling and population growth before any rezoning progresses.

  2. Require the NSW Government to prepare and publicly exhibit a detailed reconciliation for the proposed infrastructure including the:
  1. Infrastructure identified in the exhibited proposal;
  2. Infrastructure identified through Council’s evidence base;
  3. Infrastructure accepted as necessary by responsible government and delivery agencies;
  4. Infrastructure that is funded and programmed; and
  5. Infrastructure that can realistically be delivered.
  1. Require the NSW Government to protect existing housing diversity and secure substantially stronger affordable-housing outcomes by: 
  1. Comprehensively quantify the loss of existing smaller, diverse and relatively affordable housing;
  2. Introduce binding statutory controls to prevent a net loss of dwellings through redevelopment;
  3. Substantially increase the proposed affordable-housing contribution requirements;
  4. Requiring affordable housing generated by the rezoning to be retained as affordable housing in perpetuity;
  5. Requiring all monetary and in-kind affordable-housing contributions arising from the rezoning to be spent or delivered within the Woollahra LGA;
  6. Identifying and reserving dedicated key sites for affordable housing in accessible locations within the Precinct, particularly around Edgecliff Station and the proposed Woollahra Station;
  7. Demonstrating that the proposal will produce a genuine net increase in housing diversity and affordability; and
  8. Preventing increases in height and floor-space ratio from being used principally to deliver fewer, larger and substantially more expensive apartments.
  1. Require the NSW Government to undertake and publicly exhibit a comprehensive cumulative impact assessment before any rezoning is finalised. The assessment must examine the combined effects of the Rezoning Proposal with:
  1. Existing development capacity;
  2. The increased dwelling and population growth resulting from the LMR and the Infill Affordable Housing provisions
  3. State Significant Development and Housing Delivery Authority pathways;
  4. Planned and government driven growth including in Edgecliff, Double Bay, Rose Bay and Bondi Junction;
  5. Other current and foreseeable State planning reforms;
  6. Approved and proposed major developments; and
  7. Existing infrastructure, transport, environmental, social and community-service constraints across the Woollahra LGA.
  1. Recommends the Rezoning Proposal not proceed unless it is amended to prioritise retention of existing urban forest, vegetation and habitat connectivity, avoid encroachment into Trumper Park, strengthen threatened species protection, reduce built form impacts near key habitat areas, and include enforceable biodiversity controls.

  2. Require the NSW Government to undertake genuine and transparent public consultation, including a substantially longer, properly resourced and genuinely consultative public exhibition process. This must also demonstrate how the recommendations of its own consultants, the State Design Review Panel and all submissions have informed the final rezoning framework. Where recommendations have not been adopted, modified or have been departed from, the NSW Government must provide a clear and transparent explanation of the reasons for doing so.

  3. Require the NSW Government to obtain and publish formal advice and binding delivery commitments from all relevant infrastructure and service agencies named here that confirms these agencies ability to provide the relevant infrastructure required to service the proposed increased population as a result of the rezoning proposal and prior to any rezoning being finalised: Transport for NSW, Sydney Water, Ausgrid, NSW Health, the Department of Education, NSW Ambulance, Fire and Rescue NSW, the NSW Police Force, the NSW State Emergency Service, Heritage NSW and the Heritage Council of NSW.

  4. Require the NSW Government to undertake and fully fund the preparation, public exhibition and finalisation of all necessary amendments to the Woollahra Section 7.12 Development Contributions Plan before any rezoning commences.

  5. Require the NSW Government to ensure that any Rezoning Proposal is referred to the Independent Planning Commission for review and advice before determination.

  6. In follow up to the meeting held on 15 September 2026 with the Minister for Planning & Public Spaces, request that the Mayor, General Manager and Director Planning and Place request a meeting with the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces as soon as practicable following the public exhibition period of the rezoning proposal, to present Council's concerns, recommendations and supporting technical evidence, and to advocate for substantive amendments to the Edgecliff-Woollahra State-led Rezoning Proposal, the proposed Woollahra Station project and associated infrastructure commitments prior to any final determination, as contained within this Council submission.

  7. Request that the General Manager request that senior representatives of the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure meet with key Council staff following the close of public exhibition of the rezoning proposal, for the purpose of undertaking a detailed review of Council's submission, supporting technical evidence and Alternative Approach, and to discuss potential amendments to the rezoning proposal, Woollahra Station project and associated infrastructure framework prior to any final determination.

  8. Continue to advocate for amendments to the Edgecliff-Woollahra State-led Rezoning Proposal and the proposed Woollahra Station following the closure of public exhibition, including through direct engagement with the NSW Government, Transport for NSW, the City of Sydney, Waverley Council and other relevant agencies, to influencing the final planning framework, infrastructure commitments and station design, if the rezoning proposal is to move forward. This advocacy should seek a genuine subregional planning response that recognises the cumulative impacts of growth across the Eastern Suburbs and inner-east, including Edgecliff, Woollahra, Double Bay, Bondi Junction and surrounding centres, and ensures that future planning decisions are informed by an integrated assessment of housing, infrastructure, transport and community-service capacity rather than consideration of individual precincts in isolation.

  9. Request that this submission, supporting technical evidence, Council report and adopted recommendations be provided to Kellie Sloane MP, Member for Vaucluse; Alex Greenwich MP, Member for Sydney; Allegra Spender MP, Federal Member for Wentworth, Ryan Park Minister for  Health, Regional Health and Mental Health and Sarah Mitchell, Shadow Minister for Health, Regional Health and Mental Health, Prue Car Minister for Education and Early Learning, Make Speakman, Shadow Minister for Minister for Education and Early Learning, Rose Jackson Minister for Homelessness, Natasha Maclaren-Jones, Shadow Minister for Homelessness and Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault, Jodie Harrison Minister of Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault; other Ministers, the Mayor and Chief Executive Officer of Waverley Council; and the Lord Mayor and Chief Executive Officer of the City of Sydney, and that those parties be invited to support Council's advocacy for a more balanced, evidence-based and coordinated subregional planning outcome for the eastern suburbs.

  10. Respectfully request the NSW Government work with Councils to agree realistic housing targets in line with The Sydney Plan and then permit local Councils to use their detailed and intimate knowledge of their local areas to develop strategic plans to meet those targets.

  11. Note the extensive submissions made to Council and the petition tabled.

  12. Thank staff and independent consultants for their considerable efforts in reviewing the exhibition material, preparing Council's Alternative Approach and supporting technical evidence, and assisting in the preparation of Council's submission within the short consultation timeframe.

  13. Recognises the extensive late correspondence that was provided to the Council meeting of 30 September 2026, the petition tabled with 70 signatures, and thank all the community members who attended one of the Council-led Community Activation sessions.

The Panel has undertaken a site inspection, reviewed the report including its attachment prepared by Council officers and heritage consultant.  

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel advises Council to proceed with the Planning Proposal (at Attachment 1) to list 33 Edward Street, Woollahra and the portion of the adjacent road reserve as a local heritage item in Schedule 5 and on the associated Heritage Maps of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014.

The Panel further advises Council that, additional detailed consideration may be given to creating an expanded curtilage to the proposed heritage item, over the adjoining property at 35 Edward Street Woollahra, should the matter proceed to Gateway.

Marea Jordan-Watt, Barbara Mortimer, George Karavanas, and Councillor Mark Silcocks addressed the Panel.

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, is satisfied that the matters required to be addressed under Clause 4.6(3) of the Woollahra Local Environmental Plan 2014 have been demonstrated and that consent may be granted to the development application, which contravenes the Floor Space Ratio development standard under Clause 4.4(E) of the Woollahra LEP 2014.

AND

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, grant development consent to Development Application No. 236/2026/1 for Alterations and additions to a CDC new dwelling house approved under CDC2025-0550, including excavation for a new basement level on land at 14 Forest Road DOUBLE BAY, subject to the recommended conditions in Attachment 2.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel Experts Graham Brown and Lee Kosnetter were supportive of the DA in its current format with the inclusion of Council's staff recommended conditions. 

The Chair and Community Representative Luise Elsing were supportive of the DA scheme subject to the inclusion of condition D.1 c) which requires the re-design of the basement level to reduce its level of volume of excavation by 23 cubic metres to ensure compliance with Council's DCP control.

The Chair used her casting vote to approve the development application with the inclusion of condition D.1 c).

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion


Kara KrasonGraham Brown
Luise ElsingLee Kosnetter


2/2

Frank Femia, Tracy Newfield, Ann Privitera, Peter Rose, Evelyn Weltlinger, and Lynette Zines addressed the Panel.

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, refuse development consent to Development Application No. 187/2026/1 for demolition of two existing dwellings and construction of a new eight-storey residential flat building above two levels of basement parking, containing 31 units, as well as landscaping and associated site works on land at 35-37 Wilberforce Avenue ROSE BAY.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

The Panel is satisfied that the application be refused for the reasons set out in Attachment (Adopted Reasons for Refusal).

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion

Matina Psaltis, George Karavanas, and Mazdak Goudarzi addressed the Panel.

Panel's Decision

THAT the Woollahra Local Planning Panel, exercising the functions of Council, as the consent authority, modify development consent to DA335/2022/1 for demolition of the existing dwellings and construction of a residential flat building, basement parking and landscaping works on land at 84-88 Birriga Road BELLEVUE HILL, subject to the conditions of consent outlined in Attachment 2.

Reasons for Decision

The Panel has undertaken site inspection, considered the submissions and late correspondence, and reviewed the assessment report prepared by Council officers that addresses the relevant matters detailed in Section 4.15 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.  

 

The Panel specifically considered the late correspondence by GSA Planning seeking deletion of conditions A.7 and C.23, but did not have sufficient information or justification for the deletion.

For the reasons generally in the assessment report, the Panel is satisfied that the application can be approved subject to the Conditions as set out in Attachment (Adopted Conditions).

Note: In accordance with the Woollahra Local Planning Panel Operational Procedures the votes are recorded on this planning matter.

For the Motion
Against the Motion


Kara KrasonNil
Graham Brown
Lee Kosnetter
Luise Elsing


4/0
